5. Data
5.1 Data Architecture and Data Rights
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Health data can improve continuity while also enabling surveillance or exclusion, so operational access and enforceable individual rights must be designed together. Why this structure: Data are specified as governed records with provenance, rights, and quality controls rather than as an undifferentiated national database. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes data architecture and data rights explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the governed information environment that makes care, payment, rights, oversight, adaptation, and simulation observable without converting the Information Mesh into an uncontrolled central database. |

| System entities | DNHA; NHRA; NEEA; NCCA; THDO; NHSA; OCDTI; NSAA; NHWB; HCCA; AICIO; NHAC; NHASB; CHAO; PRTO; RHA; state/regional/tribal partners; patients; providers. |

| Assumptions | ASM-009 human-accountable AI; ASM-012 federated mesh; D4-DEC-01–04; OI-020/022. |

| Data / parameters | KPP/TPP observations; operational datasets; access/correction logs; provenance; schema and formula versions; data-quality results. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-DATA; SR-RGT; SR-IF-001–015; VR-010/011/014; TPP-10.*, TPP-11.*, TPP-FORM1. |

| Principal risks | Identity errors; unlawful access; missing/late records; inconsistent definitions; surveillance overreach; cyber outage; automated-decision opacity. |

| Simulation implication | Model data availability, latency, identity error, correction, downtime, missingness, disclosure constraints, and definition/version changes as state variables or events. |
The National Health Assurance Information Mesh is a federated public infrastructure: common identity, locator, vocabulary, access-control, audit, conformance, and exchange services coordinate distributed authoritative nodes. The mesh does not confer ownership of every source record on a single agency. Authority answers who may define and certify the datum; custody answers where it is stored and operated; access answers who may use which fields for which purpose; verification answers who may test completeness, correctness, and compliance.
5.1.1 Logical data planes

| Plane | Primary purpose | Typical records | Control |

| Identity and authority | Resolve people/entities and controlling legal/clinical authority | person, provider, facility, product, program, rule/formula versions | Verified keys; effective dating; merge/split correction |

| Operational event | Run coverage, care, supply, workforce, payment and rights workflows | eligibility, encounter, result, referral, claim, payment, appeal | Bitemporal events; state transitions; idempotency |

| Ledger and state | Maintain balances, capacity, queues, budgets, inventory and obligations | reserve, hospital budget, specialty slots, inventory, workforce FTE | Reconciliation; stock/flow distinction; exclusive booking |

| Assurance and evidence | Verify requirements, safety, quality, equity and phase gates | metric observations, audit results, safety events, gate packages | Independent verifier; immutable lineage; exception state |

| Analytic and simulation | Create reproducible comparison, forecast and sensitivity inputs | comparator observation, parameter version, scenario override, aggregate outputs | Snapshot/version; uncertainty; disclosure review |

| Public transparency | Publish understandable performance, rules, conflicts and corrections | dashboard metric, formula version, compact, audit finding | Aggregate approval; revision history; accessibility |
5.1.2 Record lifecycle
Authorize: identify the statutory/clinical authority, purpose, collection basis, access class and schema version.
Create or receive: assign record ID; capture event, effective and ingest times; validate identity and required fields.
Validate and reconcile: apply schema/terminology/business rules, duplicate checks and cross-ledger reconciliation; quarantine defects.
Use and disclose: enforce role, purpose, minimum necessary, segmentation/consent, break-glass and downstream-use policy.
Correct and supersede: adjudicate correction, preserve provenance and disputes, notify affected downstream systems, and recompute dependent outputs.
Archive, hold or dispose: apply controlled retention/disposition rules; preserve legal holds and public/audit history; log destruction. Exact periods remain OI-022.
5.1.3 Access classes
Table D4-5. Data access and sensitivity classes

| Class | Name | Scope | Minimum control | Examples |

| R0 | Public | Approved public records and aggregates | Anonymous access; publication review and version history | Public dashboards, formula registry, certified aggregate metrics |

| R1 | Operational—non-sensitive | Low-risk operational reference data | Role or service account; integrity logging | Facility directory, code sets, public capacity status |

| R2 | Confidential operational | Nonpublic financial, contracting, workforce, or security-adjacent data | Need-to-know; purpose binding; disclosure review | Hospital budget workpapers, workforce plans |

| R3 | Protected person/health | Identifiable clinical, eligibility, claims, or benefits data | Minimum necessary; role/purpose; segmentation; access audit | Longitudinal record, claim, referral, eligibility |

| R4 | Highly sensitive segmented | Records requiring heightened legal or ethical protection | Explicit segment policy; break-glass controls; enhanced notice and audit | Genetic, reproductive, behavioral-health, substance-use, tribal-governed data |

| R5 | Restricted safety/security/legal | Data whose disclosure could harm operations, safety, litigation, or national continuity | Named authorization; isolated environment; immutable audit; release adjudication | Cyber vulnerabilities, protected safety reports, sealed appeals |
5.1.4 Enforceable data rights
Table D4-6. Data-rights control set

| Control | Right | Operational rule | Trace |

| DR-01 | Notice and intelligibility | People receive understandable notice of collection, use, sharing, automated assistance, correction, appeal, and breach consequences. | SN-14, SN-15, SN-17, SN-19; TPP-USE1 |

| DR-02 | Access and portability | An authenticated person may inspect and obtain a usable copy of records and access history, subject only to narrow controlled exceptions. | SN-15; SR-RGT; IF-016–017 |

| DR-03 | Correction and provenance | A person may request correction; original, corrected, disputed, and superseded states remain traceable without presenting obsolete data as current. | TPP-10.5; VR-010 |

| DR-04 | Consent and segmentation | Where consent is the legal basis or a sensitive segment applies, authorization scope, duration, revocation, and downstream use are machine-enforceable. | SN-15; IF-017; OI-022 |

| DR-05 | Minimum necessary and purpose limitation | Access is limited to the minimum fields and period necessary for the declared care, payment, oversight, safety, public-health, or research purpose. | ASM-012; SR-DATA |

| DR-06 | Human review and contest | High-stakes AI-assisted decisions preserve the model/use record, accountable human reviewer, explanation, override, and appeal path. | ASM-009; SN-17; TPP-11.5 |

| DR-07 | Breach and continuity | Affected people and authorities receive timely notice, provisional protections, and correction when confidentiality, integrity, or availability fails. | SN-05, SN-13, SN-15; TPP-11.1–11.3 |

| DR-08 | Research and public transparency | Research uses governed, minimized data; public reporting uses approved aggregates, disclosure controls, provenance, and equity strata. | SN-20; IF-023, IF-030 |
HUMAN ACCOUNTABILITY  AI assistance does not change the identity of the accountable human or public authority. A model output is evidence attached to a decision record; it is not a self-authenticating legal or clinical decision. High-stakes use requires a registered model/use version, validation state, named human review, override path, contest mechanism, and suspension capability.
5.1.5 Authority, custody and verification rule

| Question | Required field | Rule |

| Who may define the datum? | source_authority | One controlling authority per version; joint authority must declare decision rights. |

| Who operates the store? | steward/custodian | May be different from authority; custody never expands permitted use. |

| Who may read/change it? | access policy | Role + purpose + minimum fields + time + segmentation; changes create events. |

| Who tests it? | verifier | Independent where required; verifier records method, evidence, result, uncertainty and exception. |

| Which record is operative? | effective/supersession state | Late arrival does not overwrite history; operative view is reproducible as of any snapshot. |
5.2 Required Data Sets for Framework Operation
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Enrollment, care, payment, supply, workforce, safety, and finance cannot be operated or simulated from one claims file; each function needs defined authoritative records. Why this structure: Data are specified as governed records with provenance, rights, and quality controls rather than as an undifferentiated national database. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes required data sets for framework operation explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Specify the minimum logical datasets and record envelopes needed to operate and simulate the framework; physical implementations may partition or federate them without changing semantics. |

| System entities | All Section 4 operating, oversight, judicial, regional, tribal and Treasury entities; patients, providers, facilities, suppliers, employers and researchers. |

| Assumptions | D4-DEC-01–04; dataset keys are local machine keys; exact API/code-set profiles remain OI-020. |

| Data / parameters | Fifty logical datasets; universal record envelope; fourteen record-level schema templates; data lineage and quality metadata. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-DATA; SR-IF-001–015; TPP-10.*, TPP-11.*, TPP-FORM1; KPP/TPP and CP observations. |

| Principal risks | Data duplication, ownership ambiguity, schema drift, incompatible time/geography definitions, nonrepresentative analytics, excessive collection. |

| Simulation implication | Each simulation module reads a versioned snapshot or event stream declared here; synthetic inputs must conform to the same schemas and access-class metadata. |
The catalog is logical. A dataset name is a stable semantic contract, not a mandate for one national database or a specific vendor. Dataset partitions may remain at federal, regional, tribal, state, facility, pharmacy, laboratory or other authorized nodes, provided the authority, identity, schema, provenance, rights and conformance rules are preserved.

5.2.1 Universal record envelope
Table D4-8. Fields inherited by operational and analytic records

| Field | Canonical type | Control |

| record_id | string/UUID | Unique within the declaring dataset; immutable |

| source_authority / steward | controlled entity IDs | Legal authority and operational custodian are separately identified |

| schema_version | semantic version | Points to a published schema and validation profile |

| event_time / effective_time / ingest_time | ISO-8601 | Observed event, legal/clinical effectiveness, and receipt are distinct |

| geography | versioned code | Nation, region, state, tribal jurisdiction, locality, facility as applicable |

| subject keys | governed references | Person, provider, facility, program, product, fund, or case keys as needed |

| population/equity strata | controlled categories | Collected only when lawful and necessary; missing/unknown remain explicit |

| authority/rule/formula version | object ID + version | Decision logic is reproducible for the effective period |

| provenance/evidence | source IDs + transformations | Origin, custody path, transformation, and verifier are retained |

| access_class / purpose / consent | R0–R5 + codes | Minimum-necessary enforcement, segmentation, and break-glass state |

| correction/supersession | record links + status | Corrections preserve the chain and identify the operative record |

| quality_flags | controlled array | Completeness, validity, timeliness, conformance, duplication, consistency |

| retention/disposition | status + dates | Active, archived, legal hold, suppressed, disposed; periods remain OI-022 |
5.2.2 Record-level schema templates
Templates define the required semantic core. A physical schema may add fields, split records, or use interoperable references, but it may not omit a controlled field needed for authority, rights, verification, reconciliation, or simulation without an approved exception.
Table D4-9. Schema-template catalog

| Schema key | Applies to | Required domain fields (universal envelope also applies) | Integrity constraints |

| schema.person_eligibility | registry.person; coverage.eligibility_event | person_key; identity_evidence; residency_basis; eligibility_class; provisional_flag; coverage_state; effective_start/end; termination_reason; decision_id | One eligibility event per authority decision; late correction supersedes rather than overwrites; termination requires notice/appeal state. |

| schema.provider_facility | registry.provider; registry.facility | entity_key; identifiers; credential/certification; scope/service; affiliation; geography; effective dates; status; verification_source | Affiliation is time-bounded; active status requires source verification; facility and provider keys are distinct. |

| schema.clinical_event | clinical.encounter/result/medication/care_plan | person_key; provider/facility; request/encounter/result times; code/value/unit; clinical status; responsible_owner; follow_up_due/closed; provenance | Clinical source is preserved; abnormal results require closure state; correction never erases provenance. |

| schema.referral_capacity | care.referral_packet/specialty_capacity/specialty_event | referral_id; person; specialty; region; diagnostic_packet; urgency_class/version; queue timestamps; protected_capacity_type; offer/completion/closure | Urgency version travels with referral; e-consult and urgent capacity cannot be double-counted; lost-to-follow-up is an explicit state. |

| schema.claim_payment | claims.*; payment.* | claim_id; service lines; coverage rule/version; adjudication state; obligation_id; payee; amount; due/payment time; explanation; appeal; reconciliation | A clean-claim flag is versioned; a payment event cannot substitute for an obligation; patient charge is separately recorded. |

| schema.hospital_budget | care.hospital_budget/service_line | hospital; period; operating/readiness/capital/teaching/drug/clinician components; certified amount; paid amount; variance; service-line state; staffing | Components are mutually exclusive or reconciled; capital, transition and recurring costs remain separate. |

| schema.supply | supply.formulary/drug_inventory/manufacturing/device_diagnostic | product/SKU; product_family; site; access_class; source; capacity; stock; demand; shortage; lot/release; unit_price; substitution | Stock and flow timestamps differ; shortage definition/version is mandatory; price retains net/gross basis. |

| schema.workforce | workforce.* | person/program/role keys; specialty; region; FTE; vacancy; slot; enrollment/completion; obligation; placement; workload; survey_weight | Headcount and FTE are not interchangeable; projections are distinguished from observed state. |

| schema.rights_case | rights.*; safety.event | case/event_id; affected person; decision/incident; urgency; evidence; accountable actor; reviewer; provisional relief; disposition; order; notice; corrective_action | Sealed/sensitive fields are segmented; operative orders remain available to systems that must execute them. |

| schema.fiscal_cost | fiscal.*; cost.event | ledger_event; authority; fund; payer/payee; CP_id; cost_view; amount; price_year; period; region; population; transition_project; offset_link; reconciliation | Every amount has one primary booking; gross cost and offset remain visible; reserves are balances, not annual expense. |

| schema.governance | governance.*; public.metric_release | object_id/version; owner; rule/formula; effective period; evidence; verifier; result; exception; notice; sunset; rollback; publication | Published revisions preserve prior versions; emergency changes require review and rollback path. |

| schema.ai_cyber | ai.model_decision; cyber.continuity_event | system/model/version; use_class; validation; input/output reference; human reviewer; override; drift; vulnerability/outage; failover; recovery; impact | Do not duplicate protected clinical payloads; reference them by governed key; high-stakes decisions require accountable human state. |

| schema.comparator | comparator.observation | comparator_id; metric_concept; value; unit; geography; population; reference period; publication vintage; evidence_id; definition; uncertainty; limitation | Reference year and source vintage are separate; forecasts and observations are explicitly typed. |

| schema.metric_observation | public.metric_release; governance.requirement_result | metric_id/version; numerator; denominator; exclusions; value; unit; baseline; target; period; geography; strata; uncertainty; status; evidence | No target is recorded as observed; suppression and weighting rules are versioned; missingness is reported. |
5.2.3 Exchange and snapshot conventions
Events are idempotent: replaying the same record_id and version cannot create a second legal, clinical, financial, or simulation event.
Every derived table or model input declares snapshot_time, source versions, transformation version, exclusions, quality state, and access/disclosure approval.
Person-level linkage uses governed keys or privacy-preserving linkage; public output never exposes operational identifiers.
Geography and jurisdiction are versioned because service regions, compact participation and tribal governance may change over time.
Terminologies and formulas are effective-dated. A result calculated under an older version remains reproducible and is not silently restated.
Simulation test data use synthetic identifiers and declare which missingness, error, latency, outage, correction, and adversarial conditions are injected.
5.3 KPP and TPP Dictionary
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: A performance target without a numerator, denominator, period, owner, and verifier can look precise while remaining impossible to compare or enforce. Why this structure: Data are specified as governed records with provenance, rights, and quality controls rather than as an undifferentiated national database. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes kpp and tpp dictionary explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Normalize every source KPP and TPP into a testable metric contract while preserving the source ID, name and target text. |

| System entities | Metric operating owners; NHASB scorekeeping; CHAO audit; NHAC rights/safety review; domain verifiers; PRTO publication. |

| Assumptions | D4-DEC-05; source target does not imply baseline or achievement; OI-001/008/021/023 remain explicit. |

| Data / parameters | Metric version; target; numerator/denominator; unit; eligibility/exclusions; baseline; time/geography; strata; source datasets; uncertainty; verifier result. |

| Requirements / performance | SN-01–25; PR/SR/VR; 41 KPPs; 79 TPPs; phase gates and public dashboard. |

| Principal risks | Metric gaming; denominator drift; target/baseline conflation; unmeasured equity; nonrepresentative survey; duplicate events; unaudited composite. |

| Simulation implication | Each metric is an output contract. Simulation runs emit its numerator, denominator, value, uncertainty and target comparison separately, including unavailable/not-baselined states. |
A metric is simulation-ready only when the source target and an executable observation contract are both present. The tables preserve all 120 source IDs and targets. Formula text below establishes the calculation shape; detailed eligibility, episode, risk-adjustment, survey, sampling and acceptance protocols remain versioned verification artifacts where indicated.
5.3.1 Common metric observation contract

| Field group | Required content |

| Identity | metric_id; metric_version; source target text; owner; verifier; requirement/need trace |

| Population | eligibility; exclusions; episode/exposure; denominator; geography; time; approved equity strata |

| Calculation | numerator/statistic; denominator; unit; weights/risk adjustment; missingness; suppression; rounding |

| Comparison | baseline value/version; target; direction; threshold period/phase; comparator scenario |

| Evidence | source datasets/snapshot; transformation code/version; quality state; uncertainty/confidence; verifier result |

| Publication | release state; explanation; revision/supersession; accessible machine and human display |

TPP-6.6 INTERPRETATION  The phrase '>=125% improvement' is ambiguous. Until OI-008 closes, simulation and verification must run both a 1.25x-baseline branch and a 2.25x-baseline branch, with clinical safety, under-referral and equity constraints applied to both. Neither branch becomes the controlled meaning by implication.
5.3.4 Verification result states

| State | Meaning | Allowed publication |

| specified | Target and calculation contract exist; baseline or evidence may not | Publish as specification, never as performance |

| baselined | Controlled comparator/reference observation and protocol exist | Publish baseline with vintage/uncertainty |

| measured | Observed value calculated from certified snapshot | Publish with quality and uncertainty |

| verified-pass / verified-fail | Independent verifier applied controlled acceptance protocol | Publish result, evidence class and exceptions |

| indeterminate | Missing, conflicting or insufficient evidence prevents decision | Publish limitation; do not coerce to pass/fail |

| superseded | New version controls prospective use; prior result retained | Publish version history and effective dates |
5.4 Cost Parameter Dictionary
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: A $4.75 trillion system cannot be simulated from a single total; cost drivers, units, distributions, correlations, and accounting boundaries must be explicit. Why this structure: Data are specified as governed records with provenance, rights, and quality controls rather than as an undifferentiated national database. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes cost parameter dictionary explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Normalize the complete 310-record cost dictionary into typed simulation and accounting objects without inventing missing values or concealing cost boundaries. |

| System entities | HFASB; THDO; NHETF; NHASB; CHAO; NHTCA; domain operating owners; hospitals; providers; suppliers; employers; households. |

| Assumptions | D4-DEC-06; D2-DEC-05/06; OI-001/002/011/017/024; real 2024 USD; source names remain controlling. |

| Data / parameters | CP ID; definition; unit; index; stock/flow; model role; price year; source/calibration; uncertainty; correlation; ledger/cost view. |

| Requirements / performance | PR-CST; KPP-C1–C8; CP-TOT/POP/CLM/HOSP/CLIN/UNIT/LTC/RX/DX/BH/DVH/EMS/PH/IT/GOV/RD/EDU/TRN/FIN/OFF. |

| Principal risks | Double counting; mixed price years; stock/flow confusion; gross/net substitution; public/total-system substitution; unrealized offsets; transition leakage. |

| Simulation implication | Every cost module emits gross recurring, capital, transition, reserve and offset events with CP IDs; the integrator reconciles them into public, residual-private, patient and total-system views. |
Master total-system equation  C_total_system(t) = C_hospital + C_clinical + C_units + C_LTC + C_drugs + C_devices_labs_diagnostics + C_behavioral + C_DVH + C_EMS + C_public_health + C_info_cyber_AI + C_governance_oversight + C_R&D + C_education_workforce + C_transition_net - C_offsets
Terms remain separately observable. A cost is not netted away inside a component and again in CP-OFF.
Offset equation  C_offsets(t) = ED_diversion_savings + avoidable_admission_savings + private_admin_savings + PBM_savings + drug_price_savings + duplicate_testing_savings + hospital_extraction_savings + revenue_cycle_savings + medical_debt_collection_savings
Offsets are realized savings relative to a versioned comparator, not automatically assumed design promises.
Cost views  C_total_system = C_net_public + C_residual_private + C_patient_paid; C_transition_adjusted = C_mature_operating + C_incremental_transition - realized_transition_offsets
Reserve authority/fund balance is reported separately from annual expense; financing transfers do not create health-system resource cost.

| Object | Class | Controlled quantity | Accounting treatment |

| CP-TOT-001 | FA / calibrated model output | $4.75T/year mature central; $4.30T–$5.25T/year plausible range | Total system; public + residual private + patient; 2024 USD |

| Transition envelope | FA / aggregate constraint | $1.2T–$2.0T over 10–12 years | Incremental time-limited implementation/continuity; component CP-TRN records reconcile to envelope |

| CP-TOT-007 | FA / output range | $4.90T–$5.05T/year first decade | Transition-adjusted annual total-system cost; not mature recurring cost |

| KPP-C1/C2 | TG / open | Source targets preserved; not baselined | OI-001 prevents substitution for controlled cost assumptions |
5.4.1 Accounting and simulation controls
Exclusive primary booking: each resource-use or transfer event has one primary CP, cost view and period. Allocation across dimensions must reconcile to that event.
Gross-before-net: gross resource cost, recovery, transfer and offset remain separately visible; a negative cost must reference the comparator event it offsets.
Stock/flow separation: reserve, inventory, installed capacity and fund balances are states; annual spending, receipts and services are flows; rates/prices are parameters.
Price and volume separation: costs store nominal amount, real-2024 amount, deflator, price, quantity and unit where applicable. A price change is not a utilization change.
Perspective separation: total-system resource cost, federal/public outlay, residual private spending, patient-paid spending, employer transfer and household incidence are distinct views.
Transition exclusivity: project, capital, continuity, stabilization and operating subledgers use mutually exclusive event IDs; transition cost cannot migrate silently into recurring operations.
Offset realization: an offset is recognized only when the corresponding comparator activity/cost falls and no constrained service, quality, safety or access requirement is violated.
Uncertainty: each CP value has provenance, status, distribution/bounds, correlation group and scenario override. Missing values remain MP/OI rather than zero.

5.5 Existing-System Comparator Data
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: The existing system changes over time, so both a frozen 2024 comparator and a current-policy comparator are needed to avoid attributing unrelated trends to the framework. Why this structure: Data are specified as governed records with provenance, rights, and quality controls rather than as an undifferentiated national database. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes existing-system comparator data explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the versioned empirical comparator against which NHAF scenarios are calibrated and evaluated, with definition symmetry and transparent gaps. |

| System entities | NHASB; CHAO; HFASB; PRTO; statistical agencies; CMS; Census; HRSA; GAO; FDA; SAMHSA; CDC; model builders. |

| Assumptions | D2-DEC-01–04; D4-DEC-07; 2024 principal baseline; older records retain actual year; projections retain vintage; OI-013/025. |

| Data / parameters | Twenty-three sourced comparator records; definition/unit/year/vintage; scenario path; uncertainty; limitation; gap and acquisition plan. |

| Requirements / performance | KPP/TPP baselines; CP calibration; CMP-STATIC-2024 static; CMP-CURRENT-POLICY current-policy; red-team/shock scenarios. |

| Principal risks | Cherry-picked years; incompatible measures; static-baseline bias; projection misuse; missing subgroup/region detail; framework/comparator asymmetry. |

| Simulation implication | Run NHAF and comparator with shared population, macro, shock and accounting assumptions where appropriate; preserve structural differences and report paired uncertainty. |
The comparator has two primary paths. CMP-STATIC-2024 is a static 2024 reference used for transparent cross-sectional comparisons. CMP-CURRENT-POLICY is a dynamic current-policy path using authoritative projections where available and separately calibrated submodules elsewhere. Shock and red-team scenarios apply the same exogenous event to both systems when logically possible; different resilience mechanisms remain endogenous.

COMPARATOR SYMMETRY  A framework target may not be compared with an existing-system observation as though both were achieved values. Primary outputs show observed/current-policy comparator distributions, NHAF simulated distributions, target thresholds, and the difference between systems—each with period, definition and uncertainty.
5.5.1 Comparator acquisition gaps
Table D4-16. Calibration gaps and controlled acquisition plan

| Gap key | Required concept | Trace | Current limitation | Acquisition/validation action |

| administration | Administrative spending and transaction cost by payer/provider function | KPP-C3/C4; CP-CLM/CP-OFF | No controlled nationally comparable functional baseline | Commission a cross-payer/provider time-and-cost study; preserve payer and provider perspectives. |

| primary_access | Same-day/front-door request-to-care time and low-acuity ED avoidability | KPP-B1–B3 | No harmonized request-origin national series | Define request episode; collect stratified patient/provider/event data before target verification. |

| specialty_access | Routine/urgent specialist wait, e-consult resolution, queue equity | KPP-B4–B6/T-ED-003; TPP-7.* | National denominators and urgency standards absent | Pilot structured referral/capacity ledger and publish specialty-region distributions. |

| quality_safety | Avoidable admissions, readmissions, prevention, control, safety-report completeness | KPP-D1–D6 | Definitions/risk adjustment/reporting capture require calibration | Version measure specifications; link clinical and safety records; estimate under-reporting. |

| experience_trust | Patient experience, fairness trust, clinician safety culture | KPP-D7/TRUST1/CULT1 | Survey instrument and baseline not controlled | Select representative instruments, weights, modes, languages and repeatability rules. |

| employer_household | Employer admin burden, wage pass-through, ordinary-household incidence | KPP-A6/C8; TPP-EMP1 | Incidence and counterfactual wage response require modeling | Link employer/payroll survey and tax microdata under disclosure controls; test behavioral ranges. |

| ltc_capacity | LTC need, unmet demand, workforce, home/community/institutional capacity | TPP-9.1/9.2; CP-LTC | Coverage rule is sourced, demand/capacity baseline is incomplete | Build functional-need and service-capacity microbaseline; include unpaid caregiving. |

| equity | Comparable coverage, access, quality and outcome gaps | KPP-E1–T-ED-005 | Strata, reference group, missingness and small-cell rules incomplete | Control strata and suppression policy; publish maximum, distribution and intersectional analyses. |
5.5.2 Comparator transformation rules
Retain source definition, population, geography, reference period, publication vintage, nominal/real basis and uncertainty. Never overwrite an older record with a newer definition under the same key/version.
Convert currency using a declared deflator and retain the source nominal value. Convert rates only when numerator and denominator concepts are compatible.
Do not mix point-in-time stocks with annual flows, forecast values with observations, or state ACS coverage measures with CPS annual national measures without an explicit bridge.
For a missing national baseline, use a range, pilot estimate or hierarchical prior labeled MP/OI; report sensitivity and information value. Do not insert an unsupported national point estimate.
Version all crosswalks and risk adjustment. Publish pre- and post-adjustment values where adjustment materially changes conclusions.

5.6 Data Quality, Uncertainty, and Sensitivity
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: False precision would make the simulation persuasive but unreliable; missingness, bias, uncertainty, and sensitivity therefore require their own operating rules. Why this structure: Data are specified as governed records with provenance, rights, and quality controls rather than as an undifferentiated national database. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes data quality, uncertainty, and sensitivity explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Make data fitness, uncertainty, model dependence and sensitivity visible enough for operational decisions, phase gates, public reporting and reproducible simulation. |

| System entities | Data authorities/stewards; NHRA; HCCA; NHASB; CHAO; NHAC; domain verifiers; model validation teams; PRTO. |

| Assumptions | D4-DEC-03/07/08; missing is not zero; uncertainty type is explicit; OI-021/024/025. |

| Data / parameters | Quality dimensions; validation results; missingness; provenance; uncertainty distribution/bounds; correlation; scenario; sensitivity indices; validation evidence. |

| Requirements / performance | VR-001–015; TPP-10/11/12/FORM; all KPP/TPP; phase gates; CP dictionary; SCN outputs. |

| Principal risks | False precision; hidden missingness; unmodeled correlation/tails; overfitting; data leakage; unjustified causal inference; inequitable measurement error. |

| Simulation implication | Run deterministic reconciliation, stochastic uncertainty, structural alternatives, global sensitivity, subgroup/region checks, calibration and out-of-sample validation. |
5.6.1 Data-quality controls
Table D4-17. Quality dimensions and dispositions

| Control | Dimension | Test concept | Indicator | Disposition |

| DQ-01 | Completeness | Required fields and expected records present | missing-field rate; expected/observed record ratio | Reject, quarantine, impute only under registered rule |

| DQ-02 | Validity | Value obeys type, range, terminology and business rule | validation-failure rate | Quarantine; source correction; do not silently coerce |

| DQ-03 | Timeliness | Data arrive within clinical/operational/statistical deadline | ingest_time - event_time; late rate | Flag stale state; use provisional estimate only if disclosed |

| DQ-04 | Conformance | Schema, code set, interface and version comply | conformance pass rate | Versioned transformation or rejection |

| DQ-05 | Uniqueness | No unintended duplicate event/entity | duplicate and merge/split error rates | Preserve lineage; correct identity links |

| DQ-06 | Consistency | Cross-field and cross-dataset states do not conflict | rule-violation rate; reconciliation difference | Reconcile by authority precedence; retain dispute |

| DQ-07 | Provenance | Source, authority, transformations and verifier are reproducible | lineage-complete rate | Exclude from certified metric if material lineage missing |

| DQ-08 | Representativeness | Population/geography/time and nonresponse support inference | coverage, response, weight diagnostics | Weight/adjust; report limits; do not generalize unsupported |

| DQ-09 | Privacy/disclosure | Use and publication meet R-class and disclosure rules | unauthorized access; reidentification/small-cell checks | Suppress/aggregate; incident and remedy workflow |
5.6.2 Uncertainty representation
Table D4-18. Uncertainty types

| Code | Type | Meaning | Required representation |

| U-EPI | Epistemic | Unknown but learnable parameter or definition | Range/distribution from evidence; value-of-information analysis |

| U-ALE | Aleatory | Inherent event/person/region variability | Stochastic draw with calibrated distribution and seed |

| U-STR | Structural | Alternative causal/model architecture | Competing model forms/scenarios; model averaging only if justified |

| U-IMP | Implementation | Adoption, delay, compliance, learning and ramp uncertainty | Phase/region curves, correlated implementation scenarios |

| U-POL | Policy/legal | Authority, judicial, appropriation, compact or sabotage outcome | Discrete legal/governance scenarios with fallback states |
Every uncertain MP or calibrated CP should carry: central/nominal value if justified; lower and upper bound or distribution family/parameters; evidence/provenance; reference period/geography/population; correlation group; truncation/support; update rule; scenario override; and calibration/validation status. Outputs report distributions or intervals, not only means.

5.6.4 Analysis sequence
Unit and accounting tests: validate schema, dimensions, stock/flow identity, ledger reconciliation and invariant constraints before calibration.
Comparator calibration: reproduce controlled existing-system baseline records within stated tolerances and identify uncalibrated modules.
Local diagnostics: vary one parameter near baseline to detect sign, scale, discontinuity, threshold and coding errors; do not treat this as global sensitivity.
Global uncertainty: sample joint distributions with correlation and tail assumptions; report outcome distributions and failure probabilities by scenario.
Global sensitivity: calculate variance- or distribution-based importance for key outcomes and failure states; include interaction effects where material.
Structural/scenario alternatives: compare cost boundary, TPP-6.6 interpretation, rollout, financing, workforce, legal, transition and shock structures.
Validation: use temporal, regional, subgroup and event holdouts where possible; test face, construct, predictive, policy and extreme-condition validity.
Decision reporting: show which conclusions are robust, which depend on open assumptions, which parameters merit data collection, and which gates must not advance.
5.6.5 Minimum reproducibility package

| Artifact | Required content |

| Input manifest | Dataset/parameter IDs and versions; snapshots; access/disclosure approval; quality state; missingness and transformations |

| Model manifest | Code/model version; module/configuration; formulas; random seed policy; solver/runtime; dependency lock |

| Scenario manifest | SCN ID/version; comparator path; phase state; shocks; overrides; legal/governance state; stopping rules |

| Execution record | Run ID; start/end; hardware/runtime; warnings; reconciliation results; failed/indeterminate checks |

| Output package | KPP/TPP/CP numerator/denominator/value/uncertainty; distributional outcomes; audit trail; machine and human formats |

| Verification package | Independent method; acceptance criteria; evidence links; result; exceptions; reviewer and timestamp |
6. Concepts
6.1 National Health Assurance Concept
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: The public needs a plain account of how automatic coverage, benefits, care, payment, rights, and private residual roles work together during an ordinary healthcare episode. Why this structure: Each concept joins institutions, workflows, rights, performance measures, risks, and simulation behavior in one operational explanation. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes national health assurance concept explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the end-to-end operating concept for automatic public default coverage, covered-care financial protection, public adjudication/payment, bounded private roles and enforceable rights. |

| System entities | ARCH-DNHA; ARCH-NEEA; ARCH-NCCA; ARCH-THDO; ARCH-NHA-TRUST; ARCH-NHETF; ARCH-HFASB; ARCH-PPCO; ARCH-NHAC; ARCH-PROO; ARCH-A1-HCAC; patients; providers. |

| Assumptions | ASM-003 public default; ASM-004 bounded private roles; ASM-006 zero/near-zero point-of-care price; ASM-007 capacity gate; ASM-013 durable/repairable; OI-005/010/026. |

| Data / parameters | registry.person; coverage.eligibility_event/private_plan_certification; claims.medical; payment.*; rights.appeal_case; fiscal.*; public.metric_release. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-COV-001–011; SR-PAY-001–010; KPP-A1–A7/C4; TPP-1.1–1.4/2.1–2.5; IF-001–004/021–025. |

| Principal risks | Coverage error/churn; hidden billing; payment-rail failure; private-role duplication/risk selection; prior-review creep; executive interference; unusable appeals. |

| Simulation implication | Model person-time coverage state, eligibility latency/error, care demand, patient price, claim/payment state, appeals, residual private roles, household burden, provider cash flow and fiscal obligations. |
National Health Assurance (NHA) is the public core coverage and payment system administered by the Department of National Health Assurance (DNHA) through the allocated national, regional and independent-accountability architecture. Its service promise is that an eligible person can seek medically necessary covered care without first proving employment-linked insurance status, absorbing routine point-of-care financial risk, or navigating conflicting payer rules. The economic cost remains real and publicly financed; the point-of-care price and covered-care debt exposure are the variables driven toward zero.
6.1.1 Service principles and operational contracts
Table D5A-5. NHA principles translated into operating contracts

| Principle | Operating contract | Authoritative data | Performance trace |

| Public default | Eligible people enter active coverage automatically; unresolved identity/eligibility cases receive provisional coverage. | coverage.eligibility_event | KPP-A1/A2; TPP-1.2–1.4 |

| Covered-care financial protection | Covered medically necessary care normally carries zero or near-zero point-of-care price; covered-care debt and balance billing are prohibited. | claims.medical; public.metric_release | KPP-A3–A5 |

| Employment independence | Employment does not determine access to core coverage; employer transition and wage pass-through are separate obligations. | coverage.eligibility_event; workforce.transition | KPP-A6; TPP-EMP1 |

| Public payment | NCCA adjudicates the covered obligation; THDO executes mandatory payment and remittance; patient liability remains a separate explicit field. | claims.medical; payment.obligation/disbursement/remittance | TPP-2.1–2.5; KPP-C4 |

| Bounded private role | Only certified supplemental, substitute, or fixed-fee administrative roles may coexist with the core benefit; final boundaries remain OI-005. | coverage.private_plan_certification | ASM-004; SR-COV |

| Low-friction routine care | Routine covered care is not delayed by legacy-style prospective authorization; bounded high-risk/high-cost/nonstandard review remains OI-026. | governance.formula_version; rights.appeal_case | SN-03/SN-14; TPP-LEG1 |

| Enforceable rights | Denial, delay, routing, exception, termination and payment decisions preserve facts, rule/version, accountable reviewer, explanation, provisional relief and appeal. | rights.appeal_case; governance.requirement_result | SN-14/SN-20; TPP-12.6/LEG1 |

6.1.2 Coverage-state model
Table D5A-6. Person coverage states and transition safeguards

| State | Entry condition | Required behavior | Permitted next state |

| coverage.unresolved | Identity or eligibility evidence is incomplete | Activate provisional state within 24 hours; no care/payment denial solely because resolution is pending | coverage.provisional |

| coverage.provisional | Temporary public coverage is operative | Continue verification; pay covered care; give notice and review before adverse change | coverage.active or coverage.disputed |

| coverage.active | Core public entitlement is operative | Maintain continuity across employment, income, geography and life events | coverage.active |

| coverage.disputed | Proposed termination, duplicate-role, benefit or identity decision is contested | Continue legally required provisional protection; compile decision record; expedite review | coverage.active, modified, or terminated |

| coverage.terminated | Controlled legal basis and effective date exist | Require notice, explanation, appeal and post-termination continuity rules; erroneous termination remains measured | coverage.active on reversal or terminal |
Continuous coverage  KPP-A1 = eligible person-time continuously covered / eligible person-time
Coverage is measured as person-time, not merely a point-in-time enrollment snapshot. Provisional coverage counts only while legally operative and must remain distinguishable from resolved active coverage.
Patient price  patient_charge = covered_allowed_charge - public_obligation - certified_other_payment; for covered medically necessary core care, patient_charge -> 0
The claims record retains any patient charge and the rule/version that created it. A nonzero value is not hidden inside provider payment and is subject to billing/rights controls.
6.1.3 End-to-end covered-care transaction
Identity and coverage: NEEA resolves the person key and active/provisional state through IF-001/002. An unresolved case receives provisional protection rather than a front-door denial.
Care and coverage rule: the provider identifies the covered service and controlling benefit/formula version. Routine covered care proceeds without legacy-style prospective authorization; bounded review classes remain OI-026.
Clinical delivery: care is delivered by the appropriate primary, unit, specialty, hospital, pharmacy, long-term-care, behavioral-health or other covered pathway. Clinical necessity remains accountable to human professionals.
Adjudication: NCCA validates coverage, service, coding, duplication, patient charge, explanation and appeal rights. A clean claim becomes a certified legal obligation.
Disbursement: THDO pays the provider/pharmacy/hospital through IF-003/004. Late clean transition claims receive provisional Treasury payment and later reconciliation.
Rights and correction: the complete decision record supports operational reconsideration, NHAC review and expedited Article I relief through IF-021/022. Reversals propagate to coverage, claim, payment, debt and public reporting records.
Assurance: NHASB/CHAO test coverage, billing, debt, claim cost, payment and fiscal performance; PRTO publishes approved aggregates without presenting targets as achieved results.
6.1.4 Benefit and prospective-review boundary

| Class | Baseline treatment | Guardrail | Status |

| Core medically necessary | Public default coverage; zero/near-zero point-of-care price; routine care generally no prospective authorization | Benefit/rule version, explanation, audit and appeal remain | Framework baseline; detailed clinical coverage OI-010 |

| Conditional/high-risk/high-cost/nonstandard | Bounded clinical/evidence review may precede nonemergency service | Statutory clock, accountable reviewer, no emergency delay, reasons/evidence, provisional relief and appeal | OI-026 |

| Clinically linked supports | Covered only when linked to medical need and controlled eligibility | Do not charge general social-policy cost to NHA absent clinical link | ASM-014; OI-010 |

| Residual private/amenity | May be offered only under certified role | Cannot displace or relabel the public core or weaken public rights | OI-005/010 |

| Excluded general policy | Outside core health-system boundary | Requires explicit scope change before cost or performance enters NHA | Scope control |

Table D5A-7. Permitted role classes pending final statutory boundaries

| Role | Permitted purpose | Core guardrails | Status |

| Supplemental | Benefits outside the public core or noncovered amenities | May not relabel covered core care, balance bill, or use core-data access for risk selection | OI-005/OI-010 |

| Certified substitute | Narrow alternative meeting or exceeding public standards under statute | Must preserve rights, data, continuity, risk adjustment and public fallback; exact role open | OI-005 |

| Fixed-fee administrator | Administrative service without bearing unmanaged core-benefit insurance risk | Transparent fee; public rules; auditability; no PBM-style spread or opaque denial incentives | OI-005; ASM-004/005 |
6.1.6 Capacity and phase dependency
CAPACITY GATE  Zero or near-zero point-of-care price is a coverage design assumption, but broad national removal of cost sharing is a gated implementation event. Gate 2 must show adequate unit coverage, same-day access, closed-loop follow-up and safe referral performance. Failure delays the phase transition; it does not authorize permanent financial barriers as a substitute for capacity.

| Provider/payment | clean/manual/improper claims; obligation/payment time; disruption; provisional payment/recovery | TPP-2.1–2.5; KPP-C4 |

6.2 Four-Unit Diagnostic-Treatment Network Concept
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Insurance expansion alone cannot create appointments; distributed diagnostic-treatment capacity is needed to absorb routine demand without turning emergency departments into the default front door. Why this structure: Each concept joins institutions, workflows, rights, performance measures, risks, and simulation behavior in one operational explanation. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes four-unit diagnostic-treatment network concept explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Specify the front-door capacity architecture that safely absorbs routine measurable care and low-acuity demand while preserving relationship-based primary care and appropriate escalation. |

| System entities | ARCH-ACDRH; ARCH-RHA; ARCH-OCDTI; ARCH-NCDTN; ARCH-NEMTA; ARCH-NPHPA; ARCH-NHRA; ARCH-AICIO; primary care; units; EMS; patients. |

| Assumptions | ASM-007 capacity-before-price; ASM-008 specialist constraint; ASM-009 human-accountable AI; expected absorption ranges are MP; OI-007/008/027/032. |

| Data / parameters | registry.facility/provider; clinical.encounter/result/medication/care_plan; care.unit_encounter/ems_transport; workforce.*; supply.*; public.metric_release. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-ACC-001–015; KPP-B1–B3/B7–B9; TPP-6.1–6.6; IF-007/011/012/016–020; Gate 2/5/6. |

| Principal risks | Underbuild; workforce/equipment mismatch; unsafe under-referral; diagnostic/antibiotic overuse; follow-up loss; AI bias; cyber outage; rural/weather fragility. |

| Simulation implication | Represent geography, demand, eligibility, unit type, staffing/equipment, safe service rate, queue, encounter state, escalation, bounce-back, follow-up, capital/operating cost and substitution. |
The four-unit network is the framework's distributed front door, not a wholesale replacement for primary care. Its controlled family consists of Type A Micro-Units, Type B Standard Neighborhood Diagnostic and Treatment Units, Type C Rural Enhanced Units and Type D Urban/Public Health Units. It standardizes national capabilities while allowing regional siting, hours, staffing and mobile configurations. Routine, measurable and protocol-bounded work shifts toward convenient diagnostic-treatment capacity; complex longitudinal judgment remains anchored in primary care and specialty/hospital pathways.

Eligible demand  unit_eligible_demand(t,r,c) = total_requests(t,r,c) x clinical_eligibility_share x access/adoption_share
Eligibility and adoption are distinct. A request may be clinically unit-eligible but unable or unwilling to use a unit because of geography, hours, language, disability, continuity needs or preference.
Safe unit capacity  safe_capacity(t,r,u) = certified_units x open_hours x staffed_clinician_hours x safe_throughput x uptime x capability_match
Throughput is constrained by diagnostic completeness, human accountability, follow-up and scope. Productivity cannot be increased by suppressing escalation or omitting required work.
Realized absorption  absorbed_encounters = min(unit_eligible_demand, safe_capacity) subject to KPP-B9, TPP-6.2–6.5 and Gate 2
Demand exceeding safe capacity remains queued, routed to primary care, escalated or otherwise served; it does not disappear from total-system demand.
6.2.3 Encounter state model
Table D5A-11. Unit encounter states

| State | Meaning | Guard/output |

| request.received | Channel, location, symptoms, constraints and identity/coverage are recorded | Request timestamp starts KPP-B1/B2 clocks |

| triage.screened | Acuity, red flags and population-specific lower thresholds are applied | Emergency/unstable cases bypass unit workflow to EMS/ED |

| unit.accepted | Encounter fits certified unit capabilities, staffing, equipment and scope | Assign accountable clinician and follow-up owner |

| diagnostics.in_progress | Protocol-required history, exam, tests and stewardship checks occur | Disposition prohibited until applicable completeness rule passes or documented emergency exception applies |

| resolved_or_managed | Treatment, prescription, protocol management or scheduled recheck closes immediate request | Write longitudinal record; monitor seven-day escalation/bounce-back |

| escalated | Primary care, e-consult, tele-specialty, in-person specialist, hospital or EMS pathway is initiated | Structured handoff and urgency class; no capacity-protection hold for red flags |

| follow_up_open | Abnormal result, recheck, medication or handoff requires action | Responsible owner and due time remain visible |

| closed | Result/action and patient notice are complete | Closure evidence supports TPP-6.3; late/bounce-back events remain linked |
6.2.4 Safety architecture
Table D5A-12. Non-negotiable safety controls

| Control | Operational rule | Trace |

| Human accountability | AI does not act as final clinician; high-stakes routing/non-escalation requires accountable human review | ASM-009; TPP-11.4–11.6 |

| Forced escalation | Red flags, instability and time-sensitive disease override throughput, queue and capacity goals | KPP-B9; SR-SPEC-007 |

| Lower thresholds | Pediatric, pregnancy, older-adult, immunocompromised and complex patients use lower escalation thresholds | OI-032; clinical protocol version |

| Diagnostic completeness | Applicable first-line diagnostics precede unit disposition; emergency exceptions remain explicit | SR-ACC-011; TPP-6.2 |

| Closed-loop follow-up | Abnormal results have owner, due time, notice, action and closure state | SR-ACC-012; TPP-6.3 |

| Stewardship | Antibiotic and diagnostic appropriateness are monitored and audited | SR-ACC-013; TPP-6.4 |

| Bounce-back review | Same-problem 72-hour return and seven-day escalation trigger linked review | SR-ACC-014; KPP-B8 |

| Longitudinal writeback | Every encounter, result, medication and handoff writes to the federated record | IF-007; TPP-10.* |
ANTI-GAMING INVARIANT  A unit may not improve resolution, productivity, ED-diversion or cost metrics by avoiding diagnostics, delaying escalation, relabeling bounce-backs, excluding complex patients without transparent rules, or transferring unresolved follow-up. KPP-B8/TPP-6.6 must be read with KPP-B9 and TPP-6.2–6.5.
6.2.5 Siting, capacity and resilience inputs
Table D5A-13. Regional siting model inputs

| Input domain | Required variables | Trace |

| Demand | Population, age/clinical mix, observed requests, unmet need, released demand, seasonal/surge profile | CP-POP; CP-UNIT; SG-DEMAND |

| Access | Travel time, operating hours, transit/mobile reach, disability/language access, weather and connectivity | KPP-B7/T-ED-002/T-ED-004; OI-027 |

| Capacity | Unit type, rooms/stations, equipment, clinician/technician hours, safe throughput, uptime | CP-UNIT-001–024; TPP-6.1/6.6 |

| System substitution | Primary-care availability, ED patterns, specialist/EMS/hospital proximity, pharmacy/lab links | KPP-B3/B8; IF-007/011/012 |

| Equity | Rural, tribal, safety-net, disability, language, income and historically underserved gaps | KPP-E2/T-ED-004/T-ED-005; SN-18/SN-24 |

| Resilience | Mobile reserve, backup power/connectivity, climate/public-health surge and cyber/offline operation | TPP-11.1/11.2; SCN-CYBER/PANDEMIC/RURAL-STRESS |
6.2.6 Phase and scenario behavior
PH-P4 pilots Type A–D capabilities, workflow, safety, workforce, capital and specialist/EMS/hospital interfaces in varied regions.
PH-P5 scales certified units and expands specialty ledgers; regional evidence updates siting, staffing, equipment and demand parameters.
PH-P6 may combine national public default coverage with major cost-sharing elimination only after Gate 2 passes and transition/legitimacy dependencies permit conversion.
SCN-UNIT-UNDER delays Gate 2, routes excess demand to existing capacity, activates mobile/converted options and measures ED/primary/specialist spillover rather than assuming unmet demand disappears.
SCN-RURAL-STRESS tests Type C, weather resilience, EMS transfer, tele-specialty, rural pharmacy links and protected hospital services together.
SCN-AI-FAIL suspends affected models and reduces modeled productivity while human/manual triage, documentation and routing continue.

6.3 Specialist Backplane Concept
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Specialists are scarce and unevenly distributed; structured questions, complete packets, urgency classes, e-consults, and visible capacity are needed to use their time safely. Why this structure: Each concept joins institutions, workflows, rights, performance measures, risks, and simulation behavior in one operational explanation. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes specialist backplane concept explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the clinical-routing and capacity-control backplane that converts complete first-line work into timely e-consult, tele-specialty, diagnostic-first, in-person, urgent, hospital or emergency pathways. |

| System entities | ARCH-NSAA; ARCH-RHA; ARCH-OCDTI/NCDTN; primary care; specialists; ARCH-NHRA; ARCH-NOPRSL; ARCH-NHAC; ARCH-AICIO; hospitals; EMS; patients. |

| Assumptions | ASM-008 specialist capacity is binding; D5A-DEC-04/05/12; OI-012/020/023/028/032. |

| Data / parameters | care.referral_packet/specialty_capacity/specialty_event; clinical.*; rights.appeal_case; registry.provider/facility; public.metric_release. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-SPEC-001–010; SR-ACC-004–006/009; KPP-B4–B6/B9/T-ED-003; TPP-7.1–7.5/LEG1; IF-008–010/021/023. |

| Principal risks | Queue collapse; incomplete packets; false urgency; unsafe deferral; capacity double counting; lost referral; inequitable wait; AI routing bias; patient constraints ignored. |

| Simulation implication | Model specialty-region demand, route level, urgency, packet completeness, service-time distributions, protected capacity, queue/offer/completion, reclassification, safety events, equity and workforce expansion. |
The specialist routing backplane is a shared national-regional service combining e-consults, tele-specialty, diagnostic-first pathways, structured referral packets, urgency classes, regional specialty capacity ledgers and protected urgent specialist slots. It does not make specialist capacity infinite; it makes demand, diagnostic readiness, urgency, available capacity, responsibility and failure visible. Its core efficiency rule—complete first-line work before routine specialist use—is always subordinate to the safety counter-rule: red flags, instability and time-sensitive disease cannot be held to protect capacity.
6.3.1 Routing ladder
Table D5A-15. Level 0–7 routing ladder

| Level | Route | Operational contract |

| 0 | Resolved in unit or primary care | No specialist work required; follow-up remains assigned where needed |

| 1 | Protocol management with automated follow-up | Accountable clinician remains responsible; AI/automation may support reminders and monitoring |

| 2 | Specialist e-consult | Specialist answers focused question using complete packet; may resolve, request workup or reclassify |

| 3 | Tele-specialist visit | Patient-specialist interaction without in-person facility requirement |

| 4 | Diagnostic-first specialist pathway | Defined diagnostic work precedes or substitutes for conventional consult sequence |

| 5 | In-person specialist visit | Routine/expedited/new or complex in-person capacity |

| 6 | Urgent specialist or hospital pathway | Same-day or 24–72-hour protected capacity; direct coordination |

| 7 | Emergency transfer | Immediate EMS/ED; no routine queue placement |
6.3.2 Urgency classes
Table D5A-16. Source-controlled urgency classes

| Class | Meaning | Target | Routing treatment |

| E | Emergency | Immediate EMS/ED | No queue; direct transfer and handoff |

| U1 | Urgent—same day | Same day | Protected urgent specialist/hospital capacity |

| U2 | Urgent—stable | 24–72 hours | Protected urgent capacity; monitor for deterioration |

| T-ED-001 | Expedited | 1–2 weeks | Prioritized regional queue |

| R1 | Routine high-value | 30 days | Routine queue with value/need rule |

| R2 | Routine lower-complexity | 45–60 days | Routine queue; may resolve through Levels 1–4 |

| EC | E-consult only | 24–72 hours | Dedicated e-consult block |

| D | Diagnostic-first | Protocol-specific | Diagnostic pathway clock and follow-up owner required |
The source target is preserved for each class. Exact clock start, allowed pause, reclassification, missed-offer and cross-region rules remain OI-028. An urgency class is a clinical state with accountable authority and versioned evidence, not an administrative priority label.
6.3.3 Structured referral contract
Table D5A-17. Required referral-packet fields

| Machine field | Content | Requirement |

| problem_representation | Concise problem summary and relevant context | required |

| clinical_question | Specific decision or assistance requested | required |

| red_flag_screen | Positive/negative/unknown with protocol version | required |

| completed_tests | First-line tests, dates, values, images and provenance | required when applicable |

| treatments_tried | Treatment, dose/duration, response, adverse effects | required when applicable |

| medication_list | Current medicines, allergies and reconciliation state | required |

| relevant_results | Images, labs, pathology and other diagnostic artifacts | required when applicable |

| patient_constraints | Language, disability, travel, caregiving, availability, preference and other access constraints | required/unknown explicit |

| urgency_class | Class, assigning authority, protocol version and timestamp | required |

| follow_up_owner | Accountable person/team and due action | required |
PACKET EXCEPTION  Incomplete first-line work may be bypassed only when the missing work is unsafe, unavailable, clinically inappropriate, or would create harmful delay. The exception records the responsible clinician, reason, evidence, urgency, missing item and downstream owner; it does not silently convert an incomplete packet into a complete one.

| Category | Capacity represented | Double-counting control |

| urgent | U1/U2/T-ED-001 protected slots and coordination time | Cannot be counted again as routine new-patient or general availability |

| e_consult | Asynchronous review blocks | Record available minutes/cases and response clock; do not count as in-person slots |

| tele_specialty | Synchronous remote visits | Track clinician time and room/technology constraints |

| new_patient | In-person new or diagnostically complex visits | Track specialty-specific duration/case mix |

| follow_up_complex | Continuity, complex management and return capacity | Protect against displacement by new-patient targets |

| procedure_planning | Pre-procedure evaluation and planning | Separate from procedure-room/operating capacity |

| Metric | Measure | Source target | Status |

| KPP-B4 | Specialist e-consult resolution rate | >=40% | Source target; baseline/acceptance evidence required |

| KPP-B5 | Routine specialist wait time | median <=30 days | Source target; baseline/acceptance evidence required |

| KPP-B6 | Urgent specialist timeliness | >=95% within urgency-class target | Source target; baseline/acceptance evidence required |

| KPP-E3 | Specialist wait equity ratio | <=1.10 | Source target; baseline/acceptance evidence required |

| TPP-7.1 | Referral packet completeness | >=98% | Source target; baseline/acceptance evidence required |

| TPP-7.3 | Inappropriate specialist referral rate | <=5% | Source target; baseline/acceptance evidence required |
