| TPP-7.5 | Regional queue participation | >=95% publicly paid specialists | Source target; baseline/acceptance evidence required |
Available specialty capacity  available_capacity(t,r,k,q) = staffed_time - committed_time - unavailable_time, indexed by region r, specialty k and category q
A scheduled slot and the clinician time behind it are one resource. The ledger retains duration, modality, skill, facility/technology constraints and reservation/release state.
Queue evolution  queue_next = queue_current + validated_arrivals + reclassified_in - completed - resolved_by_econsult - withdrawn - reclassified_out
Every subtraction is an explicit event. 'Resolved by e-consult' requires a returned clinical answer and accountable follow-up, not mere referral cancellation.
6.3.5 Referral state model and rights
Table D5A-19. Referral lifecycle states

| State | Meaning | Guard/output |

| packet.draft | Referrer compiles fields and source evidence | Incomplete; not yet in routine scheduling queue |

| packet.validated | Required fields and diagnostic prerequisites pass or a justified exception is recorded | Starts completeness and routing workflow |

| urgency.assigned | Authorized clinician assigns class/version/time | Starts class clock; review/override remains auditable |

| route.selected | Level 0–7 is selected | Emergency/urgent safety rules dominate capacity optimization |

| capacity.reserved | Named ledger category and slot/effort are reserved | No double counting; expiration/release event required |

| care.offered | Patient receives accessible offer and instructions | Constraints, declined/missed offers and clock effects are recorded |

| care.completed | Consult, diagnostic pathway or visit occurs | Specialist returns answer/plan and responsibility |

| follow_up.closed | Referrer/specialist/patient actions and results are closed | Closure owner, notices and unresolved exceptions remain visible |
The patient and referrer receive an explanation of the route and urgency class, accessible timing information and the identity of the follow-up owner.
A patient/referrer may seek urgency or routing review without losing the existing queue position or emergency access. Urgent provisional relief remains available.
The system records offers, patient constraints, failed contact, declined/missed appointments, clock effects and alternate routes; it does not label access failure as patient choice without evidence.
Specialist answers, diagnostic requirements and returned plans write to the longitudinal record and close the loop with the accountable referrer/team.
Equity monitoring compares wait, completion, reclassification and loss-to-follow-up by region and approved strata; correction plans use IF-032 when gaps exceed controlled limits.
6.3.6 Performance and failure behavior

| Condition | Expected backplane behavior | Measured effects |

| Normal | Route eligible work to e-consult/tele/diagnostic-first/in-person; protect urgent capacity; return plan | KPP-B4–B6; TPP-7.1–7.5 |

| SCN-SPEC-SEVERE | Activate cross-region routing, protected-capacity enforcement, tele/e-consult expansion, workforce premium/training and transparent backlog | wait distribution, safety, equity, completion, cost |

| Red flag/deterioration | Immediate class/route escalation; do not preserve routine queue optimization | KPP-B9; adverse events; clock and handoff |

| AI failure | Suspend affected routing model; human review/manual queue continues | productivity, delay, override, safety/equity |

| Cyber/downtime | Use offline referral/urgent roster; reconcile capacity, offers and completions after recovery | continuity success, duplicate/lost events |
6.4 Hospital Public-Service Model
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Per-service hospital payment rewards volume and permits essential but unprofitable services to disappear; a public-service obligation requires a different budget and accountability model. Why this structure: Each concept joins institutions, workflows, rights, performance measures, risks, and simulation behavior in one operational explanation. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes hospital public-service model explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Specify the charter, global-budget, readiness, capital, essential-service, staffing, anti-extraction, stabilization and regional-governance model for hospitals. |

| System entities | ARCH-NHSA; ARCH-PSHCO; ARCH-RHA; ARCH-HFASB; ARCH-THDO; ARCH-NHETF; ARCH-NHAC; ARCH-CHAO; hospitals; workforce; EMS; communities. |

| Assumptions | ASM-011 continuity constraint; D5A-DEC-06/07; OI-011/020/023/029/031; rural and safety-net functions remain explicit. |

| Data / parameters | care.hospital_budget/service_line; workforce.safety_culture/supply_demand; fiscal.*; cost.event; clinical/EMS/safety records; governance.formula_version. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-HOSP-001–010; TPP-5.1–5.6; IF-013/014/024/025/028; KPP-C5/D1/D2; Gate 4/7/8. |

| Principal risks | Under/overcalibrated budget; service closure; unsafe staffing; readiness erosion; related-party extraction; capital backlog; duplicate payment; rural collapse; transition cash shock. |

| Simulation implication | Model component budgets, payment schedule, actual cost, service/capacity/staffing, variance, corridor state, capital, patient flows, quality/safety, extraction, closures and regional spillovers. |
The hospital public-service model combines hospital global budgets with enforceable public-service hospital charters. A chartered hospital is not paid primarily by multiplying facility-coded encounters by fragmented payer prices. It receives a certified budget for defined obligations, readiness and infrastructure, subject to charter duties, regional need, transparent formulas, periodic payment, component reconciliation, service-line protection and independent oversight. Professional compensation and exceptional pass-throughs remain separately controlled so the model does not hide duplicate payment.
6.4.1 Public-service charter
Table D5A-20. Hospital charter obligations

| Domain | Charter obligation | Trace |

| Access | Deliver covered services without routine facility fees or balance billing; maintain nondiscrimination and accessibility | SR-HOSP-003; SN-01/SN-18/SN-19 |

| Essential services | Maintain protected service lines unless regional review authorizes a controlled change | SR-HOSP-004/007/009 |

| Readiness | Maintain emergency, surge, ICU, trauma-relevant and other certified readiness capabilities | SR-HOSP-010; CP-HOSP-003 |

| Staffing and safety | Meet staffing floors, safety reporting, corrective action and workforce protections | SR-HOSP-005; TPP-5.5 |

| Financial integrity | Accept global-budget reconciliation, related-party limits, anti-extraction controls and audit | SR-HOSP-002/006; TPP-5.2/5.6 |

| Data and transparency | Report budget, service line, staffing, capacity, safety, quality, capital and related-party data | IF-014; SR-HOSP-009 |

| Continuity | Participate in regional transfer, EMS, specialist and transition continuity workflows | IF-012/014/026; SN-05/SN-07 |
6.4.2 Global-budget composition
Table D5A-21. Mutually reconciled hospital budget components

| Component | Purpose | Cost trace | Boundary/control |

| operations | Recurring facility operations required for covered service delivery | CP-HOSP-001/002 | Do not include separately paid clinician compensation, capital, transition or pass-through items without controlled allocation |

| emergency_readiness | Standby capacity, surge, disaster and emergency obligations | CP-HOSP-003 | Formula Registry; readiness is paid even when volume is low |

| essential_service_support | Incremental support for protected regional service lines | CP-HOSP-004/005 | Linked to charter obligations and continuity measurements |

| staffing_safety | Incremental safe-staffing requirement | CP-HOSP-006 | Cannot be treated as discretionary margin reduction |

| capital_replacement | Planned infrastructure and equipment renewal | CP-HOSP-007 | Capital plan, condition, depreciation/useful-life and project evidence |

| teaching_research | Approved education, training and public-interest research functions | CP-HOSP / CP-EDU / CP-RD | Separate allocation and deliverables; OI-011 |

| high_cost_pass_through | Controlled high-cost drugs, devices, blood, implants or exceptional diagnostics | CP-RX / CP-DX | Explicit eligibility and no duplicate claim/global-budget payment; OI-011/031 |

| clinician_compensation | Professional compensation where outside facility operations | CP-CLIN | Separate view pending final employment/payment design; OI-011 |

| transition_stabilization | Temporary corridor payment or recovery during conversion | CP-HOSP-008 / CP-TRN | Time-limited, evidence-based, separately booked and reconciled |
Certified hospital budget  B_h,t = B_operations + B_readiness + B_essential + B_staffing + B_capital + B_teaching/research + B_pass_through + B_transition_stabilization - certified_recoveries
Each term is separately observable. Clinician compensation is added only under the controlled employment/payment allocation and may not also be embedded in operations or claims.
Budget variance  variance_h,t = (actual_eligible_component_cost - certified_component_budget) / certified_component_budget
TPP-5.2 uses absolute variance. Variance alone does not determine fault or recovery; cause, service, quality, safety, volume and extraordinary events are evaluated.
Constrained savings  recognized_savings = max(0, comparator_cost - observed_cost) only if service, staffing, readiness, access, quality and safety constraints pass
A budget cut that closes an essential line, creates unsafe staffing, shifts uncompensated demand, or violates access is a failure/cost transfer, not a recognized offset.
6.4.3 Stabilization corridor
During conversion, a corridor prevents an abrupt budget drop below the level needed for access, staffing, emergency readiness and essential services, while also preventing transition fear from locking in excessive legacy revenue. The corridor is a temporary state and formula, not a permanent entitlement to historical revenue.

| Element | Required control | Status |

| Reference amount | Versioned baseline with cost, volume, service, readiness, staffing, capital and related-party adjustments | Design specified; formula OI-029 |

| Floor | Minimum temporary payment consistent with certified essential obligations and safe transition | OI-029 |

| Ceiling | Maximum temporary protection after removing unjustified extraction/duplication and accounting for service need | OI-029 |

| Trigger | Material cash, staffing, service-line or readiness risk supported by evidence | OI-029 |

| Duration/exit | Time limit, milestones, recalibration, recovery/clawback and appeal | OI-029 |

| Transparency | Formula/version, evidence, payment and service effects published subject to protected data | SR-HOSP-009/010 |
6.4.4 Protected service lines and closure control
Table D5A-22. Source-identified protected service lines

| Service line | Protection rationale/operational meaning |

| Emergency department | Emergency screening, stabilization and regional access |

| Obstetrics | Regionally essential maternal delivery and emergency capacity |

| Psychiatric beds | Acute behavioral-health and crisis capacity |

| Trauma-relevant services | Certified trauma/stabilization capability appropriate to region |

| ICU | Critical-care readiness and surge |

| Dialysis access | Where regionally essential; coordinate chronic and emergency continuity |

| Rural inpatient beds | Low-volume essential inpatient/readiness function |

| Stroke/cardiac pathways | Time-critical stabilization and transfer |

| Pediatric essential services | Regionally necessary pediatric emergency/inpatient capability |

| Safety-net clinics | Hospital-linked access serving safety-net populations |
A hospital proposing closure or material degradation submits service, workforce, quality, capital, demand, transfer, travel-time, equity, fiscal and alternative-capacity evidence to the RHA/NHSA process.
The region tests whether remaining hospitals, units, EMS, specialists and transport can safely absorb the service. Paper capacity is not treated as available without staffed and reachable capability.
Patients, workforce, local government, tribal partners and affected communities receive notice and a usable participation/review path.
The decision may deny closure, require mitigation, authorize staged change, fund stabilization/conversion, or approve closure after replacement capacity and continuity conditions are met.
Quarterly public service-line status and corrective milestones are required; emergency orders and appeals remain available.

PAYMENT-RESOURCE SEPARATION  THDO disbursement executes a certified obligation; it does not define hospital resource cost. Transfers among Treasury, trusts and hospitals are financing flows. Hospital operations, capital, readiness, clinician services, transition support and recoveries remain distinct CP/ledger views.

6.5 Drug, Pharmacy, Device, and Diagnostic Concept
CONTROLLED PMC MANUFACTURING OBLIGATION  By the end of PH-P8, the Public Medicines Corporation must maintain qualified public manufacturing capability and routine production for all 200 product families identified as PF-001 through PF-200. A purchasing contract, private inventory, or unused emergency option does not count. Production may occur in a PMC-owned facility or a PMC-controlled public manufacturing affiliate operating under the same quality, transparency, and continuity duties.
The portfolio is intentionally narrower than the complete national formulary. National purchasing remains the primary price and access mechanism for thousands of products. PMC manufacturing is reserved for products whose loss, price, concentrated production, fragile platform, population burden, equity importance, maternal-child role, or preparedness function justifies permanent public production capacity.
A product-family ID is not an NDC. It identifies a clinically coherent active ingredient, combination, biologic, solution family, or antidote platform and the dosage forms that must remain available. Strengths, package sizes, devices, and presentations become controlled subordinate SKUs. This prevents the framework from claiming 200 products by counting trivial package variations.
Table 6.5-1. PMC controlled portfolio by clinical domain

| Clinical domain | Families | Why public manufacturing is used |

| Critical care, emergency medicine, anesthesia, and surgery | 30 | Time-critical sterile products cannot wait for price signals or slow capacity restoration. |

| Anti-infectives | 35 | Antimicrobial availability is a safety, stewardship, and preparedness dependency. |

| Cardiovascular, renal-circulatory, and hematology | 30 | High-volume chronic treatment and emergency anticoagulation/thrombolysis require continuous access. |

| Endocrine, metabolic, electrolyte, and fluid support | 25 | Insulin, thyroid replacement, electrolytes, and IV fluids are foundational and often have fragile production platforms. |

| Neurology, psychiatry, substance-use treatment, and pain | 25 | Interrupted therapy can cause seizure, withdrawal, relapse, destabilization, or uncontrolled pain. |

| Respiratory, allergy, and gastrointestinal care | 20 | High-volume chronic and acute products require affordable devices, liquids, and injectables. |

| Maternal, reproductive, neonatal, and pediatric care | 15 | Low-volume or politically vulnerable markets must not determine whether time-sensitive care is available. |

| Oncology, transplant, and immune support | 10 | Shortages can force non-equivalent regimens or delay curative treatment. |

| Antidotes and national medical countermeasures | 10 | Commercial demand is too episodic to guarantee national preparedness capacity. |
Table 6.5-2. What counts toward SR-DRUG-006

| Counts | Does not count |

| Released conforming lots from a qualified PMC-owned or PMC-controlled public line | A framework agreement with no exercised production |

| Current API source, validated process, quality-release record, and routine output | Private market inventory that PMC cannot direct |

| Required dosage-form group and controlled subordinate SKU schedule | Counting each strength, package, or NDC as a separate family |

| Continuity stock and surge plan backed by exercised manufacturing capacity | A stockpile with no replenishment capability |
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Fragmented purchasing, PBM incentives, concentrated production, and shortage-prone manufacturing separate medicine availability from public need; purchasing, claims, formulary, and production must be coordinated. Why this structure: Each concept joins institutions, workflows, rights, performance measures, risks, and simulation behavior in one operational explanation. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes drug, pharmacy, device, and diagnostic concept explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Specify the integrated public architecture for formulary/access governance, national purchasing, real-time pharmacy claims, utilization/safety, essential-product manufacturing, inventory/shortage response, devices, supplies, laboratories, diagnostics and innovation delinkage. |

| System entities | ARCH-AMDDT; ARCH-NDPA; ARCH-PCU; ARCH-PMC; ARCH-NFTSB; ARCH-MARB; ARCH-DUSO; ARCH-MDSA; ARCH-LDA; ARCH-NBIA/PILO; pharmacies; manufacturers; labs; providers; patients. |

| Assumptions | ASM-001/002 R&D delinkage/public funding; ASM-005 PBM displacement; D5A-DEC-08–12; OI-020/023/030/031. |

| Data / parameters | supply.formulary/drug_inventory/manufacturing/device_diagnostic; claims.pharmacy; clinical.medication/result; innovation.program_license; rights.appeal_case; payment/cost events. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-DRUG-001–010; SR-PAY-009; TPP-3.1–3.6/4.1–4.5; KPP-T2/D5; IF-005/006/017–019/029. |

| Principal risks | Pharmacy outage; shortage; substitution harm; inventory opacity; manufacturing quality failure; capture/formulary denial; R&D underperformance; device/diagnostic overuse; duplicate payment. |

| Simulation implication | Model prescription/claim/fill/adherence, product/formulary/access class, price/contract, inventory/capacity/shortage, substitution/appeal, manufacturing quality, device/lab utilization, diagnostic stewardship and innovation outcomes. |
The medicines and diagnostic architecture replaces fragmented PBM-mediated core purchasing with national drug purchasing, a public pharmacy claims utility, accountable access review and the Public Medicines Corporation as the permanent public manufacturing arm for PF-001 through PF-200. Devices, supplies, laboratories and diagnostics share the same discipline: transparent standards, procurement, inventory/capacity visibility, interoperability, stewardship, safety and cost boundaries. Innovation financing is modeled separately from product price.

6.5.2 Pharmacy claim and access lifecycle
Table D5A-26. Pharmacy transaction states

| State | Meaning | Control/output |

| prescription.received | Prescriber, patient, product, dose, indication where required, allergies and continuity flag are available | Resolve identity and current medication/formulary versions |

| claim.adjudicating | PCU applies eligibility, formulary, quantity, safety, substitution and patient-price rules | Real-time target; no PBM spread/pricing for core benefit |

| preferred_or_exception | Preferred fill, clinically reviewed substitution, access exception or safety restriction is selected | Record accountable reviewer and appeal path |

| inventory.reserved | Dispensing site has stock or alternate source is located | Near-real-time critical-SKU visibility; shortage rules apply |

| dispensed | Product, lot/source where required, quantity, price, patient charge and pharmacist action are recorded | Write medication record; create payment obligation |

| continuity.monitored | Refill, adherence, interruption, adverse event and substitution outcome are monitored | Critical regimens trigger no-interruption response |

| closed_or_escalated | Routine fill closes or access/safety/shortage appeal escalates | MARB/NHAC review; emergency bridge where required |
Net unit price  net_unit_price_d,t = gross_contract_price - rebates/credits/recoveries + distribution/dispensing components allocated per contract
The model records gross and net terms, quantities, timing and responsible payer. Spread, undisclosed rebate retention and PBM-like margin cannot be hidden inside the core public benefit.
Shortage exposure  TPP-3.5 = critical products below controlled availability threshold / products on critical list
The critical list and availability threshold are versioned under OI-030. Stock, expected demand, inbound supply, source reliability and therapeutic alternatives inform the state.
Therapeutic substitution  TPP-3.6 = eligible nonpreferred prescriptions converted to preferred equivalent therapy without successful adverse appeal / eligible nonpreferred prescriptions
Eligibility excludes contraindication, allergy, prior failure, instability and other controlled clinical exceptions. A successful adverse appeal reverses the conversion outcome.
6.5.3 Medication continuity
During transition, an established medication filled under a legacy plan is bridged unless a clinically reviewed equivalent substitution or safety restriction applies. Coverage/formulary migration does not itself constitute a clinical reason to interrupt therapy. Critical chronic classes receive heightened detection, emergency-fill, alternate-source and appeal behavior.
Table D5A-27. Source-identified no-interruption medication classes

| Class | Continuity concern |

| Insulin | Avoid interruption and uncontrolled glycemic risk |

| Anticoagulants | Avoid thrombotic/bleeding risk from unreviewed interruption or substitution |

| Antiepileptics | Avoid seizure destabilization |

| Psychiatric medicines | Avoid destabilization/withdrawal; preserve sensitive-record controls |

| Transplant-related medicines | Avoid graft-threatening interruption |

| Dialysis-related medicines | Coordinate with dialysis continuity and regionally essential access |
CONTINUITY INVARIANT  A formulary, payer, pharmacy-rail, data-migration or contract transition may not silently terminate an active critical regimen. The system must produce a fill, clinically reviewed substitution, documented safety restriction, or urgent access case with an accountable owner and provisional bridge.
6.5.4 Product, supply and shortage state model
Table D5A-28. Drug/device/diagnostic product states

| State | Meaning | Authority/output |

| candidate | Product is proposed for formulary, purchasing, public production or device/diagnostic catalog | Evidence, clinical role, demand, price, supply and alternatives |

| evaluated | Clinical value, safety, comparative evidence and operational requirements are reviewed | NFTSB/MDSA/LDA and applicable independent review |

| contracted_or_produced | National contract, cost-plus/nonprofit arrangement, PMC production or approved supplier exists | Access, price, quality, source and license terms |

| available | Inventory/capacity and claims/order pathway are active | Critical-source and visibility targets monitored |

| shortage | Supply falls below controlled threshold or reliable fulfillment is threatened | Allocation, substitution, emergency purchase, alternate source and PMC response |

| restricted_or_recalled | Safety, quality, efficacy or legal issue limits use | Notice, clinical substitution, patient continuity and corrective action |

| retired | Product/version exits standard use | Migration, residual patient need, records and contract closure |
National purchasing uses aggregated demand and public access terms but retains supplier, product, quality, geography and timing detail needed for resilience.
Critical products require dual-source strategy, secure API/source coverage, inventory visibility and a response plan. A contract name is not equivalent to physically available, quality-released supply.
PMC shall place all 200 controlled families in routine production through PMC-owned facilities or PMC-controlled public manufacturing affiliates; separate dual-source partners provide redundancy but do not replace the public-production obligation. Quality release, recall, source, lot and capacity are visible; public ownership does not relax quality controls.
Shortage response may allocate supply, authorize therapeutic substitution, buy emergently, invoke alternate contracts, expand PMC/contract production, coordinate imports under law, or prioritize clinically—but every access decision is reviewable.
Devices and diagnostics maintain catalog, standards, price, inventory/capacity, maintenance/quality, interoperability and patient-result linkage; high-cost pass-through remains separately reconciled under OI-031.
6.5.5 Laboratory, device and diagnostic stewardship

| Domain | Required behavior | Safety/cost control |

| Laboratory orders/results | Standard code/specimen/result/reference range; source provenance; timely interoperable result and abnormal closure | Avoid duplicate testing; do not suppress clinically necessary testing to meet cost targets |

| Imaging/diagnostics | Order/indication, capability/site, acquisition, interpretation, result and follow-up | Diagnostic-first pathways and appropriateness; emergency access protected |

| Devices/DME | Catalog, eligibility, standard, fit, fulfillment, maintenance/replacement and outcome | National purchasing with patient-specific exception; prevent low-quality lowest-price substitution |

| Supplies | SKU/source/stock/use/criticality and facility/unit allocation | Near-real-time visibility for critical items; no double booking with global budgets |

| AI diagnostic assistance | Registered model/use, validation, accountable clinician, audit, override and drift monitoring | No final high-stakes diagnosis; suspension and human/manual fallback |
6.5.6 Innovation-price separation
NBIA and the public-interest licensing functions finance and govern innovation through public R&D portfolios, milestones, prizes/rewards, subscriptions, comparative evidence and licensing covenants. Product purchasing pays for efficient production, supply, quality, distribution and allowed return under the applicable instrument; it is not presumed to repay an opaque monopoly-financed R&D portfolio.

| Instrument | Model function | Required outputs |

| Public R&D grant/contract | Fund priority scientific/clinical work | cost, milestones, probability/time to success, evidence and rights |

| Milestone/prize/reward | Pay for controlled technical or health achievement | eligibility, measured value, payment, post-market reconciliation |

| Subscription | Purchase access/readiness/value over time | covered population/use, availability, quality and total payment |

| Public-interest license | Attach access, price, supply, transparency and march-in/alternative rights to public funding | license version, funded contribution, compliance and remedy |

| National procurement | Purchase mature product supply | net unit price, volume, quality, access, source and shortage terms |

| SCN-PANDEMIC | Surge purchasing/production, allocation, Type D/hospital/public-health coordination | demand, capacity, stockout, price, readiness and health effects |

| Innovation underperformance | Rebalance portfolio/instruments without shifting recovery automatically to product price | portfolio cost, failures, time to adoption, health/value outcomes |

6.6 Workforce and Education Concept
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Coverage and facilities cannot deliver care without trained people; compensation, scope, education, geography, workload, and transition labor must be planned as one capacity system. Why this structure: Each concept joins institutions, workflows, rights, performance measures, risks, and simulation behavior in one operational explanation. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes workforce and education concept explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the workforce control system that estimates safe role-region need, supplies and retains qualified workers, allocates education, governs scope and compensation, protects wellbeing, and transitions displaced administrative workers. |

| System entities | ARCH-AHWCS; ARCH-NHWB; ARCH-NPCB; ARCH-NCSWB; ARCH-NHWECA; ARCH-RS-CORPS; ARCH-HATC; ARCH-RHA; employers; training programs; workers; unions/professional bodies. |

| Assumptions | ASM-007 capacity-before-price; ASM-008 specialist constraint; ASM-009 human-accountable AI; D5B-DEC-01–03; OI-023/024/033/034. |

| Data / parameters | workforce.supply_demand; workforce.training; workforce.transition; workforce.safety_culture; registry.provider; care.specialty_capacity; governance.formula_version/requirement_result. |

| Requirements / performance | PR-WF-001–010; SR-HOSP-005; KPP-W1/CULT1; TPP-5.5/8.1–8.6; IF-009/014/015/023/027/028/032. |

| Principal risks | Vacancy and pipeline lag; unsafe scope expansion; burnout/turnover; rural maldistribution; training bottleneck; compensation gaming; service-obligation inequity; worker-transition failure. |

| Simulation implication | Model role-specialty-region FTE need/supply, hours, productivity subject to safety, vacancies, pipeline cohorts/lags/attrition, compensation/retention, scope, rural placement, service obligations, burnout, transition placement and cost. |
The framework treats workforce as a hard system constraint. Coverage, unit deployment, specialist routing, hospital readiness, expanded benefits, public health, diagnostics, records and appeals operate only to the extent that qualified people are available with safe schedules, appropriate scope, usable tools and accountable support. Workforce plans therefore translate demand into function-specific need, then test whether active supply, training pipelines, retention measures, scope rules and cross-region capacity can satisfy that need without shifting harm to workers or patients.
6.6.1 Workforce governance and decision rights
Table D5B-5. Workforce architecture

| Entity | Full name | Primary operating contract | Hard boundary |

| ARCH-AHWCS | Administration for Health Workforce, Compensation, and Scope | Integrates planning, compensation, scope, education and workforce-policy execution | Cannot self-verify gates or suppress safety/workload evidence |

| ARCH-NHWB | National Health Workforce Board | Maintains role-region demand/supply, vacancy, retention, staffing and bottleneck plans | Need is safe staffed capacity, not payroll headcount alone |

| ARCH-NPCB | National Physician Compensation Board | Sets transparent compensation bands, specialist-backplane and rural/priority premiums | Compensation cannot reward unsafe volume, denial, under-referral or geographic abandonment |

| ARCH-NCSWB | National Clinical Scope and Workforce Board | Sets national scope floors, team boundaries, competency, escalation and supervision rules | Scope expansion requires training and accountable clinical governance |

| ARCH-NHWECA | National Health Workforce Education and Capacity Authority | Funds slots, scholarships, fellowships, hubs, bottleneck programs and continuing education | Allocation follows measured need and completion/service evidence |

| ARCH-RS-CORPS | Rural Service Corps | Supports rural placement, housing, premiums, rotations, retention and local pipeline formation | Placement does not substitute for safe facilities, transport, supervision or family support |

| ARCH-HATC | Health Administration Transition Corps | Retrains and redeploys eligible displaced payer/PBM/billing/revenue-cycle workers | Tracks offer, income bridge, training, placement, retention and appeal |
SEPARATION OF DUTIES  AHWCS and its boards plan and operate workforce policy; NHAC protects rights and safety; NHASB independently verifies gate evidence and formula performance; CHAO audits for Congress; regional administrators execute within national floors. No workforce operator may grade its own maturity gate.
6.6.2 Need, supply and bottleneck model
Required safe FTE  required_FTE[r,k,t] = service_demand[r,k,t] x minutes_per_service[k] / productive_safe_minutes_per_FTE[r,k,t] + readiness_FTE[r,k,t]
Productive safe minutes exclude leave, education, supervision, administrative duty, unavailable time and workload above the safety standard. Readiness FTE preserves emergency, rural and low-volume essential functions that encounter volume alone would understate.
Effective supply  effective_FTE = licensed_FTE x participation_share x schedule_availability x competency_match x retention_probability
Headcount is not capacity. Each factor is bounded, time-indexed and role/region specific; tele/cross-region capacity is separately allocated so it is not counted twice.
Vacancy rate  vacancy_rate[r,k,t] = max(required_FTE - effective_FTE, 0) / required_FTE
TPP-8.1 requires a controlled critical-role set and need denominator under OI-033. An unfilled authorized position is an administrative vacancy; the performance measure is unmet required safe FTE.
Specialist Bottleneck Index  SBI[t] = weighted_aggregate(queue_delay, unmet_need, urgency_miss, geographic_scarcity, vacancy, referral_growth)
Weights, normalization, specialty/function inclusion and baseline remain OI-033. The index cannot improve by suppressing referrals or shifting work to an unmeasured queue.
Table D5B-6. Workforce planning states

| State | Meaning | Required output/control |

| need.estimated | Demand, safe workload, coverage, hours, geography and service standard produce required FTE | Versioned method and uncertainty; stratified need |

| supply.active | Credentialed worker is available in a role, region, modality and schedule | Exclude leave, vacancy, unavailable time and unsafe excess overtime |

| gap.identified | Required FTE exceeds effective supply or bottleneck performance fails | Trigger compensation, scope, pipeline, routing or retention intervention |

| intervention.active | A funded recruitment, education, scope, retention, tele/cross-region or workflow action is operating | Owner, budget, milestones, equity and safety constraints |

| pipeline.training | Learner occupies a funded slot and progresses through accredited milestones | Completion probability, time lag and attrition remain explicit |

| service.obligation | Publicly funded graduate is serving an approved obligation | Location/function, duration, waiver, hardship and fulfillment state |

| retained_or_exited | Worker remains, changes role/region, retires, leaves or burns out | Exit reason and replacement/vacancy effect update the model |
6.6.3 Education and bottleneck allocation
Training allocation follows bottleneck functions remaining after safe unit-network absorption and workflow redesign. It does not equate every queue with a need for a physician specialist, and it does not assume that expanding advanced roles can replace physicians, nurses, therapists, technicians or diagnostic professionals without competency and team capacity. Each annual portfolio states the function, region, role mix, slot type, training duration, faculty/facility constraint, expected completion, service obligation, attrition and time-to-capacity.
Table D5B-7. Priority bottleneck functions

| Function group | Need represented | Allocation guardrail |

| Primary and complex longitudinal care | Continuity, multimorbidity, frailty, disability, family context and goals of care | Do not infer low need from unit-network substitution |

| Psychiatry and child/adolescent psychiatry | First contact, consultation, crisis, inpatient/outpatient continuity | Coordinate with BH crisis and specialty ledgers |

| Neurology, geriatrics, rheumatology, endocrinology, nephrology | High unmet-need and chronic/complex diagnostic functions | Allocate by function, geography and queue evidence |

| Cardiology, gastroenterology, dermatology, ophthalmology | Consultation, diagnostic-first, procedural planning and follow-up | Separate urgent/e-consult/procedure/follow-up capacity |

| Oncology/hematology | Time-sensitive diagnosis, systemic therapy, longitudinal treatment | Continuity and urgent pathways dominate throughput targets |

| Radiology, pathology and laboratory professions | Diagnostic acquisition, interpretation, quality and result closure | Diagnostic workforce is a hard dependency for units and specialty pathways |

| Behavioral health and SUD workforce | Therapy, peer, crisis, medication and recovery services | Privacy, language, cultural and rural capability included |

| Advanced clinical workforce | Nursing, advanced practice, pharmacy, therapy, dental, EMS and allied health functions | Scope expansion is competency- and team-governed |
Expected new capacity  pipeline_capacity[r,k,t] = sum_cohorts(slots x completion_probability x participation_share x service_location_match) at graduation/credential lag
A funded slot affects capacity only after the relevant time lag and successful completion/credentialing. Faculty, rotation, supervision and clinical-site capacity limit slot expansion.
6.6.4 Compensation, scope and service obligation
Table D5B-8. Workforce operating controls

| Control | Operating rule | Trace |

| Safe staffing | Staffed hours and workload must meet role/setting safety standards; temporary coverage is visible | TPP-5.5/8.1; KPP-CULT1 |

| Fair compensation | National bands permit transparent specialty, scarcity, rural, call, complexity and leadership adjustments | ARCH-NPCB; CP-CLIN |

| Scope floors | Regions implement at least the national floor after training/credentialing; upward variation preserves evidence and safety | TPP-8.5; TPP-TRIB1/REG1 |

| Wellbeing | Burnout, overtime, turnover, moral injury, schedule control and safety culture constrain capacity | TPP-8.6; KPP-CULT1 |

| Service obligation | Public support may carry a bounded public-service obligation with hardship, disability, family and due-process rules | TPP-8.4; OI-034 |

| Anti-gaming | Vacancy, productivity and access cannot improve through relabeling, unfilled authorized posts, excessive overtime or suppressed demand | VR-005/012; OI-023 |
NPCB publishes compensation bands and authorized adjustments for scarcity, complexity, rural service, call/readiness, leadership and training. Total compensation and source are visible; hidden productivity incentives are prohibited.
NCSWB publishes minimum scope floors by role and function with training, competency, supervision, escalation, documentation, data-access and liability requirements. Regions may exceed a floor through controlled evidence, not fall below it by inertia.
NHWECA funds scholarships, residencies, fellowships, advanced-role programs, diagnostic workforce, continuing education and training hubs. Public-service obligations specify function/location/duration plus hardship, disability, family, appeal and alternative-service rules.
RS-CORPS packages placement with housing, family/spousal support, supervision, local pipeline, tele-support, transport and retention measures; a signing premium alone is not modeled as durable rural capacity.
HATC records eligible displaced workers, existing skills, income bridge, training offer, completion, placement quality and retention. Placement means paid work or approved training with a verified start—not a referral or application.
6.6.5 Wellbeing, safety culture and anti-gaming
Burnout-constrained capacity  safe_capacity = nominal_capacity x (1 - absence - turnover_loss - unsafe_overtime_penalty - burnout_impairment)
The model does not create productivity by extending unsafe hours. Parameters are empirically calibrated and tested in sensitivity analysis; they are not assumed benefits of public employment.
WORKFORCE INVARIANT  An access, cost, vacancy or productivity result is invalid if it depends on staffing below the controlled floor, uncompensated labor, unsafe overtime, untrained scope, suppressed demand, hidden queue work, or a worsening safety-culture constraint.

6.6.6 Phase, scenario and cost behavior
PH-P1/P2 establish verified workforce registries, governance, education authority and baseline need/supply methods; HATC is active before legacy wind-down.
PH-P4 pilots role mix, unit/specialist/hospital workflows, scope, compensation, training and safety measurement across representative regions.
PH-P5 scales workforce and scope reforms; Gate 3 prevents full expanded-benefit rollout when critical vacancy, LTC assessment/home-care or BH access evidence fails.
PH-P8 tests annual training slots, service-obligation fulfillment, vacancy, bottleneck reduction, scope implementation, burnout and safety culture for maturity.
SCN-WF-SHORT increases vacancies, attrition and pipeline lag; the model activates retention, premiums, scope, training, tele/cross-region support and phase delay while preserving safety constraints.
SCN-RURAL-STRESS couples workforce scarcity to Type C units, EMS, hospitals, pharmacy, weather, housing and compact capacity rather than treating rural supply as an isolated premium response.

6.7 Long-Term Care, Behavioral Health, Dental/Vision/Hearing, EMS, and Public Health Concept
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: A medical benefit limited to acute physician and hospital care shifts unmet need into families, emergency departments, disability, and preventable crisis. Why this structure: Each concept joins institutions, workflows, rights, performance measures, risks, and simulation behavior in one operational explanation. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes long-term care, behavioral health, dental/vision/hearing, ems, and public health concept explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the expanded-benefit operating architecture, common pathway, domain-specific safety/continuity rules, capacity dependencies, public-health interfaces and clinically linked support boundary. |

| System entities | ARCH-NLTCA; ARCH-NBHA; ARCH-NDVHO; ARCH-NEMTA; ARCH-NPHPA; ARCH-RHA; units; hospitals; primary/specialty care; state/tribal/local public-health and service partners. |

| Assumptions | ASM-010 staged expansion; ASM-011 continuity; ASM-014 clinical linkage; D5B-DEC-04/05; OI-010/023/024/035/036. |

| Data / parameters | benefit.long_term_care; benefit.behavioral_health; care.ems_transport; public_health.event; clinical.encounter/result/medication/care_plan; supply.device_diagnostic; rights.appeal_case; workforce.supply_demand. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-LTC-001–003; SR-BH-001–003; SR-DVH-001–002; SR-EMS-001–002; SR-EQ; KPP-D3/D4/T-ED-002/T-ED-004/T-ED-005; TPP-9.1–9.7; IF-011/012/016/017/021–023/027/032. |

| Principal risks | Released unmet demand; unsafe home substitution; caregiver overload; BH crisis delay; sensitive-data breach; DVH/device backlog; EMS underreadiness; public-health fragmentation; rural/tribal inequity. |

| Simulation implication | Model eligibility, latent/released demand, assessment/queue, service plan, workforce/capacity, site/device/transport, setting choice, continuity, safety events, appeal, outcome, equity, public-health shock and cost by domain. |
Expanded benefits are not a single catch-all program. The National Long-Term Care Authority, National Behavioral Health Authority, National Dental, Vision, and Hearing Benefit Office, National EMS and Medical Transport Authority, and National Public Health and Prevention Authority each retain domain-specific clinical and operational responsibility while using the same public coverage, rights, data, payment, workforce, regional-capacity and assurance infrastructure. The common contract is a closed pathway from request through assessment, plan, capacity match, delivery, reassessment and appeal. A missing provider, device, transport option or caregiver is a capacity failure to be managed and reported—not an invisible benefit denial.

6.7.2 Long-term care and caregiver support
Table D5B-13. LTC decision controls

| Control | Operating rule | Trace |

| Functional assessment | Measures activities, cognition, behavior, medical complexity, supervision, environment and informal support | TPP-9.1; OI-035 |

| Beneficiary preference | Home/community/institutional preference is recorded and revisited | SR-IF-006; SN-05/14 |

| Safe-home test | Authorized hours, workforce, housing, equipment, transport, caregiver capacity/consent and contingency can meet need | OI-036; CP-LTC |

| Home-first | Select home/community when eligible, preferred and safe | TPP-9.2; never a forced cost substitution |

| Institutional entitlement | Institutional care remains available when clinically/functionally required or preferred under the benefit rule | OI-010/036; appealable |

| Caregiver protection | Training, respite, compensation/support and refusal/availability are explicit | CP-LTC-007; no assumed unpaid capacity |

| Reduction control | No active-service reduction without notice, reassessment, evidence, transition and appeal | SR-LTC-003; Layer 4 |
LTC service-plan capacity  authorized_home_hours = assessed_need_hours - safe_informal_capacity, bounded below by 0 and by beneficiary preference/safety
Safe informal capacity is counted only with informed caregiver consent, availability and sustainability. It cannot be imputed from household presence, and the beneficiary retains institutional/home-community rights under the controlled benefit rule.
Home-first placement  TPP-9.2 = eligible beneficiaries choosing and safely receiving home/community service / eligible beneficiaries with completed setting decision
Eligibility, choice, safe-service sufficiency, observation window and transfer cases remain controlled under OI-036. A person placed home without adequate hours does not count as success.
6.7.3 Behavioral health and substance-use care
A first-contact front door offers self-referral, primary/unit referral, digital/telephone access and crisis access without requiring a completed specialist packet for urgent stabilization.
Noncrisis demand enters a stepped pathway spanning brief intervention, therapy, peer/recovery support, medication, psychiatry e-consult/tele/in-person services and higher levels of care. Step changes are clinical decisions with explanation and appeal where adverse.
Crisis requests receive a statutory regional response standard, mobile/telephone/on-site capability, EMS/unit/hospital routing and post-crisis follow-up. Administrative or bed-capacity delay does not reclassify urgency.
Behavioral health and SUD records use sensitive segmentation and purpose-limited access while preserving emergency access, patient access/correction and lawful continuity. Privacy is not used to fragment care invisibly.
Released unmet demand is explicit in the simulation: coverage expansion may initially increase contacts, therapy episodes, crisis detection and medication treatment before avoided ED/hospital effects mature.
BH first-contact queue  wait_BH = queue_demand / effective_first_contact_capacity, with crisis demand preemptive under the crisis standard
Demand includes newly released unmet need; capacity includes therapists, peers, primary/unit integration, psychiatry and crisis teams without double counting shared staff.
6.7.4 Dental, vision and hearing pathways

| Pathway | Core operating sequence | Capacity and rights control |

| Dental | prevention/screen → basic/urgent appointment → diagnostics → treatment/advanced referral → recall | Basic access clock, urgent escalation, covered catalog, specialist/workforce capacity and appeal |

| Vision | exam → refraction/medical screen → standard device or medical pathway → fitting → repair/replacement | Standard device target; clinical exception; ophthalmology route for disease/red flags |

| Hearing | screen/exam → diagnostic confirmation → standard device/other treatment → fitting/training → follow-up/repair | Device inventory, audiology/ENT capacity, communication access and exception review |

| Device procurement | catalog/standard → eligibility → order → fulfillment → fit/acceptance → maintenance | National purchasing cannot force an unsafe/inappropriate lowest-price substitute |
6.7.5 EMS, transport and escalation
EMS is modeled as a readiness service and an event service. Regional readiness includes staffed units, dispatch, clinical oversight, geographic/time coverage, interoperable communication, vehicle/equipment state, hospital/unit interfaces, mutual aid, weather/disaster posture and air/ground/non-emergency transport. Treat-and-release or alternate-destination pathways are permitted only through validated protocols, accountable clinicians, patient preference and closed handoff; they are not transport-denial mechanisms.
EMS readiness compliance  TPP-9.7 = regions meeting every controlled readiness component / EMS regions
The denominator and required components include rural/weather and surge capability. A region does not pass by averaging a failed critical component with strong urban performance.

| Event state | Required behavior | Primary interface |

| call/alert | location, access needs, symptoms, acuity and hazards captured | dispatch/identity |

| triage/dispatch | resource and urgency selected with clinical oversight | NEMTA operations |

| response/stabilization | scene care, reassessment and destination/alternate pathway | IF-011 |

| transport/handoff | ETA, capacity request, care record and acceptance | IF-012 |

| nontransport closure | patient preference, capacity, instructions, follow-up owner and safety review | clinical.longitudinal_record |

| readiness recovery | unit back in service, coverage gap closed, mutual aid reconciled | public.metric_release |
6.7.6 Public health, prevention and clinically linked supports
NPHPA maintains national standards, surveillance interoperability, prevention programs and surge coordination; state, local and tribal public-health authorities retain lawful roles and governed data/command interfaces.
Type D and other units provide vaccination, screening, respiratory surge, STI/reproductive services, addiction linkage, wound care, heat/smoke/climate response and outreach within clinical/public-health protocols.
Surveillance signals produce a versioned public-health event with jurisdiction, condition, severity, evidence, intervention, capacity request, privacy rule and closure state. Aggregate surveillance is separated from an identified care record unless law and purpose authorize linkage.
Clinically linked nutrition, home modification, heat/cooling or similar supports enter an individual care plan only when medical need, eligibility, duration, responsible owner and outcome are explicit. General housing, food and income policy remain outside the core cost boundary absent a controlled scope change.
Prevention savings are recognized only with an evidence-based time horizon, attribution rule and offset ledger; program spending and downstream health effects remain separately visible.

6.8 Information Mesh and AI Concept
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Interoperability and AI can reduce friction but can also scale error, bias, and surveillance; the information mesh must preserve provenance, human authority, and offline continuity. Why this structure: Each concept joins institutions, workflows, rights, performance measures, risks, and simulation behavior in one operational explanation. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes information mesh and ai concept explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Specify the federated information infrastructure, authoritative-source and event contracts, patient data rights, interoperability, cyber/offline continuity, and lifecycle governance for human-accountable AI. |

| System entities | ARCH-AHIRC; ARCH-NHRA; ARCH-NHIS; ARCH-NMPI; ARCH-NLLHR; ARCH-NRLS; ARCH-NCDSO; ARCH-NAIG; ARCH-PACP; ARCH-CIRBAS; ARCH-HCCA; ARCH-AICIO; NHAC/HRPO/PRTO; all operating nodes. |

| Assumptions | ASM-009 human-accountable AI; ASM-012 federated mesh; D5B-DEC-06–08; D4 data-rights rules; OI-020–024/037. |

| Data / parameters | All D4 dataset contracts, especially registry.*, clinical.*, claims/payment.*, rights.*, governance.*, public.metric_release, ai.model_decision and cyber.continuity_event. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-DATA-001–012; SR-AI-001–010; TPP-10.1–10.6/11.1–11.6; IF-016–020/023/026/030–032. |

| Principal risks | Identity mismatch; stale/incomplete record; privacy breach; sensitive-data overexposure; vendor lock-in; cyber outage; unsafe AI; equity drift; unauditable automation; public-data suppression. |

| Simulation implication | Model node/registry availability, event latency/completeness, matching/error/correction, access/segmentation, API conformance, outage/failover/reconciliation, vulnerability, AI lifecycle/decisions/drift/override, vendor exit and cost. |
The National Health Assurance Information Mesh is a federated public infrastructure, not a single uncontrolled database and not a collection of opaque vendor portals. It connects authoritative registries, source clinical systems, event streams, shared data products, rules-as-code, audit logs and governed analytics through common identity, provenance, access, correction, segmentation, cybersecurity and conformance contracts. The mesh makes accountable action possible while preserving the distinction between a source record, an assembled longitudinal view, an operational state, an oversight case and a public aggregate.
6.8.1 Ten information layers

| Layer | Name | Primary stewards | Content | Boundary |

| 1 | Identity | NHIS/NMPI/CIRBAS | Person/provider/facility keys, credentials, roles and matching evidence | Separate health identity; mismatch queue; least privilege |

| 2 | Clinical record | NHRA/NLLHR/NRLS | Federated encounters, results, medication, care plans, provenance and locator | Source record remains attributable; longitudinal view is governed |

| 3 | Coverage and claims | NEEA/NCCA/THDO/PCU | Eligibility, claim, obligation, disbursement and remittance events | Financial and clinical states remain linked but not conflated |

| 4 | Rules-as-code | DNHA/NHASB/NHAC | Benefit, payment, routing, access, appeal and formula versions | Human-readable authority, test cases, notice, rollback and review |

| 5 | Drug/device/supply ledger | AMDDT authorities | Formulary, price, inventory, quality, shortage, substitution and device/diagnostic status | Product provenance and critical-availability state |

| 6 | Hospital budget ledger | NHSA/HFASB/THDO | Operating, readiness, service-line, capital, variance and payment states | Distinct cost components and audited reconciliation |

| 7 | Workforce registry | NHWB/NHWECA/NCSWB | Credential, FTE, availability, vacancy, training, obligation, scope and safety | Purpose-limited access; workforce surveillance controls |

| 8 | Quality, safety and appeals | NHAC/NPSMIB/PROO | Performance, incidents, injury, complaints, decisions, relief, remedy and correction | Sensitive case segmentation; independent oversight |

| 9 | Analytics and research | SRAE/NBIA/NHASB | Governed datasets, queries, evidence, evaluation and simulation products | Minimum necessary, disclosure review and reproducibility |

| 10 | Public transparency | PRTO/NHASB/CHAO | Approved metrics, denominators, equity strata, revisions and audit history | Privacy suppression cannot become performance suppression |
6.8.2 Federated records, authority and provenance
NHIS/NMPI resolve a health identity and mismatch state separate from Social Security number use. Provider/facility and clinician-role registries identify who may act, in what role and at what site.
The source node remains authoritative for its created observation or order unless a lawful correction/supersession occurs. NLLHR assembles a governed longitudinal view through NRLS and does not erase source provenance.
Every material event carries subject/object key, source, creator/authority, event and effective time, schema/version, purpose/access class, provenance, correction/supersession link, quality flags and retention/disposition state.
Rules-as-code must remain paired with human-readable law/policy, version, owner, evidence, tests, notice, effective period, appeal treatment, emergency correction and rollback. Code cannot become the unpublished rule.
Operational and public data products declare denominator, exclusions, transformations, equity strata, suppression and revision history. A target value is never substituted for a measured observation.
Record completeness  completeness = required valid elements present and reconciled within target / eligible records or events
The denominator, required elements, lateness and reconciliation window are metric specific. Duplicate contradictory elements do not count as complete until provenance and current-state rules resolve them.
Table D5B-17. Patient data-rights workflow

| Right/control | Operational behavior | Evidence |

| Access | PACP provides an accessible longitudinal view, source/provenance and export within statutory standards | access event, fulfillment time, format and failure reason |

| Disclosure accounting | Patient can see who accessed which segment, purpose, authority, time and break-glass use | rights.access_event and audit result |

| Correction | Patient submits evidence; source and assembled views show pending, accepted, denied, superseded and downstream notice states | rights.correction_case; TPP-10.5 |

| Consent/segmentation | Where consent or sensitive-segment law applies, scope, purpose, recipient, duration, revocation and redisclosure are enforceable | IF-017; OI-022 |

| Sensitive records | BH/SUD, reproductive, HIV/STI, genetic, minor/adolescent and tribal-governed data use controlled segmentation and emergency rules | SR-DATA-012; access audit |

| Human assistance/remedy | Portal failure or disagreement routes to accessible support, HRPO/NHAC review and enforceable correction/remedy | IF-021/022; TPP-USE2 |
6.8.3 Interoperability and conformance
NCDSO publishes semantic, clinical, laboratory, pharmacy, imaging, device, workforce, payment, rights and event profiles. NAIG runs registration, certification, test harnesses, production monitoring, version compatibility and nonconformance remediation. Exact standards remain OI-020, but the business contract is fixed: a receiving system must preserve meaning, identity, time, provenance, access restrictions, correction state and accountable failure handling.

| Conformance state | Meaning | Permitted action |

| registered | Node/endpoint, owner, capability, version and security posture declared | Test only |

| tested | Required positive, negative, error, privacy, performance and offline cases pass | Controlled pilot |

| certified | Profile/version authorized for defined production use | Operate and monitor |

| degraded | Latency, completeness, security or semantic defect exceeds warning threshold | Restrict, alert, remediate, preserve fallback |

| nonconformant | Material requirement fails | Suspend affected exchange; manual/alternate path; corrective plan |

| retired | Endpoint/version exits after migration | Preserve records, replay and vendor-exit obligations |
6.8.4 Cybersecurity, resilience and offline continuity
HCCA maintains identity/access, segmentation, encryption/key management, logging, vulnerability/remediation, supply-chain, backup, failover, recovery and incident-command standards for critical nodes.
Critical functions are mapped to recovery-time/recovery-point objectives, dependency graphs and tested degraded modes. Uptime is necessary but not sufficient; a reachable system with unsafe or stale data is degraded.
Essential care, emergency routing, medication access, minimal record lookup, claims intake and mandatory payment retain offline/manual mechanisms with bounded authorization, duplicate controls and reconciliation after recovery.
Break-glass access is purpose-, role-, time- and scope-bounded; it creates immediate patient-visible/auditable events and post-use review, not a general bypass.
Vendor exit, escrow, portable schemas, model/data artifacts and replacement drills are funded so a failed vendor cannot hold clinical, payment or rights functions hostage.
Continuity success  TPP-11.2 = essential-function drills meeting service, safety, reconciliation and recovery criteria / required drills
A drill fails if the fallback technically starts but cannot deliver safe care/payment, loses required events, violates segmentation, or cannot reconcile afterward.
6.8.5 AI use classes and lifecycle
Table D5B-18. AI use-class controls

| Class | Name | Examples | Required boundary |

| 0 | Administrative support | Formatting, coding assistance, scheduling support, search, summarization | Human remains accountable for released record/action |

| 1 | Low-risk support | Reminders, translation draft, inventory/workflow cues | Validation, monitoring and easy override; no material adverse decision |

| 2 | Clinical decision support | Differential, testing, medication or follow-up suggestions | Qualified clinician validates; source/evidence and uncertainty visible |

| 3 | Routing/priority support | Triage, referral completeness, urgency or queue suggestions | High-stakes log and human review; no final non-referral/non-escalation |

| 4 | High-stakes clinical support | Support affecting diagnosis, treatment, benefit, LTC, emergency or other material outcome | Prospective validation, named human authority, patient review right, intensive monitoring |

| 5 | Prohibited autonomous use | Final denial, non-referral, emergency non-escalation, LTC reduction, termination or high-stakes diagnosis | Not deployable; attempted use is a reportable control failure |
HARD AI RULE  No AI system may serve as final authority for denial of covered care, specialist non-referral, emergency non-escalation, long-term-care reduction, benefit termination, or high-stakes clinical diagnosis. Classifying an autonomous function as low risk does not legalize it.
Table D5B-19. AI model lifecycle

| State | Meaning | Guard/output |

| proposed | Use case, owner, class, intended population and decision influence are declared | No production use |

| validated | Technical, clinical, usability, equity, security and workflow evidence meets class standard | Validation package and known limits registered |

| authorized | AICIO grants version/use/population/site authorization with controls | Registry entry, expiry and monitoring plan active |

| operating | Recommendations and human dispositions are logged | Override, disagreement, appeal, harm and drift monitored |

| restricted | Scope/population/site/function is narrowed after warning | Human/manual fallback and notices active |

| suspended | Safety, equity, security, evidence or audit threshold fails | Model output disabled; affected decisions reviewed |

| retired | Authorization ends or replacement completes | Records, reproducibility, vendor exit and downstream cleanup preserved |
Table D5B-20. Minimum high-stakes AI decision log

| Field group | Required content |

| identity | model_id, version, vendor/developer, owner, use class, authorization |

| context | time, site, role, patient/episode key, input categories, data-quality flags |

| output | recommendation, score/category, uncertainty/limitations, evidence references |

| human action | reviewer, approval/override/exception, reason, final decision, elapsed time |

| rights | patient notice where required, requested review, appeal, provisional relief, outcome |

| monitoring | performance, subgroup deviation, safety event, drift alert, restriction/suspension |
Protected-group deviation  TPP-11.6 = max_g |performance_g - reference_performance| under the approved task/metric
Task, outcome, reference, sample adequacy, uncertainty and action thresholds remain controlled. Aggregate performance cannot offset a subgroup safety failure.
6.8.6 Human review, drift and affected-case replay
A high-stakes recommendation reaches a qualified human with model identity/version, intended use, relevant inputs, uncertainty/limitations and a viable non-AI/manual path.
The reviewer records approval, override or exception and the final decision. Rubber-stamp capture without adequate time, authority or information does not satisfy human accountability.
Patients receive notice and a human-review path when required. Appeal records link the model/version and downstream outcome so reversal and harm can be analyzed.
Monitoring detects performance, calibration, workflow, data, safety, subgroup and security drift. Warning may restrict use; threshold breach suspends the affected scope and activates manual fallback.
Material failure defines an affected-case cohort by version, time, site, population and use. The system replays/reviews cases, corrects decisions/records/payment, notifies affected people where required and verifies closure.

6.9 Transition Protection Concept
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Replacing payment and coverage rails can harm the people it is meant to help unless active treatment, provider liquidity, medications, records, and appeals survive conversion. Why this structure: Each concept joins institutions, workflows, rights, performance measures, risks, and simulation behavior in one operational explanation. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes transition protection concept explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define Layer 3 as an executable continuity, liquidity, stabilization, migration, compact, worker, employer, legal-safe-harbor and phase-gate control system for conversion from legacy arrangements. |

| System entities | ARCH-NHTCA and PCO/PLCCO/HESSO/PDCO/HATC/SRCO/EPTO/LPWO/DMRCO/TRTO/TLSHO/TRPGO; DNHA; THDO; RHAs; states; tribal nations; employers; legacy payers; providers; patients. |

| Assumptions | ASM-010 staged rollout; ASM-011 continuity; ASM-019 transition-cost exclusivity; D5B-DEC-09/10; OI-017/038/039. |

| Data / parameters | clinical.care_plan/medication; coverage/claims/payment.*; workforce.transition; governance.phase_gate/compact_waiver; rights.appeal_case; cyber.continuity_event; cost.event; legacy migration extracts. |

| Requirements / performance | PR-TRN-001–010; SR-IF-014; KPP-T1/T2/W1; TPP-EMP1/TRIB1/2.4/12.1/12.5; IF-003/004/013/021–028. |

| Principal risks | Continuity loss; liquidity failure; unsafe hospital/pharmacy conversion; data mismatch; compact failure; worker/employer harm; legal ambiguity; transition double counting; premature sunset. |

| Simulation implication | Model wave cohorts, readiness, dual-run/bridge, continuity assets, exceptions, complaints, payments/liquidity, stabilization, data match, compacts, employer/worker states, rollback, exit/sunset, incremental cost and failure recovery. |
Layer 3 is commanded by the National Health Transition and Continuity Authority (NHTCA) because a desirable end-state architecture can still fail during conversion. The system may change who pays, how claims are processed, how hospitals are budgeted, how drugs are purchased, how records are exchanged and how workers are deployed, but it may not permit an unmanaged gap. Every wave is therefore a stateful migration with inventoried obligations, readiness evidence, continuity guarantees, protected liquidity, exceptions, complaints, reconciliation, rollback and independently verified exit.
6.9.1 Transition command and accountable offices
Table D5B-23. Layer 3 operating architecture

| Entity | Function | Operating contract | Boundary |

| ARCH-NHTCA | Transition command | Integrated wave plan, continuity state, incident command, gates and stabilization | Time-limited; no-later-than-Year-15 sunset absent affirmative extension |

| ARCH-PCO | Patient continuity | Active treatment, medication, referral, appeal, authorization and care-plan migration | Provisional bridge and accountable case owner |

| ARCH-PLCCO | Provider liquidity | Claims continuity, provisional Treasury payment, reconciliation and complaints | No provider bears public-rail failure without remedy |

| ARCH-HESSO | Hospital/essential service | Stabilization corridor, service-line, staffing and regional continuity | Corridor is temporary, evidenced and reconciled |

| ARCH-PDCO | Pharmacy/drug continuity | Pharmacy onboarding, formulary bridge, emergency fill and medication continuity | Critical regimens receive no-interruption protection |

| ARCH-HATC | Worker transition | Eligibility, income bridge, training, placement and retention | Tracks meaningful placement, not referral alone |

| ARCH-SRCO / ARCH-TRTO | State, regional, tribal and rural | Compacts, direct federal fallback, sovereignty, funding, rural continuity and data governance | State cannot veto federal entitlement or tribal participation |

| ARCH-EPTO | Employer/payroll | Contribution conversion, payroll interfaces and wage-pass-through compliance | Worker premium relief and wage treatment remain separately auditable |

| ARCH-LPWO / ARCH-DMRCO | Legacy wind-down and data | Runout, liabilities, appeals, records, authorizations, cleaning and reconciliation | Legacy duty persists until transfer/closure certification |

| ARCH-TLSHO / ARCH-TRPGO | Legal safe harbor and risk/gates | Bounded transition safe harbors, dispute resolution, risk state and gate packages | No safe harbor waives patient safety, fraud, rights or mandatory payment |
6.9.2 Conversion-wave state model
Table D5B-24. Transition wave states

| State | Meaning | Gate/output |

| baseline.inventory | People, providers, plans, services, authorizations, records, liabilities and dependencies are enumerated | Population/asset reconciliation and unresolved-case queue |

| readiness.verified | Target rails, capacity, rights, cyber/offline, liquidity and fallback pass wave criteria | Independent evidence package; no schedule-only approval |

| dual_run_or_bridge | Legacy and public mechanisms overlap or continuity guarantees substitute safely | Duplicate/conflict ledger and bounded duration |

| wave.converted | Defined population, region, provider or function moves to public operation | Effective time, notices, owner and rollback point |

| stabilizing | Exceptions, complaints, data mismatches, cash flow and service continuity are actively resolved | Daily/weekly thresholds and corrective authority |

| wave.certified | Continuity, payment, records, rights, compacts and financial reconciliation meet exit criteria | Legacy duty can close only for certified scope |

| rolled_back_or_paused | Safety, continuity, capacity, legal, fiscal or cyber threshold fails | Protected return/bridge; root cause and re-entry gate |
Wave failure rate  transition_failure_rate = people_or_obligations with unresolved harmful continuity/payment/record failure / wave exposure
Exposure and harm categories are stratified by asset type and severity. A corrected error remains an event and contributes to recovery-time and remediation outputs; it is not erased.
Net transition cost  C_transition_net = unique transition cost events - recoveries - duplicate reclassifications
Each event has one CP-TRN or other controlled capital/project classification. Recurring operations are transferred out of the transition ledger when enduring; reserves and authorizations are not automatically treated as consumed cost.
6.9.3 Continuity guarantees
Table D5B-25. Protected parties and assets

| Protected party/domain | Guarantee | Primary trace |

| Patient | Active treatment, medication, referral, authorization, appeal and care plan transfer | KPP-T1/T2; PR-TRN-002–004 |

| Provider | Clean-claim continuity, provisional payment, reconciliation and complaint remedy | TPP-2.2/2.4/12.1; PR-TRN-009 |

| Hospital/essential service | Stabilization corridor, safe staffing and protected service lines | TPP-5.4/5.5; CP-TRN-007 |

| Pharmacy | Onboarding, emergency fill, formulary/medication bridge and payment continuity | KPP-T2; CP-TRN-008 |

| Records/data | Complete transfer with provenance, mismatch queues, correction and legacy accessibility | PR-TRN-005; IF-026 |

| Jurisdictions | Compact funding/data/operations or direct federal fallback; tribal sovereignty preserved | PR-TRN-006; TPP-TRIB1 |

| Employer/worker | Payroll conversion, wage pass-through, income bridge, training and placement | TPP-EMP1; KPP-W1 |

| Legal | Safe harbor for compliant conversion plus preserved rights, liability, review and fallback | OI-038/039; TPP-12.5 |
PATIENT CONTINUITY GUARANTEE  A coverage or payer migration cannot silently interrupt active treatment, a critical medication, an accepted referral, an authorization, an appeal or an accountable care plan. The converted state must contain a valid continuation, a clinically reviewed change, a documented safety restriction, or an urgent case with provisional protection and an owner.
PROVIDER CASH-FLOW GUARANTEE  A provider or pharmacy that submits a clean covered obligation is protected from failure of the public transition rail through provisional Treasury payment, complaint/review rights and later reconciliation. Fraud exclusions and duplicate recovery remain controlled and reviewable.
6.9.4 Legacy payer, data and liability wind-down
LPWO inventories enrollment, claims, authorizations, medication history, appeals, contracts, reserves, complaints, over/underpayments, records and unresolved liabilities by plan/function/wave.
DMRCO maps, validates and transfers data with provenance, source/version, completeness, conflicts, sensitive-segment rules and mismatch queues. Missing data activates provisional continuity and manual evidence review.
Legacy and public systems run concurrently only as long as needed for a bounded safe bridge. Duplicate coverage/payment/conflicting authorization events are reconciled through an explicit ledger.
A legacy duty closes only after the receiving authority accepts the record/obligation, exceptions are resolved or transferred, people/providers receive required notice, and independent certification covers that scope.
Records and liability do not disappear at institutional sunset. Continuing retention, audit, appeal, recovery and litigation obligations transfer to named durable custodians.
Data-transfer completeness  legacy_transfer_completeness = required valid migrated objects reconciled / required legacy objects
PR-TRN-005 sets at least 99% by maturity; object classes, validity, duplicate/conflict treatment and unresolved high-risk cases require the wave-specific acceptance protocol.
6.9.5 State, regional, tribal and rural conversion
Compacts allocate administration, data, workforce, facility, public-health, financing-maintenance and transition responsibilities while preserving national floors and federal fallback. Tribal nations retain direct consultation, compact, funding and data-governance pathways; state participation cannot be made a veto over tribal or federally authorized health-assurance functions. A nonparticipating or failing state activates direct federal/RHA administration with continuity funding and a recorded transfer of responsibilities.

| Compact element | Required content | Failure behavior |

| scope/authority | functions, population/geography, national floors, sovereignty and responsible parties | direct federal or tribal-authority path for unperformed federal entitlement function |

| data | sources, access, standards, sensitive/tribal governance, migration and correction | minimum necessary alternate feed/manual reconciliation; no silent patient exclusion |

| workforce/facilities | credential/scope transition, staffing, units, hospitals, EMS, LTC/BH and public health | regional surge/contract/direct capacity and phase pause |

| finance | maintenance contribution, grants, transition booking, audit and remedy | statutory funding/default rule; protect service while dispute proceeds |

| evaluation/sunset | hypothesis/endpoints, milestones, equity, public reporting, correction and expiration | waiver/variation ends or repairs; core rights continue |
6.9.6 Employer, payroll and worker transition
EPTO publishes employer contribution, payroll interface, effective date, legacy premium cessation, worker notice and wage-pass-through requirements by wave.
Worker premium relief, employer contribution and wage pass-through are measured as separate flows. An employer cannot count benefit removal or an unrelated wage change as compliance without the controlled attribution method.
HATC identifies eligible displaced insurance, PBM, billing and revenue-cycle workers before affected wind-down; provides skill assessment, income bridge, approved training/placement options, appeal and retention follow-up.
Training and placement prioritize usable public-system functions—claims/payment, records, navigation, rights, analytics, compliance, procurement and care-support administration—without guaranteeing a specific job or preserving unnecessary administrative work.
SCN-EMP-FAIL applies enforcement, restitution/correction, worker support and public reporting while preserving the broader conversion unless the failure breaches a wave threshold.
6.9.7 Legal safe harbor, complaints and sunset
Transition safe harbors protect good-faith compliance with an approved conversion protocol from conflicting legacy process duties only to the extent specified by statute. They do not waive patient safety, civil rights, privacy, fraud, mandatory payment, labor rights, professional accountability or the duty to preserve records. Patient and provider transition complaints receive accessible intake, urgency, owner, provisional relief, response clock, remedy and escalation to NHAC/Article I review.
SUNSET CONTROL  NHTCA sunsets no later than Year 15 unless Congress affirmatively extends it after independent review. Sunset requires a function-by-function transfer of open cases, records, liabilities, reserves, contracts, litigation, metrics and continuing duties. The calendar cannot extinguish an unresolved right or obligation.
