6.10 Legitimacy and Safety Concept
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: A technically efficient system can still lose legitimacy through hidden rationing, unexplained decisions, safety failures, inaccessible services, or remedies that arrive too late. Why this structure: Each concept joins institutions, workflows, rights, performance measures, risks, and simulation behavior in one operational explanation. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes legitimacy and safety concept explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define Layer 4 as an enforceable rights, explanation, appeal, ombudsman, diagnostic/patient-safety, injury, AI-accountability, data-rights, accessibility, equity, transparency and trust system. |

| System entities | ARCH-NHAC; ARCH-NOPRSL; ARCH-HRPO; ARCH-PROO; ARCH-NAT if retained; ARCH-A1-HCAC; ARCH-NPSMIB; ARCH-HAAO; ARCH-PRTO; operators; patients/providers/public. |

| Assumptions | ASM-009 human accountability; ASM-011 continuity; ASM-013 durable/repairable; D5B-DEC-11/12; OI-022/023/039/040. |

| Data / parameters | rights.access_event/correction_case/appeal_case; safety.event; ai.model_decision; clinical.result/care_plan; governance.requirement_result; public.metric_release; workforce.safety_culture. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-RGT-001–012; SR-EQ-001–010; SR-AI-004–010; KPP-D6/D7/T-ED-001–T-ED-005/TRUST1/CULT1; TPP-LEG1/USE1/USE2/11.5/11.6/12.4/12.6; IF-017/020–023/031/032. |

| Principal risks | Silent rationing; unusable notice/appeal; delayed relief; retaliation; diagnostic harm; underreporting; punitive safety culture; AI opacity; inequity; privacy/reporting conflict; trust collapse/capture. |

| Simulation implication | Model decision/explanation/notice, appeal urgency/queue/relief/remedy, safety detection/harm/review/compensation, rights usability, language/disability, equity gaps/correction, AI influence, publication, trust and corrective-action closure. |
Layer 4 supplies the system's permission to operate. The National Office of Patient Rights, Safety, and Legitimacy (NOPRSL), operating within the independent National Health Accountability Commission, anchors a broader rights, safety, judicial-remedy and transparency architecture. Public coverage and capacity are not legitimate if denial, delay, routing, data use, safety events and resource constraints remain hidden or practically unchallengeable. The legitimacy architecture turns rights into executable controls attached to the operational event, separates review from operation, provides time-sensitive relief and remedy, learns from injury and reversal, publishes performance with privacy protection, and measures whether people and clinicians experience the system as fair, safe and usable.
6.10.1 Oversight and remedy architecture

| Entity | Primary role | Independence/remedy boundary |

| ARCH-NHAC | Independent rights, privacy, safety, anti-fraud, appeals and public-accountability commission | Does not operate DNHA benefits/payment; can inspect, order correction and refer/enforce |

| ARCH-NOPRSL | No Silent Rationing, patient rights, safety, AI accountability, service design, equity and trust | Sets/enforces Layer 4 standards independent of operational throughput goals |

| ARCH-HRPO | Privacy, data rights, access audit, segmentation, consent and breach oversight | Can inspect sensitive access and require correction/remedy |

| ARCH-PROO | Patient/provider ombudsman, navigation, complaint resolution and provisional-relief triggers | Assistance is not a substitute for enforceable appeal/court access |

| ARCH-A1-HCAC | Article I expedited claims, care, payment, rights and anti-impoundment remedies | Judicial order is enforceable; optional NAT cannot block urgent access |

| ARCH-NPSMIB | Patient/diagnostic safety, injury compensation and learning network | Separates learning and fair compensation from concealment or retaliation |

| ARCH-HAAO / ARCH-PRTO | Hospital accountability and public dashboards/publication | Audit/suppression rules are visible; operators cannot suppress adverse performance |
6.10.2 Patient Bill of Rights as an operational contract
Table D5B-29. Core rights and executable evidence

| Right | Operational meaning | Evidence/remedy |

| Covered care and continuity | Receive covered medically necessary care without silent financial, administrative or capacity exclusion | Coverage/benefit record; provisional protection; appeal/remedy |

| Explanation | Know facts, rule/version, evidence, accountable authority, timing and reason for a material decision | TPP-LEG1; decision record |

| Human review | Obtain accountable human review of high-stakes AI-influenced or adverse decisions | SR-AI-010; TPP-11.5 |

| Appeal and provisional relief | File accessibly, preserve urgency, obtain interim protection where required and receive enforceable remedy | TPP-USE2/12.6; IF-021/022 |

| Records and privacy | Access, correct, see disclosures, control applicable consent/segmentation and challenge misuse | TPP-10.5; IF-017 |

| Safety and disclosure | Have abnormal results closed, serious incidents learned from, and injury/remedy processes available | KPP-D6; SR-RGT-006/007 |

| Language/disability usability | Use services, notices and remedies in accessible language and form | KPP-E5; SR-RGT-008/009 |

| Equity and civil rights | Receive protected, stratified monitoring and corrective action without discriminatory routing or burden | SR-EQ; IF-032 |

| No retaliation | Report, complain, appeal, decline informal caregiving, or request accommodation without retaliation | NHAC/PROO enforcement |
NO SILENT RATIONING DOCTRINE  No covered person may be denied, delayed, deprioritized, rerouted, or refused covered care except through an explicit statutory, clinical, budgetary, or evidence-based rule that is visible, explainable, appealable, and audited.
Table D5B-30. No Silent Rationing decision test

| Test | Required evidence | Failure meaning |

| Rule exists | A statutory, clinical, budgetary or evidence-based rule controls the decision | No informal custom, undisclosed quota or missing-capacity fiction |

| Rule is valid | Current version, authorized owner, evidence, scope and effective date are present | Expired, unpublished or out-of-scope rule fails |

| Facts are complete | Relevant clinical, functional, preference, capacity and accommodation facts are considered | Missing facts trigger correction/provisional treatment, not automatic denial |

| Reason is explicit | The decision shows how facts and rule produce the outcome | Template language without case application fails |

| Human authority | Named accountable reviewer validates the material decision | AI/vendor/system owner cannot replace legal/clinical authority |

| Notice is usable | Language, disability, channel, timing, urgency and next steps meet standards | Delivery alone is not comprehension |

| Review is effective | Appeal, provisional relief, evidence access and remedy can occur before avoidable harm | A technically available but unusable or too-late appeal fails |

| System learns | Outcome, reversal, safety/equity effect and corrective action update oversight | Repeated high-reversal categories trigger review |
Explanation completeness  TPP-LEG1 = decisions containing every required explanation element / eligible adverse or routing decisions
Required elements include facts, controlling rule/version, evidence, accountable authority, outcome, timing, review/provisional-relief path and accessibility. Presence without case-specific intelligibility fails the usability control.
6.10.3 Appeals, ombudsman and enforceable relief
Table D5B-31. Appeal state model

| State | Meaning | Guard/output |

| decision.issued | Complete adverse/routing/delay record and accessible notice released | Urgency and provisional-relief screen starts |

| reconsideration | Operator corrects clerical, factual or rule-application error through a separate reviewer | Cannot consume time needed for emergency/expedited relief |

| rights_review | NHAC/PROO examines rights, usability, safety, evidence and interim protection | Complete packet and ombudsman assistance |

| tribunal_optional | NAT review occurs only if retained and non-delaying | May not restrict direct urgent Article I relief |

| article_i_review | A1-HCAC can stay, order, reverse, compel payment/care/data, or grant other statutory remedy | Enforceable expedited jurisdiction |

| remedy.executed | Coverage, care, routing, payment, debt, record and publication states are corrected | Downstream replay and compliance evidence |

| learning.closed | Reversal pattern, root cause and systemic corrective action are evaluated | Category review above controlled reversal threshold |
Appeal timeliness  TPP-12.6 = appeals resolved within the applicable urgency-class target / appeals due in the period
Urgency, clock start/pause, provisional relief, remand, withdrawal, incomplete notice and remedy execution need statutory definitions under OI-039. A favorable decision not executed is not closed.
The initial decision record is immutable as issued but can be superseded; later evidence and corrections remain separately attributable.
Operational reconsideration uses a separate reviewer and may correct obvious error quickly, but cannot delay emergency or expedited NHAC/court relief.
PROO helps assemble evidence, accommodations and urgency without becoming a mandatory exhaustion barrier. Lack of user skill or connectivity activates assistance.
Provisional relief preserves care, coverage, medication, LTC service, payment or another protected state when delay could defeat the remedy and statute authorizes protection.
A reversal propagates to clinical routing, coverage, claim/payment, patient debt, records, provider notices and public metrics. Systemic patterns create learning/corrective actions.
6.10.4 Diagnostic safety, injury and learning
Table D5B-32. Safety and injury control loop

| Stage | Required behavior | Primary record/owner |

| Detect | Patient/provider report, result, bounce-back, trigger, audit, complaint, model or surveillance signal | safety.event; rights.appeal_case |

| Protect | Immediate clinical response, disclosure/notice, provisional relief, model/process suspension and evidence preservation | NPSMIB/NHAC/operator |

| Investigate | Root cause across clinical, diagnostic, human factors, data, AI, staffing and governance | Independent access and just-culture controls |

| Remedy | Patient/provider relief, injury compensation where applicable, record/payment correction and continuity | IF-022/031 |

| Learn | Protocol, training, staffing, design, formula or vendor change with owner and due date | governance.requirement_result |

| Verify | Independent closure testing, recurrence monitoring, stratified effect and public aggregate | KPP-D6; IF-023/032 |
Diagnostic safety spans access, triage, testing, interpretation, communication, follow-up, referral and reassessment. The system links abnormal-result nonclosure, 72-hour bounce-backs, seven-day escalation, delayed referral, repeat presentation, AI disagreement, complaint and injury signals. A just-culture design distinguishes human error, at-risk behavior, reckless conduct and system failure; it protects good-faith reporting while preserving patient disclosure, compensation, professional accountability and corrective action.
Safety-event reporting completeness  KPP-D6 = reported serious safety events / estimated total serious safety events
The estimator and reportable taxonomy remain OI-023/040. Higher reporting can initially indicate better detection rather than worse care; harm incidence and reporting completeness are separate outputs.
6.10.5 Clinician legitimacy and safety culture
Workers can report unsafe staffing, workload, diagnostic, data, AI, retaliation and resource risks through protected channels with timely response and appeal.
Safety culture measures psychological safety, leadership response, teamwork, learning, handoff, staffing/workload, nonpunitive response and corrective-action credibility using a validated instrument.
Compensation, productivity and performance systems cannot penalize clinically justified escalation, reporting, override, accommodation or time spent on required follow-up and explanation.
Serious or repeated staffing-safety failure can restrict capacity, trigger emergency staffing/retention action, delay a gate or protect a service line; it cannot be averaged away by national performance.
6.10.6 Accessibility, equity, transparency and trust

| Domain | Required control | Trigger/correction |

| Language | Qualified language access across care, notice, records, appeal and public information | KPP-E5 failure → service correction, vendor/workforce action and affected-case review |

| Disability | Accessible channels, formats, communication, physical/digital accommodation and assistance | Compliance failure → immediate accommodation and systemic design correction |

| Equity | Stratify coverage, access, safety, appeal and outcome where lawful/ethical | Two-quarter statutory threshold breach → IF-032 correction plan |

| Tribal/rural | Sovereignty/data governance, direct funding/compact rights and rural essential access | Direct/compact remedy and KPP-E4/TPP-TRIB1 corrective action |

| Public dashboards | Approved numerator/denominator, strata, uncertainty, suppression, revision and audit history | Late/suppressed/incorrect release → TPP-12.4 remedy and public revision |

| Trust | Versioned representative measure of fairness plus qualitative complaint/service evidence | Material decline → independent public-confidence repair review |
TRANSPARENCY BOUNDARY  Privacy suppression protects people, not institutions. Suppression methods, thresholds and revisions are public; small-cell or sensitive-data protection must not be used to hide a material safety, equity, appeal or access failure from authorized oversight or the public at an appropriate aggregation level.

6.11 Adaptation and Repair Concept
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: National rules will become obsolete or fail in unforeseen conditions; repair must be possible without permitting quiet benefit erosion or executive sabotage. Why this structure: Each concept joins institutions, workflows, rights, performance measures, risks, and simulation behavior in one operational explanation. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes adaptation and repair concept explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define Layer 5 as an independent scorekeeping, formula-control, retrospective/sunset review, emergency correction, legal contingency, adversarial test, technology/vendor lifecycle, benefit update, regional waiver, appeals-learning, and public-confidence repair system. |

| System entities | ARCH-NHASB; NHAC/NOPRSL; CHAO; DNHA/RHA operators; THDO/HFASB; A1-HCAC; Formula Registry users; patients/providers/public. |

| Assumptions | ASM-013 durability/repairability; D5C6A-DEC-01–04; OI-018/019/021/023/044–048; national floors, rights, safety, equity, continuity, and human accountability remain non-waivable. |

| Data / parameters | governance.formula_version; governance.requirement_result; governance.phase_gate; governance.compact_waiver; rights.appeal_case; safety.event; ai.model_decision; fiscal.obligation_receipt_reserve; public.metric_release; cost.event. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-ADP-001–015; SR-ARCH-015; SR-INN-005/006; VR-003/021–023/025; TPP-FORM1/REG1; KPP-TRUST1; IF-020–024/027/028/032. |

| Principal risks | Operator capture; formula opacity; emergency power abuse; stale rules; false corrective closure; vendor lock-in; unevaluated waiver; legal shock; appeal repetition; trust repair as messaging only. |

| Simulation implication | Model trigger arrivals, severity, affected population, queue/clock, repair pathway, containment, decision/version, implementation lag/cost, affected-case remedy, independent verification, residual risk, recurrence, trust, and phase/gate consequences. |
Layer 5 supplies controlled learning without creating an easy sabotage channel. The National Health Adaptation and Scorekeeping Board (NHASB) independently measures fiscal and operational performance, verifies gate evidence, maintains the Formula Registry, schedules reviews, tests institutional failure, and certifies whether corrective actions work. Operators remain responsible for delivery and immediate containment; NHASB remains separate enough to challenge their data, formulas, conclusions, and claimed readiness. NHAC protects rights, safety, privacy, equity, and practical appeal; CHAO audits for Congress; courts retain enforceable remedies. Repair therefore changes a controlled rule, configuration, authority, workflow, resource plan, or institution while preserving traceable obligations and open rights.
ADAPTATION PRINCIPLE  The system must be hard to sabotage, but easy to correct through transparent, evidence-based, legally bounded repair.
6.11.1 Trigger catalog and repair lifecycle
Table D5C6A-6. Adaptation triggers

| Trigger class | Detection condition | Available response |

| Performance | KPP/TPP, SR, queue, quality, access, equity, continuity, or publication misses a controlled threshold or control limit | Parameter review, corrective action, pilot restriction, gate hold |

| Appeal/review | Reversal, remand, complaint, provisional-relief, or no-silent-rationing pattern exceeds the approved category trigger | Category review, rule/workflow repair, affected-case replay |

| Safety/equity | Serious event, diagnostic harm, subgroup deviation, retaliation, or unsafe workload indicates systemic risk | Immediate protection, safety review, restriction/suspension, remedy |

| Fiscal | Forecast error, obligation/receipt variance, reserve erosion, or formula instability crosses a registered threshold | Forecast review, stabilizer/reserve action, formula repair |

| AI/technology | Model drift, audit failure, security defect, end-of-support, lock-in, or vendor exit-plan failure | Restrict/suspend, manual fallback, migrate, review affected cases |

| Legal | Court order, preemption failure, noncooperation, impoundment, vacancy, or authority loss activates a contingency | Default rule, alternate authority, direct federal/tribal path, legal repair |

| Pilot/waiver | Interim/final evaluation shows success, harm, inequity, nonperformance, or external-validity limits | Scale, modify, extend once, terminate, or restore baseline |

| Trust | Representative trust measure, participation, complaint, misinformation, or service-experience trigger is breached | Independent review, disclosure, service repair, public confidence protocol |
Table D5C6A-7. Controlled repair states

| State | Required meaning | Exit control |

| detected | A signed trigger event identifies source, affected population/function, severity, urgency, and evidence quality | Create repair case; preserve evidence; apply immediate protection if needed |

| classified | Authority classifies technical, clinical, fiscal, legal, rights, safety, AI, vendor, waiver, or trust pathway | Name owner, independent verifier, clock, notice, and permissible actions |

| contained | Temporary guard, manual fallback, payment/coverage continuity, restriction, or provisional relief bounds harm | Containment cannot become a silent permanent rule |

| analyzed | Root cause, affected-case cohort, equity/safety/fiscal impacts, alternatives, legal basis, and dependencies are tested | Publish or protect evidence under controlled transparency/privacy rules |

| decided | Authorized body selects repair, ratification, rollback, scale, termination, sunset, or no-change with reasons | Decision links authority, formula/rule version, effective date, appeal, and rollback |

| implemented | Versioned change is deployed with training, data migration, continuity, communications, and monitoring | No uncontrolled configuration drift |

| verified | Independent evidence determines whether intended effect occurred without unacceptable displacement | VR method, subgroup analysis, reproducibility, and residual risk |

| closed_or_reopened | Effectiveness is certified and learning published, or failure reopens/escalates the case | Update registry, risks, baselines, simulation priors, and future review dates |
Repair effectiveness  corrective_effectiveness = verified_cases_with_sustained_intended_effect_and_no_unacceptable_displacement / corrective_actions_due_for_effectiveness_review
SR-ADP-014 requires at least 95% by P8. Observation window, displacement tests, recurrence rule, and materiality remain controlled under OI-021/023.
Repair backlog  repair_backlog[t+1] = repair_backlog[t] + triggered_cases - closed_effective_cases - validly_consolidated_cases
Consolidation retains every affected requirement, population, remedy, deadline, and recurrence link; it cannot hide overdue work.
6.11.2 Formula Registry and controlled rule execution
The Formula Registry is the authoritative control plane for formulas affecting payment, access, benefits, priority, routing, workforce allocation, and fiscal reserves. It contains both a human-readable specification and a reproducible executable representation. Operational systems may cache a signed authorized version, but every decision event retains the version, inputs, outputs, exceptions, and human/public authority necessary to reproduce and challenge the result.
Table D5C6A-8. Minimum Formula Registry record

| Field group | Required content |

| identity/authority | formula_id; title; statutory/regulatory authority; owner; independent verifier; affected decisions |

| version/time | version; predecessor/successor; proposed, validated, effective, expiry, sunset, and retirement timestamps |

| specification | variables; units; domains; equation/executable artifact; rounding; missing-data; precedence; dependency graph |

| data/provenance | authoritative sources; schema/version; lineage; quality constraints; protected-group treatment; code/data hashes |

| tests | reference cases; boundary/exception cases; regression corpus; reconciliation tolerance; expected outputs; independent result |

| constraints | rights, safety, equity, fiscal, access, continuity, privacy, anti-gaming, and human-review constraints |

| operations | deployment scope; feature/config flags; monitoring; alert thresholds; manual fallback; rollback package |

| review | notice/comment; appeal/review links; emergency status; retrospective/sunset outcome; corrective actions; public summary |
Table D5C6A-9. Formula lifecycle

| State | Entry meaning | Operational guard |

| proposed | Purpose, authority, variables, sources, owner, impacts, and draft tests registered | No operational effect |

| validated | Independent technical, legal, fiscal, safety, equity, usability, and regression checks pass for intended scope | Eligible for notice/authorization |

| noticed | Human-readable rule, effects, evidence, tests, and comment/review path are published as required | Comments and defects remain linked |

| active | Authorized signed version is effective for declared scope/time | Every affected event records version and input/output provenance |

| emergency | Temporary corrective version operates under limited authority, scope, clock, notice, and fallback | Must be ratified, replaced, or rolled back before expiry |

| suspended | Version is disabled after safety, equity, legal, security, data, or performance trigger | Manual/predecessor path and affected-case review active |

| superseded | Successor version is effective after controlled comparison and migration | Historical reproduction remains possible |

| retired | No new use; retention, appeals, audit, and reproducibility obligations remain | Dependencies are resolved and vendor artifacts preserved |
FORMULA INVARIANT  No formula may silently change because source data, code, weights, thresholds, rounding, dependencies, or vendor components change. A material change creates a new version, requires applicable validation and notice, and retains a tested rollback path.
6.11.3 Review, sunset, emergency correction, and adversarial test
Table D5C6A-10. Adaptation and repair pathways

| Pathway | Trigger | Required disposition |

| Major rule retrospective | Scheduled evidence after sufficient operating exposure | Continue, narrow, repair, replace, or initiate sunset; SR-ADP-004 |

| Sunset review | Authority/program/formula/waiver/vendor arrangement reaches review date | Reauthorize with evidence, transfer duties, repair, or terminate without extinguishing open rights; SR-ADP-005 |

| Emergency technical correction | Narrow defect creates immediate material risk and ordinary process is too slow | Temporary signed version, notice, protection, expiry, ratify/replace/rollback; SR-ADP-006; VR-022 |

| Red team | Scheduled or trigger-based adversarial test of sabotage, capture, gaming, cyber, continuity, equity, fiscal, or legal failure | Finding, severity, owner, target, closure evidence, residual risk; SR-ADP-012 |

| Vendor/technology lifecycle | Critical dependency, end-of-support, concentration, escrow failure, or portability test | Repair contract, migrate, insource, suspend, or retire with continuity; SR-ADP-009 |

| Benefit-boundary update | New evidence/technology, unmet need, safety/value change, or public petition | Cover, cover with evidence, restrict, delist, or retain with explanation and appeal |

| Regional adaptation waiver | Region proposes a bounded variation to improve local delivery while preserving national floors | Approve/deny; evaluate; scale, repair, expire, or terminate; SR-ADP-015; VR-023 |

| Appeals learning/trust repair | High-overturn category or trust trigger | Affected-case review, rule/service repair, remedy, public report, follow-up; SR-ADP-007/011 |
An emergency correction pathway is narrower than ordinary rulemaking because it exists to contain an immediate material defect, not to bypass policy disagreement. The initiating record identifies the defect, authority, affected scope, temporary version, protections, public notice, expiry, ratification path, rollback, and affected-case review. Expiration restores the last valid protected state unless a lawful successor is active; it does not leave a vacuum.
The legal contingency matrix operates similarly. Each vulnerable authority or operational dependency links a trigger to a preauthorized fallback owner, funding and data path, continuity obligation, rights/remedy route, public notice, and return condition. The matrix is tested before failure and updated after litigation or red-team evidence; it does not presume that every adverse decision can be cured by executive discretion.
6.11.4 Regional adaptation waivers and learning
A region files a public hypothesis, baseline, intended outcome, eligible population/function, national floors, patient-protection plan, equity/safety analysis, budget impact, data/formula plan, independent evaluator, duration, stopping rules, sunset, and restoration plan.
NHASB verifies evaluability and conflicts; NHAC verifies rights, safety, accessibility, privacy, equity, notice, appeal, and remedy; the legally authorized body approves or denies the bounded variation.
The waiver enters a signed active state only after operations, training, data, funding, fallback, and public notice are ready. Core entitlement, non-discrimination, emergency access, explanation/appeal, data rights, human accountability, and mandatory payment protections are not waivable.
Interim monitoring can contain, restrict, suspend, or terminate a waiver when stopping rules, material harm, inequity, invalid data, fiscal breach, or evaluator independence fail.
At sunset, independent evaluation supports scale, repair, one bounded extension, or termination. Scale creates a separate national change record; a regional success does not automatically become national evidence.
Waiver evaluation completion  TPP-REG1 = approved_waivers_with_completed_independent_evaluation / approved_waivers_due_for_evaluation
Target >=95%. Terminated or harmful waivers remain in the denominator when their evaluation is due; premature closure cannot erase evidence obligations.
6.11.5 Appeals learning and public confidence repair
Appeals and complaints are both individual remedy channels and sensors for systemic defect. A high-overturn category review tests whether the benefit rule, evidence standard, routing practice, notice, data, human review, staffing, queue, formula, or implementation incentive caused repeat error. The response identifies affected prior cases, supplies correction or remedy, changes the responsible control, and verifies recurrence reduction. Public confidence repair uses the same discipline: independent evidence, visible defect, accountable service change, remedy, and follow-up measurement—not a communications campaign detached from operations.

6.11.6 Phase, risk, cost, and simulation behavior
PH-P0 establishes NHASB, the initial Formula Registry, scorekeeping independence, change tiers, review inventory, legal contingency baseline, red-team plan, and gate evidence standard.
PH-P1–P3 registers identity, coverage, claims, pharmacy, payment, and early AI formulas before operational use; early transition defects test emergency repair and affected-case methods.
PH-P4–P5 requires representative pilot/waiver evaluation and scale-or-terminate decisions; favorable throughput cannot override safety, equity, rights, workforce, or fiscal evidence.
PH-P6–P7 expands benefit-boundary and technology-lifecycle governance while appeal/trust learning tests national service experience.
PH-P8 certifies scorekeeping, formula, review, sunset, vendor-exit, red-team, forecast-error, corrective-effectiveness, waiver, and trust-repair maturity without treating unresolved repair work as zero risk.

7. Implementation
7.1 Implementation Phases
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Attempting simultaneous national conversion would couple every risk; phases create controlled learning, protected continuity, and explicit limits on what may expand next. Why this structure: Implementation is organized around phased evidence and reversible gates so national scale follows demonstrated readiness. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes implementation phases explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define PH-P0–P8 as cumulative implementation capability states with planning-year anchors, controlled work packages, entry conditions, outputs, independent exit evidence, hold/rollback, and durable transfer. |

| System entities | NHTCA integrated command; DNHA and architecture owners; RHAs; states/tribal nations; THDO/HFASB/NHETF; NHASB; NHAC; CHAO; providers/vendors/employers. |

| Assumptions | ASM-010 staged rollout; ASM-011 continuity; ASM-019 transition cost; D5C6A-DEC-05/06/09; years are anchors, not automatic authorizations; overlapping work preserves dependency and configuration control. |

| Data / parameters | governance.phase_gate/requirement_result/formula_version/compact_waiver; fiscal obligations/receipts/reserves; cost.event; workforce, coverage, claims, payment, clinical, benefit, safety, rights, AI, cyber, public metrics. |

| Requirements / performance | PR-SCH-001–009; PR-TRN; all allocated SR/VR; PH-P0–P8; IF-023–028. |

| Principal risks | Calendar-driven progression; incomplete foundational data; unfunded/unstaffed mandates; capacity mismatch; regional inequity; double-run failure; configuration drift; premature institutional sunset. |

| Simulation implication | Model phases/waves as states with entry guards, task durations, resource/capacity constraints, dependencies, gates, evidence quality, delay/repair/rollback, costs, learning, regional heterogeneity, and cumulative capability. |
The 10–12-year roadmap is a capability-acquisition sequence. The year attached to each phase is the planning anchor for the nominal program, not a promise that authority, service, data, workforce, funding, or readiness exists on that date. Work may overlap across phases when its dependencies, funding, capacity, rights, and configuration are controlled. A phase can be active in one bounded region or function while a predecessor capability remains under repair elsewhere; the program records that heterogeneity rather than labeling the entire nation complete.
PHASE RULE  A phase exit means the specified capability and evidence are accepted for the stated scope. It does not imply that every mature KPP/TPP target has been achieved, and it cannot extinguish unresolved continuity, appeal, payment, safety, data, or legal duties.
7.1.1 Phase dictionary

| Phase | Anchor | Capability state | Principal work | Exit evidence |

| PH-P8 | Year 12 | Full integration and maturity certification | Mature manufacturing; information mesh; innovation delinkage; mature payment; fiscal/legitimacy/adaptation integration | All maturity targets assessed; Gate 4 and cross-domain certification; PR-SCH-009 evidence; unresolved defects retained in repair plan |
7.1.2 Phase state model and progression
Table D5C6A-15. Phase lifecycle states

| State | Controlled meaning |

| planned | Scope, baseline, owners, resources, dependencies, risks, evidence and fallback are configuration-controlled |

| entry_review | Predecessor outputs and entry conditions are independently checked; unresolved conditions are classified |

| active | Authorized work packages operate within approved regions/populations/functions and change-control bounds |

| evidence_ready | Required operational exposure, data quality, tests, audits, equity analysis and corrective-action evidence are complete |

| gate_hold | A blocking threshold, evidence deficiency, safety/equity/rights issue, or dependency failure stops affected progression |

| exit_certified | NHASB certifies the defined exit; accountable authority accepts residual risk and publishes the decision |

| rollback_or_repair | Affected scope returns to protected prior/bridge state while root cause, remedy, and re-entry evidence are completed |

| closed | Outputs, open duties, records, costs, lessons, and remaining risks transfer to durable owners |
NHTCA maintains one integrated phase/wave baseline, while each architecture owner controls its allocated work-package baseline and evidence.
Entry review verifies predecessor outputs, funding, staffed capacity, data, interfaces, legal authority, rights/safety controls, regional/tribal arrangements, suppliers, continuity, and fallback.
Work packages may proceed in parallel only when shared resource, data, formula, vendor, legal, and operational dependencies are explicit and double counting is prevented.
Evidence-ready status requires sufficient representative operating exposure and resolution or bounded classification of defects; completion of build tasks alone is not readiness.
A gate hold applies to affected scope. Protected existing care, payment, benefits, records, employment support, and legal duties continue through the hold and repair.
Exit certification identifies scope, exclusions, conditions, residual risk, next-phase dependencies, unresolved obligations, and the durable owner of every artifact and open case.

Table D5C6A-16. PH-P0–P8 milestone obligations

| Requirement | Exact obligation | Trace | Method |

| PR-SCH-001 | The project shall complete statutory establishment of core governing bodies by the end of Phase 0. | SN-13, SN-20 | Inspection |

| PR-SCH-002 | The project shall complete authoritative person, provider, facility, formulary, and claims registries by the end of Phase 1. | SN-02, SN-06, SN-15 | Demonstration |

| PR-SCH-003 | The project shall operationalize the public pharmacy claims utility by the end of Phase 2. | SN-08 | Demonstration |

PR-SCH-006 creates a Phase 5 milestone of at least 65% unit-network population coverage. PR-SCH-011 later requires at least 80% before broad cost-sharing elimination, and KPP-B7 requires at least 95% within the access standard by Phase 8. These are three distinct controls and must remain separate in schedules, dashboards, and simulation logic.
7.1.4 Cost, capacity, and configuration rules
Every phase work package books cost to a controlled CP family and cost-event identity with time, region, owner, funding source, obligation, outlay, asset/expense treatment, recurring/transition classification, and recovery/reconciliation state.
The $1.2T–$2.0T transition envelope over 10–12 years is a program constraint, not permission to invent phase shares. OI-043 controls allocation until a cost-loaded schedule reconciles shared infrastructure, contingency, reserves, capital, and recurring transfers.
Workforce, facility, supplier, training, reviewer, verifier, and change-management capacity are resources in the schedule. A task cannot finish because money is authorized if the required capacity is unavailable.
Each release records architecture, interface, schema, formula, code/configuration, procedure, training, legal, vendor, and public-document versions. A wave cannot mix incompatible baselines without an explicit bridge and reconciliation.
Schedule variance is decomposed into dependency, resource, defect/repair, approval, legal, procurement/vendor, data, regional/compact, and external-shock causes so the simulation does not treat all delay alike.
7.2 Implementation Roadmap by Domain
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: A phase label is not an implementation plan; each domain needs work packages, dependencies, accountable owners, evidence, and regional sequencing. Why this structure: Implementation is organized around phased evidence and reversible gates so national scale follows demonstrated readiness. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes implementation roadmap by domain explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Allocate phase capability across interdependent domain workstreams and define the minimum work-package contract, regional-wave method, dependency controls, deliverable baselines, and integrated cost/workforce/capacity treatment. |

| System entities | NHTCA; all DNHA/commission/Treasury/RHA architecture owners; states/tribal nations; providers/facilities; workforce/education bodies; vendors/suppliers; NHASB/NHAC/CHAO. |

| Assumptions | D5C6A-DEC-05/06/09/10; domain rows are implementation allocations, not new architecture elements or phase gates; national floors coexist with regional sequencing. |

| Data / parameters | All Section 5 operational datasets; work-package/schedule/configuration records; IF catalog; CP ledgers; KPP/TPP/VR evidence; regional population/capacity/baseline data. |

| Requirements / performance | Allocated PR/SR/VR; PR-SCH; PR-TRN; PH-P0–P8; PH-G1–G8; VR-001/002/025/030. |

| Principal risks | Siloed workstreams; hidden cross-domain dependency; regional capacity mismatch; shared-resource contention; inconsistent versions; unowned fallback; cost/workforce double count; inequitable wave selection. |

| Simulation implication | Model domain tasks as a dependency/resource network across phase, wave, region, population, architecture, interface, dataset, workforce, cost, risk, evidence, and fallback dimensions. |
The roadmap is an integrated portfolio rather than thirteen independent programs. Coverage depends on identity, claims, Treasury payment, rights, and continuity. Cost-sharing elimination depends on staffed unit and specialist capacity. Hospital conversion depends on regional services, workforce, payment, and stabilization. Expanded benefits depend on assessments, provider capacity, transport, records, and appeals. AI and the information mesh remain enabling components subject to human, safety, rights, and cyber constraints. The roadmap therefore binds each domain to a common work-package contract and makes cross-domain dependencies visible at every phase and regional wave.

7.2.3 Critical dependencies and protected fallback
Table D5C6A-19. Cross-domain dependency chains

| Chain | Required components | Integration rule | Fallback |

| Coverage-to-payment | Identity/eligibility + claims + Treasury disbursement + provider liquidity + appeal | A coverage wave cannot rely on an untested payment or provisional-coverage path | Hold/resize wave; manual/provisional rail; reconcile |

| Cost-sharing-to-capacity | Unit coverage + same-day access + closure + specialty escalation + under-referral safety | Financial access cannot be expanded beyond safe staffed service capacity | Retain protected bridge; add capacity; repair routing |

| Hospital-to-region | Global budget + charter/service lines + workforce + specialty/unit/EMS + capital/readiness | Budget change cannot destabilize essential regional services | Stabilization corridor; restore payment; regional repair |

| Expanded-benefit-to-workforce | Assessments + home-care/BH/DVH/EMS capacity + workforce/pipeline + rights | Benefit activation cannot be modeled as delivered service without capacity | Phase/wave limit; contracted/surge capacity; workforce action |

| AI-to-human operations | Validated version + human-review capacity + audit + equity/safety + manual fallback | AI productivity cannot be counted before accountable human and fallback capacity | Restrict/suspend; manual operations; affected-case review |

| Record-to-continuity | Identity + source records + corrections/segmentation + uptime/offline + legacy migration | National reliance requires usable, correct, resilient records | Federated/legacy/manual bridge; correction queue |

| Maturity-to-fiscal readiness | Certified obligations/receipts + reserves + collection + stabilizer + forecast error review | Benefit maturity cannot outrun durable financing | Hold certification; stabilizer/reserve/revenue repair |
Earliest work-package completion  finish_i = start_i + duration_i(resources, defects, learning) subject to finish_predecessor + interface_lag <= start_i
Dependencies include legal, data, formula, workforce, facility, supplier, training, rights, verifier, and regional readiness—not only technical predecessor tasks.
Regional service-ready capacity  ready_capacity[r,d,t] = min(staffed_capacity, facility_capacity, supply_capacity, payment_capacity, data_capacity, rights_and_safety_capacity)
A domain cannot claim a service-ready population beyond its constraining component. Mobile, tele, contracted, cross-region, and manual capacity are explicit and cannot be counted twice.
7.2.4 Regional waves, compacts, and equity
Wave selection uses readiness, need, representativeness, rural/urban/tribal/frontier conditions, capacity, legal/compact state, data, provider liquidity, and equity—not political convenience or ease alone.
Each wave declares population, geography, providers/facilities, benefits/functions, effective time, baseline, continuity assets, dual-run/bridge, support, communications, rights, complaints, incident thresholds, rollback point, and exit evidence.
State/regional/tribal compacts allocate duties and resources while preserving national floors, direct federal fallback, and tribal-approved evidence/data governance. A state certification cannot substitute for tribal approval under VR-026.
Representative pilot design includes safety-net, rural/frontier, high-need, disabled, low-digital-access, non-English-preferred, and historically underserved populations wherever relevant and lawful.
Equity is tested for access, service completion, safety, denial/routing, appeal, payment/liquidity, workforce, data quality, and burden. A favorable national average cannot authorize a wave with material subgroup harm.

| Evidence/public | VR protocol, observed artifacts, findings/corrective action, certification, dashboard/public explanation | Immutable retention, supersession and reproducibility |
7.3 Phase Gates
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Schedule pressure can otherwise override safety and readiness; gates make expansion conditional on evidence rather than calendar declarations. Why this structure: Implementation is organized around phased evidence and reversible gates so national scale follows demonstrated readiness. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes phase gates explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define eight evidence-based readiness gates, decision rights, universal evidence package, progression floors, mature-target distinction, outcomes, conditions, exceptions, fallback, rollback, and re-entry. |

| System entities | NHASB independent verifier; NHTCA/DNHA/RHA applicants; THDO/HFASB fiscal evidence; NHAC rights/safety/equity review; CHAO audit; accountable statutory decision body; A1-HCAC remedies. |

| Assumptions | D5C6A-DEC-02/05/07/08/10; OI-021/023/042/048; a gate applies to defined scope and cannot waive rights, safety, equity, continuity, mandatory payment, or independent evidence. |

| Data / parameters | governance.phase_gate/requirement_result/formula_version; all gate-relevant operational datasets; evidence packages; risks/findings/corrective actions; public.metric_release. |

| Requirements / performance | PR-SCH-010–015; VR-003/004/005/025/030 and domain VR; PH-G1–G8; gateway metrics and mature KPP/TPP targets. |

| Principal risks | Threshold gaming; immature denominators; operator self-certification; insufficient exposure; hidden subgroup harm; conditional pass abuse; schedule pressure; stale evidence; unenforceable rollback. |

| Simulation implication | Model gates as blocking decisions over scoped state with observed metric distributions, data/evidence quality, uncertainty, mandatory constraints, decision outcome, conditions/expiry, delay, repair, rollback, re-entry, and cost/access/trust effects. |
A phase gate is a governed decision, not a dashboard color. The implementing authority submits a versioned evidence package; NHASB independently reproduces and verifies gateway results; NHAC evaluates rights, safety, equity, usability, and remedy; fiscal and domain specialists authenticate their records; the accountable statutory authority issues a scoped public decision. CHAO may audit the process and evidence. A failed or incomplete gate stops only the affected progression but preserves care, payment, appeals, continuity, and other existing obligations.
7.3.1 Universal gate evidence package
Table D5C6A-20. Evidence required for every gate

| Package element | Required content |

| decision scope | Named phase transition, deployment, benefit expansion, record reliance, AI use, conversion, or payer sunset; affected regions/populations/functions |

| requirement baseline | Exact PR/SR/KPP/TPP/VR versions, gateway floors, mature targets, exclusions, approved open issues, and legal authority |

| operational exposure | Representative sites/populations, sufficient volume/time, surge/failure scenarios, unresolved exceptions, and comparison period |

| data/metric package | Owner, numerator/denominator, source, lineage, quality, frequency, Formula Registry version, stratification, uncertainty, and reproducible result |

| test/evaluation | Inspection, analysis, test, or demonstration protocol; entry/exit; observed outputs; pass/fail; independent sampling/audit |

| rights/safety/equity | Patient/provider notices, appeal usability, safety review, subgroup results, protected continuity, complaints, provisional relief, and remedy |

| capacity/fiscal | Staffed capacity, suppliers/facilities, payment/liquidity, obligated funding, reserves/contingency, and cost/schedule exposure |

| risk/fallback | Open findings, risk/FMEA state, corrective actions, residual risk, containment, rollback, manual/offline/legacy bridge, and re-entry plan |

| certification/publication | Operator attestation, independent verifier result, NHAC/CHAO observations where applicable, accountable decision, conditions/expiry, and public report |
INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION  Every value used to block or permit progression requires independent verification under VR-003 and VR-025. Operator attestation, vendor certification, schedule completion, or a favorable point estimate is not sufficient by itself.
7.3.2 Gate dictionary
Table D5C6A-21. PH-G1–PH-G8 readiness gates

| Gate | Name | Decision point | Minimum readiness content | Primary trace/evidence | Failure response |

| PH-G1 | Claims readiness | Before major expansion and specifically PH-P3 to PH-P4 | Clean-claim auto-adjudication >=75% for Wave I; payment timeliness; eligibility latency; provider cash-flow disruption within approved floors | PR-SCH-010; TPP-2.1/2.2/2.4; operational logs and timestamped Treasury data | Hold/resize expansion; provisional/manual payment; liquidity protection; root-cause repair |

| PH-G2 | Unit capacity | Before broad cost-sharing elimination | Unit population coverage >=80%; unsafe under-referral <=5/10,000 non-escalated encounters; same-day access and follow-up closure meet approved floors | PR-SCH-011/012; KPP-B2/B7/B8/B9; clinical review and stratified access data | Retain protected cost-sharing bridge where lawful; add staff/sites/mobile capacity; repair routing/escalation |

| PH-G3 | LTC and workforce readiness | Before full expanded-benefit rollout | LTC assessment timeliness >=85%; critical vacancy, home-care sufficiency, BH first-contact, DVH/EMS readiness meet approved floors | PR-SCH-013; TPP-8.1/9.1–9.7; workforce and service records | Limit wave/scope; maintain existing entitlement; surge/contract/train capacity; reassess and re-enter |

| PH-G4 | Fiscal readiness | Before mature full-benefit/maturity certification | Dedicated revenue sufficiency >=98%; reserves >=6 months volatile exposure; wealth collection efficiency and stabilizer readiness meet approved floors | PR-SCH-014; KPP-C5/C6; TPP-6.4; actuarially certified obligations/receipts/reserves | Hold maturity; activate authorized stabilizer/reserve/revenue corrections; publish forecast-error review |

| PH-G5 | AI safety readiness | Before national AI-assisted routing | High-stakes human-review/audit capture >=97%; validation, protected-group comparison, drift, override, suspension, and manual fallback meet approved floors | PR-SCH-015; TPP-11.4–11.6; model-version-specific validation and logs | Restrict to validated bounded pilots or suspend; use human/manual path; review affected cases |

| PH-G6 | Records and cyber readiness | Before national record reliance | Access/correction/segmentation, API conformance, uptime, vulnerability remediation, downtime continuity and reconciliation meet approved floors | SR-DATA-001–012; TPP-10.1–10.6/11.1–11.3; tests, logs, drills and user testing | Continue federated/legacy/manual dependencies; remediate; repeat drill and representative usability test |

| PH-G7 | Legitimacy readiness | Before large-scale coverage conversion | Rights, usable appeal, no-silent-rationing explanation, ombudsman, public reporting, trust baseline and safety-reporting controls meet approved floors | SR-RGT/SR-EQ; TPP-LEG1/USE1/USE2/12.4/12.6; KPP-TRUST1; case audits and representative tests | Hold/resize conversion; improve notice/navigation/relief; independent review; confidence repair |

| PH-G8 | Transition continuity readiness | Before major legacy payer sunset | Active treatment/medication/record transfer, state/tribal compact or fallback, provider liquidity, open appeal/authorization ownership and legacy reconciliation meet approved floors | PR-TRN; KPP-T1/T2; TPP-12.1/12.5/TRIB1; pre/post patient-level evidence | Maintain legacy/dual-run/bridge duty; protect payments/care; correct transfer; recertify scoped sunset |
Only source-explicit numeric progression floors are treated as fixed in this installment. Other gate components—such as payment timeliness, eligibility latency, same-day access, follow-up closure, critical vacancy, home-care sufficiency, trust baseline, and record/cyber floors—must be approved through their exact requirements, performance dictionaries, and OI-042 acceptance protocols before they become executable gate thresholds.

7.3.4 Decisions, conditions, exceptions, and re-entry
Table D5C6A-24. Gate outcomes

| Outcome | Meaning | Authorized action |

| pass | All blocking floors and evidence conditions are met for the defined scope | Authorize only the stated progression; continue monitoring toward mature targets |

| conditional_bounded | A non-rights/non-safety evidence gap has a controlled containment and does not invalidate a mandatory floor | Authorize limited scope/time with named condition, expiry, monitoring, verifier, rollback, and public reason |

| hold | A blocking floor, evidence sufficiency, independent verification, rights, safety, equity, fiscal, or continuity condition fails | Do not advance affected scope; protect existing obligations; execute corrective plan |

| rollback_or_repair | Post-pass monitoring reveals material defect, harm, invalid data/formula, or condition breach | Return to protected predecessor/bridge or restrict affected function; remedy and re-enter gate |
A decision applies only to its declared scope, evidence versions, and time. Material scope, formula, data, architecture, vendor, legal, population, or workflow change can require re-review.
A condition names the gap, owner, action, metric/evidence, monitoring cadence, expiry, verifier, public treatment, and automatic hold/rollback trigger. It cannot cure a failed mandatory gateway floor by promise.
No exception may waive core entitlement, emergency access, civil rights, safety, explanation/appeal, data rights, human accountability, mandatory clean-obligation payment, or independent verification.
A regional variation follows VR-023 and Section 6.11 waiver controls. It is not a hidden gate exception and does not relabel a national failure as local flexibility.
Re-entry uses a new evidence snapshot that preserves the failed package, root cause, affected-case remedy, corrective action, effectiveness result, changes, remaining uncertainty, and updated rollback plan.
Post-pass monitoring can reopen a gate when a control limit, material harm, invalid data/formula, condition, legal authority, or continuity threshold fails.
Gate decision  gate_result = PASS only if all mandatory_floors AND evidence_sufficiency AND rights_safety_equity_constraints AND independent_verification are true
Uncertainty rules may require a confidence bound rather than a point estimate. The exact statistical acceptance contract remains OI-021/042.
