| TPP-12.1 | Mandatory payment protection coverage | >=99.5% core spending | Source target; baseline/acceptance evidence required |

| TPP-TRIB1 | Tribal compact compliance | >=98% | Source target; baseline/acceptance evidence required |
Formal demonstrations inject normal, peak, degraded, cyber, data-mismatch, workforce-shortage, rural/frontier, state-resistance, vendor-exit, AI-failure, fiscal-stress, and trust-collapse conditions as applicable. A gate package states which required scenario was not executed; absence of a relevant failure scenario is an evidence limitation, not proof of resilience.
7.4 Implementation Assurance
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: A program can pass individual tests while its interfaces, suppliers, schedules, or benefits fail collectively; implementation assurance integrates those controls. Why this structure: Implementation is organized around phased evidence and reversible gates so national scale follows demonstrated readiness. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes implementation assurance explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the integrated management, configuration, verification/validation, readiness review, evidence, risk/corrective-action, supplier/cyber, benefits-realization, and public-reporting system that assures implementation across phases and domains. |

| System entities | NHTCA; DNHA/ARCH owners; RHAs/state/tribal partners; THDO/HFASB/NHETF; NHASB; NHAC/NOPRSL; CHAO; A1-HCAC; providers; suppliers/vendors; workforce and public representatives. |

| Assumptions | D5C6A-DEC-02/05/06/09/10; assurance is continuous and risk-proportionate; verification proves conformance, validation tests stakeholder/service value, and neither converts a target into achieved performance. |

| Data / parameters | Integrated master schedule; requirements/configuration/evidence repositories; governance datasets; operational source data; cost/workforce/capacity ledgers; risk/FMEA/findings/corrective actions; dashboards. |

| Requirements / performance | VR-001–030; all PR/SR/KPP/TPP/CP/ARCH/IF/PH/RISK/SCN allocations; PH-G1–G8. |

| Principal risks | Fragmented control; evidence fabrication; weak independence; configuration mismatch; inadequate test representation; unresolved high risk; vendor opacity; cyber/offline failure; benefit overclaim; public-report suppression. |

| Simulation implication | Model assurance capacity, review/test queues, evidence quality, detection probability, false pass/fail, defect escape, corrective lag/effectiveness, resource/cost/schedule impact, gate delay, recurrence, transparency, and trust. |
Implementation assurance is the framework's disciplined proof system. It combines program integration with independent verification, enforceable rights and safety oversight, legislative audit, fiscal reconciliation, regional evidence, and public reporting. It does not assume that a well-written architecture will be implemented as specified. Every critical capability is allocated, configured, tested under representative and degraded conditions, observed in operation, independently evaluated at the relevant decision, corrected when defective, and retained in a reproducible evidence trail.
7.4.1 Assurance organization and separation of duties
Table D5C6A-26. Assurance roles

| Actor | Assurance responsibility | Boundary |

| NHTCA | Integrated transition/program command; master schedule; dependency, wave, risk, continuity, and corrective-action integration | Cannot independently certify its own phase exit |

| DNHA and ARCH owners | Design/build/operate work packages; maintain requirements, evidence, configuration, training, fallback, cost and operational readiness | Accountable for truth of operator evidence and immediate containment |

| RHA/state/tribal compact bodies | Regional execution, capacity planning, local data, compacts/waivers, provider/facility readiness, community engagement | National floors and tribal sovereignty/direct pathways remain binding |

| THDO/HFASB/NHETF | Obligation, disbursement, revenue, reserve, provider-liquidity and fiscal-readiness evidence | Fiscal records reconcile to actuarial/Formula Registry basis |

| NHASB | Independent scorekeeping, formula verification, gate certification, retrospective/sunset review, red team, corrective-effectiveness review | Organizational, data, budget, and conflict safeguards protect independence |

| NHAC/NOPRSL | Rights, safety, equity, privacy, appeal usability, public legitimacy and patient/provider remedy oversight | Can require correction/relief and publish objections; does not operate benefits/payment |

| CHAO | Congressional audit of legality, funding, performance, implementation risk, capture, and reported evidence | Legislative oversight is distinct from executive gate operation |

| A1-HCAC | Expedited enforceable claims, care, payment, rights, and anti-impoundment remedies | Court review remains available as specified; a gate cannot extinguish a claim or right |
THREE-LINE CONTROL  Operators own delivery and first-line controls; independent executive oversight verifies scorekeeping, gates, rights, safety, and repair; Congress and courts provide external audit and enforceable remedy. The lines exchange evidence but do not collapse into one approval chain.
7.4.2 Integrated master schedule, requirements, and configuration
The integrated master schedule decomposes phases into domain work packages, regional waves, milestones, interfaces, resource calendars, test/review events, gates, contingencies, and durable transfers. It maintains a critical path and probabilistic schedule-risk view.
The requirements baseline preserves stakeholder need → PR/SR → ARCH/function/interface/data/formula → VR/test → evidence → gate/decision → operation/metric → risk/corrective-action trace. Orphans and contradictory allocations are release blockers until disposition.
Configuration control covers statute/rule/compact/waiver, architecture, interface, schema/vocabulary, formula, software/model, infrastructure, vendor artifact, procedure, training, notice/appeal, dashboard, and simulation input versions.
Change classification considers operational scope, patient/provider impact, rights/safety/equity, fiscal effect, interoperability, cyber, workforce, supplier/vendor, legal authority, evidence invalidation, migration, communications, and rollback.
The authoritative implementation status is derived from signed evidence and operational data. Presentation decks, milestone declarations, or vendor percentages are views, not the system of record.
7.4.3 Readiness review and verification strategy
Table D5C6A-27. Readiness-review ladder

| Review | Timing | Minimum decision content |

| Architecture baseline review | Before committed implementation baseline | Needs, requirements, ARCH/IF/data allocation, legal authority, assumptions, risks, cost/schedule, alternatives and open issues are coherent |

| Detailed design/configuration review | Before build/procurement or major change | Interfaces, data, formulas, security/privacy, human workflow, testability, vendor exit, capacity, fallback and traceability are complete |

| Test readiness review | Before formal test/demonstration | Procedure, environment, representative users/sites/data, entry/exit, expected output, instruments, defects, safety stop and independent witnesses are ready |

| Operational readiness review | Before wave/pilot/service activation | Staffing/training, facilities/suppliers, payment, records, support, notices/appeals, incident command, downtime/manual path and rollback are ready |

| Phase-gate review | At controlled progression decision | Universal gate package, applicable PH-G evidence, open findings, corrective effectiveness, residual risk, conditions and publication are complete |

| Post-implementation review | After sufficient operating exposure | Benefits/harms, access, cost, safety, equity, rights, workforce, trust, continuity, defects and displacement effects are measured |

| Maturity/sunset review | At P8 or statutory review date | Mature targets, fiscal durability, institutional performance, legal resilience, repair portfolio, function transfer, reauthorization or sunset are independently assessed |
Table D5C6A-28. Verification requirement groups

| Evidence domain | Requirements | Controlled method |

| Trace/metric control | VR-001–005 | Bidirectional trace; metric contract; independent verification; equity stratification; audit self-reported data |

| AI | VR-006–007 | Model-version evidence and protected-group comparison before national deployment |

| Operational rails | VR-008–009 | Operational logs for eligibility/claims/pharmacy/disbursement/uptime; timestamped payment chain |

| Usability/explanations | VR-010–011 | Representative user testing; complete decision-record audit |

| Clinical/access | VR-012–014 | Administrative plus clinical-record safety evidence; result closure; specialist timestamp chain |

| Transition/workforce | VR-015–016 | Pre/post patient continuity; worker eligibility/offer/training/placement/retention |

| Hospitals/drugs | VR-017–018 | Audited finances/disbursement/service/staffing/access; inventory/production/supplier/quality/shortage evidence |

| Legal/public | VR-019–020 | Statute/funding/disbursement/vacancy/litigation evidence; publication/completeness/privacy/reproducibility |

| Adaptation | VR-021–023 | Formula Registry; emergency change control; waiver hypothesis/protection/equity/budget/sunset/evaluation |

| Fiscal/gates/sovereignty | VR-024–027 | Certified fiscal records; independent gate verification; tribal-approved evidence; employer wage/payroll evidence |

| Trust/culture/demonstration | VR-028–030 | Representative trust; validated culture plus workload; scenario/entry/exit/observed outputs/pass-fail |
Verification asks whether the implementation conforms to its controlled specification; validation asks whether the capability solves the stakeholder problem safely and fairly in its actual context. A registry can pass schema tests and still fail validation if people cannot correct identity errors. A claims rail can meet throughput and still fail if providers experience harmful liquidity gaps. A unit can be open and still fail if unmeasured under-referral or workforce overload shifts harm. Both conformance and service validity are therefore required for gate use.
7.4.4 Evidence and corrective-action control
Table D5C6A-29. Machine-usable assurance evidence record

| Field group | Required content |

| identity | evidence_id, requirement_id, phase/gate/wave, scope, owner, verifier, status, timestamps |

| authority/configuration | statute/rule, architecture/interface/data/formula/software/procedure versions, change record |

| method | verification method, protocol, entry/exit, sampling, comparator, uncertainty, equity strata, acceptance rule |

| inputs | source datasets, lineage, quality, exclusions, missingness, audit sample, operational exposure |

| observations | raw/result artifacts, expected/observed outputs, defects, safety events, appeals/complaints, cost/schedule |

| decision | pass/fail/conditional/hold, rationale, conditions, residual risk, accountable acceptance, independent certification |

| repair | finding/corrective-action IDs, containment, owner, due date, effectiveness test, affected-case remedy, closure/reopen |

| publication/retention | public summary, suppression/privacy basis, reproducibility package, retention/legal hold, supersession |
A finding records requirement/configuration, observed evidence, expected condition, affected scope, severity, rights/safety/equity/continuity impact, immediate containment, owner, due date, and gate/operation effect.
Root-cause analysis distinguishes specification, design, implementation, data/formula, training/workflow, resource/capacity, vendor/supplier, governance/incentive, legal, external shock, and detection/assurance failure.
Corrective action identifies the changed control, affected cases, remedy, migration, verification method, observation window, displacement checks, recurrence trigger, and rollback. Closing the task is not closing the finding.
NHASB or the designated independent body verifies effectiveness. Repeated or systemic failure updates the risk/FMEA, formula/rule, roadmap, gate, baseline assumptions, and simulation distributions.
Overdue critical findings, ineffective corrections, or invalid evidence automatically escalate and can hold/reopen affected gates. Management acceptance cannot suppress a legally required remedy or patient-safety action.
Defect escape  defect_escape_rate = material_defects_first_detected_after_release_or_gate / material_defects_detected_for_released_scope
Use severity, detectability, affected population, duration, and remedy burden; a low count may indicate weak detection and is interpreted with reporting/safety-culture evidence.
7.4.5 Supplier, vendor, cyber, and continuity assurance
Critical solicitations and agreements require open interfaces, data portability, source/configuration escrow where appropriate, audit access, incident notification, subcontractor/supply-chain transparency, service continuity, pricing/change control, accessibility, security, performance evidence, and termination assistance.
Critical vendors maintain tested exit plans linked to alternate supplier, insourcing, manual operation, data/model export, licenses, credentials, hardware/spares, training, conversion duration, funding, and rollback. Paper completeness alone does not satisfy SR-ADP-009.
Cyber assurance includes threat modeling, identity/least privilege, segmentation, secure build/dependency control, vulnerability remediation, logging, backup/restore, incident command, failover/offline operation, safety review, public/breach duties, and post-recovery reconciliation.
Continuity exercises combine technology, workforce, supplier, facility, payment, clinical, pharmacy, records, rights, communications, and regional/tribal actors. A technical uptime result does not prove service continuity.
Vendor self-reported evidence is independently sampled under VR-005. Proprietary status does not override audit, safety, rights, Formula Registry, affected-case, court, or public-accountability duties established by law/contract.
7.4.6 Benefits realization, cadence, and public assurance
Table D5C6A-30. Assurance cadence

| Cadence | Evidence reviewed | Control output |

| Continuous/event | Availability, payment, identity, safety, AI, cyber, continuity, formula/version, exception and control-limit alerts | Immediate containment/escalation and immutable event evidence |

| Daily/weekly during waves | Coverage/payment exceptions, liquidity, medication/treatment continuity, capacity, complaints, incidents, rollback indicators | NHTCA incident/wave control; public summary at approved cadence |

| Monthly | Work-package milestone/cost/workforce/quality/risk/configuration/corrective-action status | Integrated program review and reforecast |

| Quarterly | KPP/TPP trends, equity, regional/service-line performance, hospital/benefit/transition/rights dashboards | NHASB/NHAC review and public reporting |

| Annual | Fiscal/operational scorekeeping, formula inventory, vendor exit tests, red-team portfolio, forecast errors, trust/culture, research/innovation | Independent report, Congressional oversight, budget/roadmap update |

| Trigger/sunset | Emergency repair, major variance, high-overturn appeal, trust collapse, legal shock, pilot/waiver end, statutory review | Bounded review/repair/ratification/termination and learning update |
Benefits realization compares observed outcomes with the controlled baseline, comparator, intended mechanism, costs, risks, and distribution. It reports coverage, access, clinical outcomes, safety, equity, household protection, provider/hospital stability, workforce, fiscal position, transition continuity, rights/appeals, trust, cyber resilience, innovation, and unintended displacement separately. No composite score may conceal failure of a mandatory right, safety, equity, continuity, or fiscal constraint.
PUBLIC ASSURANCE INVARIANT  Public reporting preserves metric definitions, denominators, dates, uncertainty, strata, revisions, responsible owners, known limitations, audit history, gate decisions, findings, and corrective status. Privacy suppression is governed and cannot become performance suppression.
7.4.7 Implementation risks and scenario coverage
Table D5C6A-31. Implementation risk allocation

| Risk | Failure mode | Phase/gate | Primary response |

| RISK-EXEC-001 | Executive sabotage, impoundment, vacancy, or refusal blocks implementation | P0–P8 | Mandatory funding/default authority, succession, anti-impoundment remedy, public evidence, legal contingency |

| RISK-FIN-001 | Revenue, reserve, forecast, or cost allocation is insufficient or misleading | P0–P8 / G4 | Certified ledgers, Formula Registry, sensitivity, stabilizers, hold maturity, forecast-error review |

| RISK-CLAIMS-001 | Claims/payment instability harms provider liquidity | P2–P6 / G1/G8 | Provisional/manual Treasury payment, wave hold, reconciliation, provider remedy |

| RISK-UNIT-001 | Unit scale or routing suppresses/strands demand | P4–P8 / G2 | Clinical review, under-referral floor, capacity build, protected escalation, repair/rollback |

| RISK-WF-001 | Workforce shortage or unsafe workload invalidates access plan | P0–P8 / G3 | Safe-capacity constraint, training/retention/scope controls, wave limit, wellbeing evidence |

| RISK-AI-001 | AI drift, opacity, automation bias, or audit gaps cause harm | P2–P8 / G5 | Version validation, human review, subgroup monitoring, suspension, manual fallback, case replay |

| RISK-DATA-001 | Bad identity/data/migration produces eligibility, care, or payment error | P1–P8 / G6/G8 | Provenance, reconciliation, correction, provisional continuity, legacy/manual bridge |

| RISK-CYBER-001 | Cyber outage disrupts essential care/payment | P1–P8 / G6 | Segmentation, failover/offline drills, manual operation, incident command, reconciliation |

| RISK-STATE-001 | State/regional noncooperation creates gaps or inequity | P0–P8 / G8 | Direct federal/tribal path, compact/default terms, protected funding/data/service continuity |

| RISK-TRUST-001 | Unusable rights, poor service, capture, or misinformation collapses trust | P0–P8 / G7 | Independent review, remedy, transparent defect disclosure, service repair, pause/resize waves |

| RISK-LEGAL-001 | Adverse ruling disables authority or interface | P0–P8 | Pre-mapped fallback, alternate authority, severability, continuity orders, repair and return criteria |
Baseline, optimistic, pessimistic, and high-need/high-cost scenarios vary phase duration, task/resource correlation, regional readiness, workforce/pipeline, capacity, adoption, utilization, payment performance, fiscal receipts, and implementation learning.
Named red-team scenarios include workforce shortage, rural stress, cyber outage, AI failure, data mismatch, pharmacy shortage/vendor exit, hospital distress, state resistance, legal/impoundment shock, employer noncompliance, pandemic/public-health surge, and trust collapse.
Scenario outputs include phase/wave/gate state, people and services affected, delay, backlog, continuity/harm, rights/remedy, provider/facility liquidity, workforce burden, fiscal/reserve state, transition and recurring cost, corrective-action effectiveness, and trust.
A scenario result cannot count unmet demand, suppressed referrals, delayed assessments, unavailable providers, missing records, unpaid obligations, or unreported incidents as savings or successful throughput.
8. Financing and Cost
8.1 Final Cost Estimate
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: The public needs one controlled statement of the central estimate, plausible range, transition envelope, and what those numbers do and do not claim. Why this structure: Costs, transition outlays, revenue, and reserves are separated to prevent double counting and to expose who bears fiscal risk. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes final cost estimate explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | State and reconcile the final framework cost position across mature, transition, annual, per-capita, GDP-share, public-budget, total-system, point-of-care, gross/net, capital and reserve views. |

| System entities | ARCH-HFASB; ARCH-NHASB; ARCH-CHAO; ARCH-NHA-TRUST; ARCH-NHETF; ARCH-THDO; DNHA domain owners; NHTCA; residual private actors; patients/employers. |

| Assumptions | ASM-015; D6B-DEC-01–03/05–07/11; OI-049–051/058; real 2024 dollars; framework figures are model assumptions unless independently sourced. |

| Data / parameters | CP-TOT-001–010; CP-POP; CP-FIN; CP-OFF; category cost events; obligations/outlays/reserves; population and GDP scenario denominators. |

| Requirements / performance | PR-CST-001–004/006–010; KPP-C1–C8; VR-002–005/024; IF-024–025. |

| Principal risks | Boundary mismatch; transfer/reserve double count; incompatible denominators; offsets without causality; point-of-care confusion; transition/mature mixing; false precision. |

| Simulation implication | Produce time-indexed public and total-system costs, per-capita/GDP ratios, category/region/group distributions, gross additions/offsets, transition/capital/reserve states, uncertainty, comparator difference and consistency flags. |
The final framework is capacity-first, safety-first, and transition-protected rather than a maximum-savings design. Its mature cost is a controlled total-system assumption, not simply a federal budget estimate. Public financing replaces much—but not necessarily every dollar—of private premium, patient, employer, supplemental, substitute, noncovered, and administrative flows. The accounting model therefore consolidates economic cost while preserving the identities needed for appropriations, cash management, incidence, reserves, and transition.
Table D6B-5. Final controlled cost position

| Quantity | Controlled value | Classification | Interpretation |

| Mature steady-state total-system cost | $4.75T/year | Final framework assumption; real 2024 dollars | Central model control after transition-specific functions are removed/transferred |

| Plausible mature range | $4.30T–$5.25T/year | Final framework uncertainty range | Scenario/calibration envelope; not a confidence interval until method is specified |

| Transition/implementation | $1.2T–$2.0T over 10–12 years | Final framework cumulative envelope | Incremental time-limited cost; profile and allocation remain OI-052 |

| First-decade transition-adjusted | $4.90T–$5.05T/year approximately | Final framework annual range | Operating ramp plus transition and recoveries; not a mature steady-state value |
CONTROLLED INTERPRETATION  The earlier annual estimate is excluded from final framework content. The $4.75T central value and related ranges are specifications to be tested and calibrated, not claims that the system has achieved those costs.
8.1.1 Cost states and views
Table D6B-6. Cost states

| State | Meaning | Controlled value | Status |

| mature_operating | Recurring annual total-system cost after transition functions and temporary stabilization are removed or transferred | $4.75T/year central; $4.30T–$5.25T plausible range | FA/model constraint |

| transition_cumulative | Incremental implementation, migration, continuity, stabilization, buildout, and wind-down cost over the program | $1.2T–$2.0T over 10–12 years | FA envelope; allocation open |

| first_decade_annual | Annual total-system cost during early operations plus time-indexed transition cost and recoveries | $4.90T–$5.05T/year approximately | FA range; not mature plus uniform amortization |

| capital | Construction, equipment, software/platform, manufacturing, facility, and other asset creation | No controlled total yet | MP/OI-049/052 |

| reserve | Eligible stabilization/shock/endowment stocks and authority available for defined draws | 6-month Gate 4 floor; 12-month maturity target for volatile exposure | TG/stock; not annual cost |

| net_public_outlay | Treasury disbursements and other public cash outlays net of recoveries/reconciliation for the selected period | Derived | MP/output; not equal to total-system cost |

| total_system | Public plus residual private plus patient-paid economic cost within the health-system boundary | Derived by consolidation | CP-TOT-001; excludes pure internal transfers |
Table D6B-7. Reconciled cost views

| View | Boundary | Primary parameters | Use |

| Total-system | Public outlay + residual private + patient-paid health cost; eliminate internal public transfers | CP-TOT-001/004–006 | Primary $4.75T control view |

| Public budget | Obligations/outlays by trust, agency, program, function, appropriation and payer rail | CP-TOT-004; CP-FIN | Budget authority and cash needs; not total economic cost |

| Operating | Recurring services, administration, readiness, workforce, maintenance and other annual operations | C_operating | Excludes time-limited transition and reserve stocks |

| Capital | Gross asset creation, replacement and expansion; cash and depreciation/amortization views both retained | C_capital | No double count with operating depreciation or transition buildout |

| Transition | Incremental time-limited conversion cost net of recoveries | CP-TRN; C_transition | One event identity and sunset/transfer |

| Household/employer | Premium, contribution, tax, wage, point-of-care and benefit-flow incidence by group | CP-FIN-017–019; CP-TOT-006 | Economic incidence distinct from statutory remitter |

| Regional/equity | Cost, receipts, access, service, burden and transfers by region/population | CP-POP; CP-FIN; category CPs | Equalization and distribution; national average cannot hide burden |
8.1.2 Master cost and consolidation equations
Master cost  C_total(t) = C_hospital + C_clinical + C_units + C_LTC + C_drugs + C_devices_labs_diagnostics + C_behavioral + C_DVH + C_EMS + C_public_health + C_info_cyber_AI + C_governance_oversight + C_R&D + C_education_workforce + C_transition_net - C_offsets
Each term has one category owner and shared-cost allocation rule. At maturity, C_transition_net is zero or only residual legally defined closeout; enduring functions transfer to operating categories.
Offsets  C_offsets(t) = admin + PBM + revenue_cycle + debt_collection + ED_diversion + avoidable_admission + readmission + drug/device_purchasing + manufacturing + duplicate_testing + specialist_substitution + prevention/early_detection + other_verified_offsets
CP-OFF interactions are modeled jointly. Gross additions and gross savings remain visible before netting.
Total-system consolidation  C_total_system = C_public_outlay + C_residual_private + C_patient_paid - internal_public_transfers - duplicate_reimbursements
Taxes and contributions finance cost but are not additional system cost; reserve contributions and draws move assets unless consumed by an external obligation.
Transition-adjusted annual  C_TA(t) = C_operating(t) + C_transition_net(t) + capital_cash_adjustment(t) + residual_private(t) + patient_paid(t) - consolidation_eliminations(t)
The first-decade range is generated from the time profile, not uniform division of the cumulative envelope.
8.1.3 Per-capita and GDP-share coherence
Per-capita  CP-TOT-002(t) = C_total_system(t) / population_denominator(t)
At $4.75T, the exact $13,300 target implies a denominator of about 357.1 million. The selected model population and coverage definition must reconcile this result under OI-050; the target is not silently changed here.
GDP share  CP-TOT-003(t) = C_total_system(t) / nominal_or_real_consistent_GDP(t)
A $4.75T numerator at 15.2% implies a consistent GDP denominator of about $31.25T in the same price/time basis. Actual scenario inputs must pass currency/base-year consistency tests.

| Check | Equation | Required disposition |

| Central per-capita | $4.75T / selected population | Compare with PR-CST-003/KPP-C2; record conflict, tolerance and authority |

| Range per-capita | $4.30T–$5.25T / scenario population | Report distribution/range, not one implied population |

| Central GDP share | $4.75T / scenario GDP | Compare with <=15.2%; maintain matched price year |

| Public budget vs total | public outlay / total-system cost | Report public share and residual flows; do not equate automatically |

| Point-of-care vs economic cost | patient payment / covered or total cost | Near-zero covered-care price does not imply zero economic cost |

8.1.5 Risk, uncertainty, and simulation behavior
Every reported value carries price year, time state, scope, payer/economic view, central/range/distribution, source/calibration status, formula version and consolidation rule.
The model reports gross added spending, gross offsets and net difference versus a separately versioned existing-system comparator. A baseline change never rewrites framework cost history.
Utilization, morbidity, workforce, capacity, compensation, prices, technology, regional need, transition timing, revenue, GDP and offsets are correlated scenario inputs; range endpoints are not assembled by independently selecting every extreme.
Cost savings fail validation when access, safety, rights, equity, continuity, workforce, quality, payment or fiscal constraints fail. Suppressed/unmet demand and unpaid obligations are not savings.
Reserve authority and balances appear in fiscal capacity outputs; only contributions, investment/administration, external obligations, losses and consumed draws enter appropriate flow/cost views.
8.2 Mature Annual Cost by Category
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: A total cost conceals which services expand, which administrative costs fall, and where uncertainty is concentrated; category-level accounting exposes those choices. Why this structure: Costs, transition outlays, revenue, and reserves are separated to prevent double counting and to expose who bears fiscal risk. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes mature annual cost by category explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the 14 mandatory mature cost categories, their CP-family mappings, owners, boundaries, shared-cost/offset rules, calibration records, and reconciliation to the controlled mature total. |

| System entities | DNHA domain owners; HFASB; THDO; NHA-TRUST; NHETF; NHASB; CHAO; NHAC; providers/facilities/pharmacies; residual private actors. |

| Assumptions | D6B-DEC-01–05/07; OI-049/051/058/059; category values are model parameters constrained by total, not authoritative allocations. |

| Data / parameters | CP-HOSP/CLIN/UNIT/LTC/RX/DX/BH/DVH/EMS/PH/IT/CLM/GOV/RD/EDU/OFF/TOT; cost.event; operational quantities and performance data. |

| Requirements / performance | PR-CST-002–004/006/010; allocated SR/KPP/TPP; VR-005/008/012–018/020/024. |

| Principal risks | Category overlap; missing shared allocation; false savings; capacity-free costing; underfunded readiness; offsets counted twice; residual private omission; legitimacy cost dilution. |

| Simulation implication | Represent each category by time/region/population/capacity/service/cost-state; calibrate quantities/prices/distributions; constrain aggregate; link offsets/outcomes and test sensitivity/correlation. |
The mature category model is a chart of accounts and simulation partition, not a claim that the source package supplies a final dollar budget for each domain. Each category has an explicit boundary and owner, while hospital, workforce, information, capital, readiness, public health, and other shared costs use controlled allocation drivers. The model solves or calibrates category values within the $4.75T central constraint and $4.30T–$5.25T range, then reports whether service, capacity, quality, safety, equity, rights and fiscal constraints are feasible at those values.

Mature total constraint  sum_i C_mature[MC-i, t=P8_mature] = 4.75T central, with plausible aggregate range 4.30T–5.25T
Category ranges are jointly calibrated and correlated. Their independent low/high endpoints need not and generally should not sum to the aggregate endpoints.
Category cost  C_i = service_volume_i x unit_cost_i + staffed_readiness_i + capital_charge_i + administration_i + other_boundary_i - verified_offsets_allocated_i
The model preserves gross components. Readiness and low-volume essential capacity are not forced into volume prices.
8.2.2 Category record and shared-cost allocation
Table D6B-11. Machine-usable category record

| Field group | Required content |

| identity/scope | category_id; CP family; owner; included services/assets; explicit exclusions; shared-cost allocation rule |

| dimensions | time, phase, region, population, provider/facility/product, unit/specialty, payer/public-private and cost state |

| quantity/price | service/capacity volume, unit cost or compensation, readiness/capital, utilization, morbidity, access and quality constraints |

| accounting | authority, obligation, outlay, accrual, asset/depreciation, transfer elimination, residual private/patient component and recovery |

| baseline/offset | comparator cost, gross addition, offset ID, causal mechanism, lag, interaction, rebound, displaced cost and net result |

| uncertainty | central/range/distribution, correlation group, scenario sensitivity, calibration source, evidence date/version and confidence |

| assurance | formula version, reconciliation tests, audit sample, equity/distribution analysis, owner/verifier and public release |
A directly attributable cost is assigned to one category at source. A shared cost uses one registered driver—such as staffed FTE, transactions, storage/compute, square footage, utilization, population, readiness, or benefit share—and retains a shared-pool identity.
Clinical labor embedded in a hospital, unit, public-health program or benefit may be reported by workforce role as a secondary view, but the consolidated primary category owns the dollar once.
Capital cash outlay, placed-in-service asset, depreciation/amortization, maintenance and financing flow are separate fields. The chosen total-system view states which is included for the period.
Regional equalization transfers do not create national cost; the service/capacity purchased by the recipient does. Internal transfers are eliminated while regional sources/uses remain visible.
Residual private and patient-paid spending is mapped to the same service categories where possible and separately tagged by payer/status so total-system consolidation is complete.
8.2.3 Gross additions, offsets, and displacement
Table D6B-12. Offset families and verification controls

| Parameters | Mechanism | Cost displaced | Control |

| CP-OFF-001/003/004/017/020 | Administrative simplification | Legacy private administration, provider revenue cycle, debt collection, interoperability and employer administration | Deduct only displaced resource cost; transition overlap and redeployed labor remain explicit |

| CP-OFF-002/008/009/010 | Purchasing/manufacturing | PBM removal, drug negotiation, public manufacturing and device/supply purchasing | Price decline, volume, quality, shortage, capital/R&D and supplier response jointly modeled |

| CP-OFF-005/006/007/012/013/014/019 | Care-pathway improvement | ED diversion, avoidable admission/readmission, specialist visit substitution, early detection, prevention and crisis diversion | Do not count avoided utilization without capacity, clinical outcome, timing and substitution evidence |

| CP-OFF-011/016 | Information/AI productivity | Duplicate testing and AI productivity | Require validated use, labor/capacity realization, safety/equity and rebound treatment |

| CP-OFF-015 | Fraud/extraction recovery | Recovered or avoided improper/extractive payments | Separate recovered cash, future avoidance, enforcement cost and contested liability |

| CP-OFF-018 | Home-first LTC | Difference between safe preferred settings | No saving if hours, caregiver support, housing/equipment, safety or beneficiary preference are unmet |
Net savings versus baseline  CP-TOT-008(t) = C_baseline_comparator(t) - C_framework_total_system(t)
Comparator and framework use matched scope, price year, population, morbidity and time state. Positive savings do not validate the framework when mandatory non-cost constraints fail.
Gross-to-net  C_framework_net = C_baseline + CP-TOT-009(gross additions) - CP-TOT-010(gross savings)
This identity is reported with interaction terms; gross savings are not simply summed when mechanisms overlap.
8.2.4 Legitimacy, safety, and governance allocation
PR-CST-010 requires 0.25%–0.50% of annual National Health Assurance spending after Phase 6 for legitimacy, safety, patient rights, transparency, appeals, and trust infrastructure. This is a tagged funding floor/range across eligible CP-GOV, CP-CLM and CP-IT events—not a statement that all governance, claims, courts, clinical safety, cyber, provider quality, or adaptation costs fit inside that percentage. OI-059 must define inclusions and denominator before gate or budget enforcement.
Legitimacy allocation  legitimacy_share = eligible_tagged_legitimacy_safety_rights_transparency_appeals_trust_spending / annual_NHA_spending
Target 0.25%–0.50% after P6. General category totals remain separately reported; no cost is tagged twice.

8.3 Transition and Implementation Cost
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Transition spending is temporary, uneven, and partly substitutive; treating it as a permanent add-on or double-counting displaced spending would distort fiscal conclusions. Why this structure: Costs, transition outlays, revenue, and reserves are separated to prevent double counting and to expose who bears fiscal risk. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes transition and implementation cost explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Specify the $1.2T–$2.0T transition/implementation envelope as a cost-loaded work-package, phase/wave, ledger, transfer-to-operations, contingency, recovery and assurance model over 10–12 years. |

| System entities | ARCH-NHTCA and suboffices; THDO; HFASB; NHETF/Transition Protection Fund; DNHA domain owners; RHAs/states/tribal nations; NHASB/NHAC/CHAO. |

| Assumptions | ASM-010; ASM-019 inherited transition exclusivity; D6B-DEC-02/06/07; OI-043/052; continuity and liquidity cannot be cut to meet the envelope silently. |

| Data / parameters | CP-TRN-001–020; transition-tagged CP-UNIT/IT/RX/DX/EDU/GOV; cost.event; work packages; obligations/outlays/reserves/recoveries; PH-P0–P8; gates. |

| Requirements / performance | PR-CST-005; PR-TRN-001–010; PR-SCH; VR-015/016/022–027/030; KPP-T1/T2/W1; TPP-12.1/12.5. |

| Principal risks | Underfunded continuity; reserve/outlay confusion; recurring cost hidden as transition; shared asset double count; cost/schedule overrun; failed transfer; premature sunset; regional inequity. |

| Simulation implication | Model work-package cost/time/resource distributions, phase/wave dependencies, contingency, reserve authority and net outlay, recoveries, failure/rollback, transfer to operation, cumulative envelope and annual transition-adjusted cost. |
Transition cost is the incremental cost of moving from fragmented legacy arrangements to the public architecture while protecting active care, medication, provider liquidity, hospitals, pharmacies, workers, records, appeals, jurisdictions and employers. The envelope is not a discretionary pool and not a mature annual category. Each dollar is attached to an approved work package, deliverable or protected obligation, and each enduring capability transfers to a mature operating category when service-ready.

8.3.2 Cost-event ledger and non-additivity
Table D6B-16. Required transition cost-event fields

| Field group | Required content |

| event identity | cost_event_id, workstream/work package, phase/wave, region/population, owner, supplier/provider and configuration |

| classification | incremental transition, capital, recurring operating, reserve authority, contribution, draw, recovery or transfer; only one primary classification |

| authority/funding | statute/appropriation/contract/compact, funding source/account, obligation authority, committed/obligated/outlay/accrued state |

| amount/time | real-2024 central/range/distribution, nominal cash view, period/profile, escalation basis, contingency and uncertainty |

| deliverable/benefit | asset/capability/continuity obligation, acceptance evidence, service-ready transfer, useful life and operating owner |

| dependency/risk | predecessors, capacity, gate, risk/FMEA, schedule sensitivity, fallback, rollback and cancellation/termination exposure |

| reconciliation | duplicate check, recovery, provisional-payment settlement, reserve release, capitalization, operating transfer and closeout |
Cumulative transition  C_transition_cumulative = sum(unique incremental transition outlays and accruals) - recoveries - duplicate reclassifications
Reserve authority and unconsumed balance are not automatically cost. Capital and operating transfers retain lineage so the same asset/service is not counted again.
Net provider liquidity  CP-TRN-006 = provisional_liquidity_disbursements - reconciled_recoveries - duplicate_or_invalid_payments
CP-TRN-005 is authority/available capacity, not net cost. Legitimate provider payment for covered care is classified to the underlying service when due.
Annual profile  C_transition_net(t) = committed_incremental_work(t) + continuity_stabilization(t) + failure_repair(t) - recoveries(t)
Profile is generated by resource-loaded work packages, not straight-line amortization. Cancellation and delay may lower near-term outlay while increasing harm or later cost.
8.3.3 Phase loading, gates, and contingency

| Phase band | Dominant transition activities | Cost-control evidence |

| P0–P1 | Statute/command, governing bodies, registries/identity/cyber/legal defaults, baseline inventories, assurance | Authorities, staffing, design/configuration, cost baseline, risk and readiness |

| P2–P3 | Pharmacy/claims/public coverage Wave I, liquidity, medication and data/legacy bridges | Operational logs, continuity, payment, reconciliation and Gate 1/7/8 evidence |

| P4–P5 | Hospital/unit/specialist pilots, workforce/scope/education scale, regional compacts | Representative pilots, scale/terminate, capacity and service-line evidence |

| P6–P7 | National coverage/cost-sharing conversion and expanded-benefit capacity/waves | Gates 2/3/5/6/7/8, provider/service continuity and burden |

| P8/closeout | Residual migration, mature manufacturing/mesh/payment, maturity evidence and function transfer | Gate 4, open-duty transfer, asset acceptance, final reconciliation and sunset |
Each work package maintains base cost, schedule/resource uncertainty, identified-risk allowance, management contingency, escalation convention and unallocated reserve separately. Contingency use requires a trigger and change record.
A gate hold preserves care/payment/continuity funding. Cost pressure cannot remove a mandatory fallback; it changes schedule, scope of new deployment, resource plan or authorized funding subject to rights and safety.
Failed pilots, cyber events, legal shocks, state resistance, vendor exit, workforce shortages and trust repair create scenario-specific repair/rollback costs. Those draws remain linked to the triggering risk and affected cases.
A workstream exits transition only after the operating owner accepts the asset/capability, recurring funding/staffing exist, records/liabilities are transferred, exceptions are resolved or owned, and independent evidence certifies the scope.
NHTCA sunset cannot erase open payments, appeals, liabilities, records, contracts, reserves or continuity duties; each transfers to a named durable custodian with budget and authority.
8.3.4 Transition cost parameters and simulation

8.4 Financing Model
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Redirected premiums and public spending will not automatically become stable progressive revenue; financing needs defined layers, incidence rules, and a protected payment path. Why this structure: Costs, transition outlays, revenue, and reserves are separated to prevent double counting and to expose who bears fiscal risk. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes financing model explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the dedicated progressive financing architecture, receipt/obligation/disbursement lifecycle, trust flows, state/local and employer contributions, wealth/high-income/rent layers, residual backstop, incidence, wage pass-through, legal fallback and Formula Registry controls. |

| System entities | ARCH-CONG; ARCH-TREAS; ARCH-IRS; ARCH-HFASB; ARCH-NHA-TRUST; ARCH-NHETF; ARCH-THDO; ARCH-EPTO; DNHA; states/localities; tribal nations; employers/workers; NHASB/CHAO/NHAC. |

| Assumptions | D6B-DEC-08–12; OI-053–055/057/058; financing changes who pays but not the total economic cost by itself; statutory remitter and economic incidence differ. |

| Data / parameters | CP-FIN-001–010/017–020; obligations, receipts, transfers, disbursements, payroll, employer baseline/wages, household incidence, GDP/economic conditions and formula versions. |

| Requirements / performance | PR-CST-006/008/009; SR-IF-008; TPP-EMP1; KPP-C5/C7/C8; VR-019/024/025/027; IF-024–025. |

| Principal risks | Revenue shortfall; avoidance/leakage; legal invalidation; regressive pass-through; employer noncompliance; state failure; timing mismatch; trust diversion; duplicate financing; opaque incidence. |

| Simulation implication | Model legally due and collected revenue by layer/time/group, behavioral/legal uncertainty, transfers/accounts, obligations/outlays, employer/worker/household incidence, sufficiency, stabilizer, fallback and distribution. |
The financing model converts fragmented premiums, public programs, employer benefit spending and patient exposure into a dedicated public financing structure. It does not assume that taxes are cost in addition to the care they finance. The model follows cash and incidence separately: who remits, who economically bears, who receives health benefits or wage/premium relief, which account holds the receipt, which authority certifies an obligation, and when Treasury disburses.

LAYERING RULE  A broad backstop is residual. The certified model tests redirected spending, maintenance, employer and progressive dedicated layers, collection repair, transfers and lawful reserve response before imposing ordinary-household burden, while preserving mandatory obligations throughout.

Table D6B-20. Financing transaction states

| State | Accountable actor | Required record | Control |

Dedicated receipts  R_dedicated(t) = federal_redirect + state_local + employer + extreme_wealth + high_income_capital + health_rent + activated_backstop
Each component records legally due, collected cash, refunds, timing, administration cost, leakage, uncertainty and legal state. Transfers between accounts are not new receipts.
Revenue sufficiency  KPP-C5(t) = available_dedicated_receipts_for_period / certified_obligations_for_period
Maturity target >=100%; Gate 4 floor >=98%. Available receipts and certified obligations require matched period, accrual/cash convention and legally usable funds.
Collection efficiency  KPP-C7 = certified_collections_received / certified_legally_due_wealth_financing
Target >=92%. Refunds, disputes, timing, enforcement, avoidance/evasion and court-disabled liability are separately classified.
8.4.3 State, tribal, employer, worker, and household treatment
State/local maintenance contributions use a statutory formula with fiscal-capacity/equalization and hardship/default rules. Services continue while disputes proceed; state noncooperation activates direct federal administration/funding as authorized.
Tribal funding, federal trust duties, direct compacts and data governance are not netted into a state contribution in a way that conditions or reduces federal obligations. Tribal-approved evidence is required under VR-026.
The Employer Health Assurance Contribution has a predictable base/rate and payroll interface set by later statute. Core legacy premium cessation, contribution liability, employer net savings, worker wage pass-through and restitution are independently measured.
Worker premium relief is a household benefit flow; wage pass-through is compensation; employer contribution is a receipt; employer net savings is an economic result. The model never treats one as proof of another.
Ordinary-household protection uses economic incidence, not only statutory remitter. Credits, exemptions, relief/refund, wage/price effects, health benefits, point-of-care reduction and subgroup burden are included.

| Field group | Required content |

| unit | household tax unit, worker, employer, business, wealth holder, region/state/tribe and sector |

| baseline | premium/employer benefit spending, taxes, wages, point-of-care spending, public benefits and existing program financing |

| statutory flow | payer/remitter, base, rate, liability, credit/exemption/refund, contribution and timing |

| economic incidence | wage, price, return/profit, employment, benefit and tax capitalization assumptions with uncertainty |

| health benefit flow | premium relief, covered benefit value, point-of-care reduction, medical-debt effect and access/utilization change |

| distribution | income/wealth/age/disability/race/ethnicity/language/rurality/region/household/employer size where lawful |

| protection tests | incremental burden share, wage pass-through, employer net savings, hardship, liquidity and subgroup adverse effect |
Ordinary taxpayer protection  KPP-C8 = incremental_financing_burden_on_defined_ordinary_households / total_incremental_financing_burden
Target <=5% at maturity. 'Ordinary household,' incremental baseline, incidence assumptions and denominator remain OI-053/057 and require public distributional testing.
Employer wage pass-through  TPP-EMP1 = compliant_employers_or_covered_workers_under_approved_attribution / eligible_employers_or_workers
Target >=95%. The statutory unit, baseline benefit spending, timing, collective-bargaining treatment and attribution method remain OI-055.
8.4.4 Formula Registry, legal contingency, and assurance
Every base, rate, bracket, exemption, credit, apportionment, maintenance, employer, incidence, sufficiency, collection, reserve, stabilizer and transfer formula is registered with authority, variables, data, tests, effective date, notice, appeal/correction and rollback/fallback.
If a financing authority is enjoined or invalidated, the legal contingency matrix activates only a preauthorized alternative. The system records disabled yield, replacement yield/time, reserve bridge, distributional change, affected obligations and return condition.
HFASB certifies obligations, receipts, reserve position, forecasts and triggers; Treasury/IRS assess and collect; THDO disburses certified obligations; NHASB independently reproduces; CHAO audits; NHAC reviews rights/equity; courts remedy unlawful nonpayment/interference.
Public fiscal reports distinguish due, collected, refunded, transferred, obligated, accrued, outlaid, reserved, drawn, recovered and residual balance by source/account/time, with uncertainty, revisions and privacy controls.

8.5 Fiscal Sustainability and Reserve Model
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Healthcare demand and revenue fluctuate differently; reserves and automatic stabilizers are needed so recessions or shocks do not force immediate care cuts. Why this structure: Costs, transition outlays, revenue, and reserves are separated to prevent double counting and to expose who bears fiscal risk. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes fiscal sustainability and reserve model explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define obligation/revenue sufficiency, operating stabilization, shock reserve, permanent endowment, volatile exposure, draw/replenishment, stabilizer triggers, stress scenarios, Gate 4 and maturity certification. |

| System entities | ARCH-HFASB; ARCH-NHETF; ARCH-NHA-TRUST; ARCH-TREAS/IRS/THDO; ARCH-NHASB; ARCH-CHAO; A1-HCAC; DNHA/NHTCA; Congress. |

| Assumptions | D6B-DEC-07–09/11/12; OI-056/057/060; reserves protect obligations and continuity, not conceal structural underfunding or bypass appropriations law. |

| Data / parameters | CP-FIN-011–016/020; certified obligations/receipts; reserve assets/liabilities/liquidity; volatile exposure; economic/health shocks; forecasts; Formula Registry; PH-G4 evidence. |

| Requirements / performance | PR-CST-006–009; PR-SCH-014; SR-IF-008; KPP-C5–C8; VR-019/021/024/025; IF-024–025. |

| Principal risks | Structural deficit masked by draw; illiquid/overvalued assets; trigger delay; procyclical replenishment; regressive stabilizer; legal/impoundment shock; account commingling; false maturity certification. |

| Simulation implication | Model account balances, asset eligibility/haircuts/returns/liquidity, receipts/obligations, volatile exposure, trigger states/actions, draws/replenishment, legal delay, burden, service continuity and stress recovery. |
Fiscal sustainability means that legally available dedicated receipts and eligible reserves can satisfy certified obligations across normal and stressed conditions without shifting unacceptable burden to ordinary households or permitting silent care/payment failure. It is not a single balanced-budget snapshot. The model distinguishes a timing mismatch from a structural gap, operating stabilization from a severe shock, and a reserve stock from annual cost. It also preserves direct Treasury and judicial/default continuity when executive interference—not economics—causes nonpayment.
8.5.1 Fund and account architecture
Table D6B-23. Fiscal accounts

| Account | Owner | Purpose | Boundary | Assurance |

| Core entitlement | ARCH-NHA-TRUST | Certified covered-care obligations and mandatory payment authority | Receipts/transfers matched to obligations; not a discretionary reserve | ARCH-HFASB/CHAO; A1-HCAC remedy |

| Operating stabilization/equalization | ARCH-NHETF | Short-horizon revenue/obligation variance and regional equalization | Liquid eligible assets; controlled draw/replenishment | ARCH-HFASB/NHASB/CHAO |

| Shock reserve | ARCH-NHETF | Specified recession, pandemic, disaster, cyber, legal or revenue shock | Separate trigger, balance, draw, recovery and after-action review | ARCH-HFASB/CHAO |

| Permanent health endowment | ARCH-NHETF | Long-horizon resilience and authorized earnings | Principal, earnings, liquidity and intergenerational rules separate | ARCH-HFASB/CHAO; OI-060 |

Period sufficiency  sufficiency(t) = legally_available_dedicated_receipts(t) + authorized_current_period_transfers(t) / certified_obligations(t)
Parentheses are applied as (receipts + transfers) / obligations. Maturity KPP-C5 >=100%; Gate 4 floor >=98%. Reserve draws are disclosed separately even when available for payment.
Structural balance  structural_balance = cyclically_adjusted_recurring_receipts - recurring_certified_obligations
A recurring negative value cannot be cured permanently by reserve draw. Assumptions and adjustment method are registered and stress-tested.
8.5.2 Volatile exposure and reserve adequacy
Volatile revenue exposure  VRE_12m = sum_s expected_12m_receipt_s x stress_loss_fraction_s x liquidity_timing_factor_s
Revenue classes, correlated stress, horizon and factors remain OI-056. The denominator excludes stable/guaranteed receipts only under an independently verified rule.
Reserve months  reserve_months = 12 x eligible_liquid_stabilization_assets / VRE_12m
If VRE is defined as annual exposure. Gate 4 floor >=6 months; KPP-C6 maturity target >=12 months. Asset haircuts, encumbrances and account purpose are applied.
Replenishment gap  reserve_gap = max(target_eligible_balance - eligible_balance, 0)
The replenishment plan balances time, economic conditions, service obligations and ordinary-household burden; it does not require destabilizing procyclical collection automatically.

| Control | Gate 4 floor | P8 maturity | Interpretation |

| Dedicated revenue sufficiency | >=98% certified obligations | >=100% obligations | Floor permits certification decision only with all other constraints and protected continuity |

| Stabilization reserve | >=6 months volatile exposure | >=12 months volatile exposure | Eligible liquid balance after haircuts; not authority alone |

| Wealth collection efficiency | Approved floor under OI-057 | >=92% legally due | Use due/collected/refund/dispute timing; not nominal forecast alone |

| Ordinary-household burden | Approved protection under OI-057 | <=5% incremental burden share | Economic incidence and relief included |
8.5.3 Stabilizer states and funding-trigger ladder
Table D6B-24. Stabilizer lifecycle

| State | Entry condition | Authorized posture |

| normal | Certified receipts meet forecast/obligations; reserve path at or above plan | Ordinary scheduled financing and reserve contribution |

| watch | Forecast error, collection, economic or obligation indicator approaches registered limit | Increase monitoring; restrict nonessential new commitments; prepare progressive actions |

| corrective | Sufficiency/reserve path breaches early threshold but continuity is not yet threatened | Progressive revenue/collection correction, transfers, cost-control repair and bounded reserve use |

| stress | Material revenue/obligation shock or reserve draw is required | Shock/operating draw, statutory progressive stabilizer, mandatory payment protection and public certification |

| emergency | Immediate risk to mandatory payment, care continuity or fiscal legality | Emergency lawful funding/disbursement, court/default remedies, temporary correction and daily assurance |

| recovery | Shock abates and obligations are current but reserve/forecast position remains impaired | Time-bounded replenishment and rollback of temporary measures subject to burden/service tests |

| restored | Sufficiency, reserve trajectory and corrective effectiveness meet restoration criteria | Return to normal; after-action/forecast-error review; update formulas/scenarios |
Table D6B-25. Ordered response ladder

| Step | Trigger | Action | Guard |

| 1. Forecast/collection repair | Variance or collection efficiency trigger | Audit base/administration/leakage, accelerate lawful collection, correct forecast/formula | No benefit/payment reduction; burden/equity review |

| 2. Internal transfer/equalization | Timing or regional mismatch with adequate consolidated resources | Authorized NHA-TRUST/NHETF transfer and regional equalization | Transfer eliminated in consolidated cost; restore account plan |

| 3. Operating reserve draw | Temporary certified shortfall within operating trigger | Draw liquid eligible stabilization balance | Floor, purpose, amount, expiry, replenishment and publication |

| 4. Progressive stabilizer | Persistent/forecast shortfall after prior controls | Adjust authorized progressive wealth/high-income/capital/rent layers within statutory bounds | Formula Registry, legal fallback, incidence and ordinary-household test |

| 5. Shock reserve | Specified severe economic/health/legal/operational shock | Draw shock reserve and activate emergency continuity funding | Named shock, protected obligations, after-action and replenishment |

| 6. Broad backstop | Residual legally certified shortfall after progressive/reserve response | Activate bounded broad contribution/assessment | KPP-C8 <=5%, relief/refund, cap, expiry, review and deactivation |

| 7. Judicial/default continuity | Impoundment, unlawful refusal, failed quorum or disabled authority | Deemed/default apportionment, direct THDO, A1-HCAC/district court and successor authority | Public evidence; no silent lapse of obligation |
NO AUTOMATIC SERVICE CUT  A fiscal trigger cannot silently reduce covered benefits, delay certified clean obligations, weaken rights/safety, or redefine unmet capacity as savings. Any lawful benefit-boundary change follows its own transparent evidence, notice, appeal and repair process.
8.5.4 Drawdown, replenishment, and investment control
A draw record identifies account, trigger, authority, amount, asset/liquidity source, protected obligations, forecast horizon, alternatives, burden/equity, expiry, replenishment and independent certification.
Operating stabilization addresses timing/ordinary variance; shock reserve addresses named severe events; endowment principal/earnings follow separate law. Account commingling or retroactive relabeling is prohibited.
Eligible assets are valued with market/liquidity/credit/concentration haircuts and encumbrances. Reported reserve adequacy uses realizable eligible value, not gross authorization, face value or inaccessible assets.
Replenishment uses a registered plan with economic-state and service-protection controls. Temporary revenue measures deactivate or review at defined criteria; emergency authority cannot become permanent by inaction.
Investment governance specifies fiduciary duty, risk/return/liquidity, prohibited conflicts, custody, benchmark, ethics, voting/stewardship, audit, public reporting and contingency. OI-060 controls the permanent endowment design.
8.5.5 Stress testing, Gate 4, and maturity certification
Table D6B-26. Required fiscal stress scenarios

| Scenario | Name | Injection | Required outputs |

| SCN-WEALTH-LOW | Progressive revenue underperformance | Collection efficiency/leakage and receipts fall | Sufficiency, reserve months, layer yield, household burden, delay/cost and legal fallback |

| SCN-PESS [recession injection] | Macroeconomic recession | Payroll/income receipts fall while need/utilization and provider stress rise | Obligations, receipts, unemployment incidence, draws, services and recovery horizon |

| SCN-PANDEMIC | Public-health surge | Care/public-health/drug/EMS/hospital costs rise with operational disruption | Shock draw, capacity, continuity, morbidity/mortality, fiscal and replenishment |

| SCN-LEGAL | Financing authority invalidation | One major revenue mechanism is enjoined or invalidated | Fallback yield/time, reserve draw, payment continuity, burden shift and litigation |

| SCN-CYBER | Treasury/claims cyber disruption | Receipt/disbursement timing and records fail | Offline payment, backlog, liquidity reserve, duplicate/error, recovery and reconciliation |

| SCN-PESS [high-cost injection] | High utilization/cost | Released demand, aging/LTC, workforce compensation, drug/device or hospital need exceeds central | Category cost, access/capacity, offsets, obligations, reserves and financing |

| SCN-EMP-FAIL | Employer/wage pass-through failure | Contribution collection or worker wage transfer underperforms | Receipts, worker/employer incidence, enforcement, restitution and trust |
HFASB produces baseline and adverse obligation/receipt/reserve/burden forecasts using registered models, matched price/time bases and correlated scenarios; NHASB independently reproduces gate quantities.
Gate 4 evidence includes certified obligations and legally available receipts, asset-level reserve eligibility/haircuts, volatile-exposure method, collection and burden tests, stabilizer readiness, legal contingencies, forecast error, unresolved findings and protected-payment continuity.
A pass is scoped and does not convert 98%/six-month gateway floors into maturity. P8 certification requires >=100% sufficiency, >=12 reserve months, >=92% wealth collection, <=5% ordinary burden and all applicable rights/safety/legal/continuity constraints.
Post-pass monitoring reopens Gate 4 for invalid data/formula, material forecast error, reserve impairment, legal authority loss, impoundment, structural deficit, burden breach or payment continuity failure.
Fiscal forecast error triggers SR-ADP-013 review and can change parameters, revenue administration, reserve plan, phase/benefit timing, authorized stabilizer or statutory design—but cannot erase observed error.

9. Legal and Governance Design
9.1 Statutory Architecture
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: The framework requires enforceable authorities and duties, not an administrative wish list; the enabling statute must connect entitlement, finance, operations, oversight, and remedy. Why this structure: Legal authorities are organized around enforceable dependencies and fallback paths so operational duties do not rest on implied power. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes statutory architecture explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the enabling act as an executable legal system that creates the entitlement, institutions, funding, duties, rights, continuity and repair mechanisms. |

| System entities | Congress; DNHA; NHAC; NBIA; THDO; NHA-TRUST/NHETF; NHTCA; NHASB; CHAO; A1-HCAC; RHA |

| Assumptions | Congress enacts a National Health Assurance and Health System Transition Act; critical functions are severable by function, not merely by sentence. |

| Data / parameters | title/provision ID, authority, duty, prohibition, owner, funding class, effective date, trigger, default, remedy, verifier |

| Requirements / performance | SR-ARCH-001–012; SR-LAW-001–010; VR-019/024 |

| Principal risks | RISK-LEGAL-001; LR-CONF-001 |

| Simulation implication | Represent every provision as a versioned legal object with state, dependencies, challenge probability, activation lag and fallback reference. |
The enabling act is the National Health Assurance and Health System Transition Act. It must do more than authorize programs: it must bind coverage, money, operations, rights and remedies into a system that remains operable during vacancies, delayed regulations, adverse judgments and the legacy-system wind-down. The nineteen-title structure below is controlled. Final section numbering and legislative wording remain open.

| II | Financing and Trust Funds | Dedicated receipts, NHA-TRUST/NHETF accounts, mandatory funding, reserves | Fiscal certification; account integrity |

| III | Enrollment and Public Default Coverage | Automatic/default enrollment, eligibility, identity, continuity | No coverage gap; correction and appeal |

| IV | Claims, Payment, and Appeals | NCCA/THDO payment rail, clean claims, provider rights, Article I review | Payment clocks; deemed allowance; judicial remedy |

| V | Drugs, Devices, Diagnostics, and Public Manufacturing | Purchasing, PCU, access, licensing, PMC and public production | Quality, shortage, competition and access |

| VI | Hospitals and Public-Service Charters | Global budgets, charter duties, capital/readiness, service continuity | Access, staffing, service-line and related-party controls |

| VII | Workforce, Education, Compensation, and Scope | Workforce bodies, education, compensation, federal scope floors | Safety, labor transition, rural distribution |

| VIII | LTC, Behavioral Health, DVH, and EMS | Expanded benefits, assessments, service authorities and continuity | Timeliness, integration and rights |

| IX | Records, Data Rights, Cybersecurity, and AI | Information Mesh, data charter, security, segmentation, AI accountability | Human accountability, audit, downtime continuity |

| X | Public Health and Prevention | Surveillance, prevention, emergency and population-health functions | Federal/state coordination and civil rights |

| XI | Biomedical Innovation | NBIA funding, trials, licensing, prizes and public-interest conditions | Access, evidence and research integrity |

| XII | Fraud, Abuse, and Anti-Extraction | Integrity enforcement, ownership transparency, anti-extraction controls | Due process; recovery; no capacity harm |

| XIII | State, Regional, and Tribal Transition | Compacts, RHA administration, preemption, tribal direct pathways, fallback | Trust duties; continuity; non-veto |

| XIV | Tax and Wealth Financing | Revenue bases, administration, incidence safeguards and fallback authorities | Sufficiency, burden, legality and review |

| XV | Transition Protection | NHTCA, continuity funds, worker/provider/patient safeguards, legacy wind-down | No unmanaged transition gap |

| XVIII | Adaptation, Scorekeeping, and Repair | NHASB, Formula Registry, review, waiver, emergency repair, sunset | Independent evidence; bounded change |

| XIX | Conforming Amendments | Federal cross-statute changes, transition clauses and legacy disposition | No conflict, orphan duty or coverage gap |
9.1.1 Provision object and dependency rules
Every operative provision identifies constitutional/statutory authority, regulated or obligated actors, enforceable duty or prohibition, effective and transition dates, implementing owner, funding classification and required records.
Every patient/provider/state/tribal/worker right identifies standing, administrative exhaustion if any, forum, standard of review, available interim/final remedy, payment or continuity effect, and nonretaliation protection.
Every delegated formula or regulation identifies its bounded discretion, Formula Registry entry, evidence/notice requirements, default if not issued, review cadence, emergency authority, expiry and correction route.
Every transition provision identifies predecessor/successor custody for claims, appeals, records, contracts, assets, liabilities, workforce and investigations; no duty may become ownerless at sunset.
Severability analysis is function-preserving: each critical function has a substitute authority or continuity default, and invalidation cannot be treated as permission for silent service withdrawal.
Table D7A-05. Cross-title dependency view

| System function | Titles | Primary entities | Legal/data object | Failure focus |

| Entitlement/coverage | I, III, VIII, XVI | ARCH-DNHA; NOPRSL; A1-HCAC | eligibility, benefit, explanation, appeal | benefit narrowing; silent rationing |

| Money/payment | II, IV, XIV, XVII | NHA-TRUST; NHETF; THDO; HFASB | receipt, obligation, disbursement, reserve | impoundment; timing mismatch |

| Care/capacity | V–VIII, X–XI | DNHA operating administrations; RHA; NBIA | capacity, service, product, workforce | underbuild; shortage; fragmentation |

| Information/rights | IX, XII, XVI | Information Mesh; NHAC; integrity offices | record, consent, audit, enforcement | privacy/cyber; inequity; suppression |

| Federalism/transition | XIII, XV, XIX | NHTCA; RHA; states; tribal authorities | compact, funding, migration, fallback | refusal; trust-duty erosion; orphan liability |

| Durability/repair | XVII–XVIII | CHAO; NHASB; courts; Congress | default, trigger, remedy, formula, sunset | sabotage; rigidity; unauthorized change |
SEVERABILITY RULE  Simulation and legislative drafting must test severability by preserved system function: coverage, payment, access, rights, data, transition, tribal duties and fiscal continuity—not only by whether isolated text survives.
9.2 Federal Conforming Changes
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Existing federal statutes would otherwise leave conflicting payer, privacy, tax, labor, procurement, and benefit rules in force after enactment. Why this structure: Legal authorities are organized around enforceable dependencies and fallback paths so operational duties do not rest on implied power. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes federal conforming changes explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Map affected federal law to explicit preserve, transfer, amend, supersede or sunset actions so no population, obligation, appeal, record or asset is orphaned. |

| System entities | Congress; CMS/HHS components; Treasury/IRS; Labor; VA; DoD; IHS; FDA; NIH; DOJ; OPM; DNHA/NHTCA |

| Assumptions | Conforming amendments are staged by phase and do not extinguish legacy duties before successor readiness and Gate 8 continuity certification. |

| Data / parameters | statute/program, section, function, population, asset/liability, successor, phase, savings clause, fallback |

| Requirements / performance | SR-ARCH; SR-LAW; SR-EQ; VR-015/019/024 |

| Principal risks | LR-CONF-001; RISK-LEGAL-001 |

| Simulation implication | Model each law/program as a dependency graph and migration inventory with dual-run cost, effective date, legal state and unresolved liability. |
Conforming legislation must be a controlled migration, not a blanket repeal. Each affected program or statute receives a disposition code: PRESERVE, PARALLEL, TRANSFER, AMEND, PREEMPT, SUNSET, or FALLBACK. The disposition is separately assigned to eligibility, benefit, funding, provider agreement, claim, appeal, record, contract, asset, liability, workforce, enforcement and data authority.

| Domain | Principal laws/programs | Required action | Continuity/control |

| Coverage/financing programs | Medicare; Medicaid; CHIP; ACA; FEHBA; TRICARE; VA | Map populations, benefits, funds, claims, liabilities and appeals into NHA or protected parallel channels | No beneficiary, provider or pending-appeal gap; preserve VA/TRICARE/IHS-specific duties until explicit transfer |

| Employer/insurance | ERISA; McCarran-Ferguson; insurance law interfaces | Define public-default preemption, supplemental coverage, employer contribution and wage-pass-through treatment | Protect collective bargaining, restitution, state safety authority and lawful supplemental markets |

| Tax/revenue | Internal Revenue Code; payroll/reporting provisions | Create dedicated financing bases, credits, reporting, collection, fallback and transition rules | Incidence guard, due process, anti-avoidance, certified yield and severability |

| Drugs/devices/innovation | FDCA; patent law; Hatch-Waxman; Bayh-Dole; Orphan Drug Act; BPCIA | Enable purchasing, public-interest licensing, government use, evidence and public manufacturing while preserving safety review | FDA quality independence; compensation; innovation/access evidence |

| Controlled substances | Controlled Substances Act | Align prescribing, dispensing, telehealth and SUD continuity with NHA clinical pathways | Diversion controls without care interruption or discriminatory barriers |

| Data/privacy | HIPAA; HITECH; 21st Century Cures; 42 CFR Part 2 | Authorize Mesh exchange, patient rights, correction, segmentation, purpose limitation and federated identity | More-protective privacy, tribal governance, minor/adolescent and sensitive-data rules |

| Fraud/referral/payment | Anti-Kickback; Stark; False Claims Act | Conform public budgets, salaries, referrals, integrity enforcement and recovery to new payment architecture | Safe harbors cannot legalize extraction; due process and whistleblower protections remain |

| Public health/federal systems | Public Health Service Act; Indian Health Care Improvement Act | Authorize national/regional public health, direct tribal funding and federal trust-duty integration | No diminution of tribal obligations; emergency and state coordination |

| Administration/appropriation | Impoundment Control Act; APA | Create mandatory payment, anti-delay remedies, default rules and bounded rulemaking/repair pathways | Notice, evidence, review, emergency expiry and judicial enforcement |

| Competition/corporate | Antitrust; corporate law; nonprofit hospital rules | Address consolidation, ownership, related parties, public-service charters and asset disposition | Preserve necessary capacity; transparent valuation and due process |

| Household protection | Medical debt; consumer-credit statutes | Prohibit or remediate covered-care debt and reporting; govern legacy debt transition | Correction, restitution, limitation periods and appeals |

| Field group | Required content |

| identity | FC-ID, citation/version, responsible committee/agency, controlled disposition and effective phase |

| function/population | covered population, benefit, funding, adjudication, enforcement, data and intergovernmental function |

| migration | predecessor, successor, dual-run interval, readiness evidence, transfer date and rollback/fallback |

| rights/liabilities | pending claims/appeals, debt, contracts, grants, investigations, judgments, records and limitation periods |

| resources | appropriation/receipt, asset, facility, IP, workforce, vendor and systems disposition |
