Providers move from negotiating and documenting across many core payer regimes toward common public rails and protocols. In return for payment protection and potential administrative simplification, providers assume clearer duties for structured routing, closed-loop safety, data quality, explanation, equity and public accountability. Clinical judgment remains human-accountable, but it operates within explicit evidence, benefit and safety rules.

| 69-I10 | Provider accountability expands for quality, safety, equity, explanation, data and public-service performance. | DUTY/EVIDENCE | VR-004/005/011–014; public dashboard | audited, stratified measures with usability and workload checks | Reporting can become punitive or distort care if measures are poorly specified. |
13.2.1 Provider transition principle
Onboard payment, credential, formulary, referral and record interfaces before legacy dependencies are removed.
Protect payroll and operating liquidity through provisional payment and rapid remedy, then reconcile without shifting system error to patients.
Measure net administrative work, including transition, correction, reporting and appeal—not only eliminated billing tasks.
Treat workload, autonomy, safety culture and retention as performance constraints during scope, compensation and AI changes.
13.3 Implications for Hospitals
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Hospitals face a shift from service-line revenue to public-service obligations, global budgets, capital review, staffing controls, and community accountability. Why this structure: Implications are organized by affected group so aggregate national gains do not conceal local burdens, duties, or transition risks. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes implications for hospitals explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Translate global budgets and public-service charters into financial, service-line, capital, workforce, interface, ownership and transition consequences. |

| System entities | Hospitals/systems; NHSA/HFASB/THDO; PSHCO; RHA; workforce/data/safety bodies |

| Assumptions | Global budgeting is not a fixed spending cap; it is a monitored public-service funding contract with readiness, capital, stabilization and repair components. |

| Data / parameters | budget/capital/readiness ledgers, service lines, staffing, access, quality/safety/equity, ownership/related parties, transition |

| Requirements / performance | SN-07/09/16; SR-HOSP; TPP-5; VR-017/021 |

| Principal risks | under/overcalibration; closure; gaming; capital neglect; workforce loss; regional inequity |

| Simulation implication | Stress budget corridors, demand, workforce, product shortage and rural conditions; report components of stability. |
Hospitals would operate under a fundamentally different financial logic. Essential capacity is funded directly through public budgets, readiness and capital allowances rather than recovered indirectly through service volume and cross-subsidy. That stability is paired with enforceable service, staffing, reporting and anti-extraction duties. Formula quality and rapid correction become central institutional risks.

| 70-I09 | Conversion is protected by a stabilization corridor, provider liquidity and delayed legacy sunset until readiness is certified. | TRANSITION/PROTECTION | NHTCA; Gate 8; RISK-HOSP | liquidity, service-line continuity, migration and reconciliation | Temporary support can become permanent or lock in an inflated base without sunset/review. |

| 70-I10 | Hospital success is defined as stable essential capacity and outcomes within a justified budget—not simply lower expenditure or positive margin. | OUTCOME/EVIDENCE | SN-07; TPP-5.4; OUT-014 | stability components, access, staffing, safety, cost and regional equity | Composite stability scores can hide a failed service line or population. |
13.3.1 Hospital budget guardrails
The floor prevents service collapse, unsafe staffing and loss of regionally essential capacity.
The ceiling and audit controls prevent transition fear, related-party extraction or unsupported base inflation from locking in excessive revenue.
Stabilization payments are temporary, evidence-triggered and reconciled; approved capital is tracked separately from operating cost.
Formula repair responds to verified access, service-line, workforce, safety, demand and regional changes under registered change control.
13.4 Implications for Employers and Workers
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Removing employment-linked core coverage changes compensation, payroll, bargaining, displaced administrative work, and employer responsibilities. Why this structure: Implications are organized by affected group so aggregate national gains do not conceal local burdens, duties, or transition risks. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes implications for employers and workers explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.

For employers, the framework replaces much of the unpredictable role of plan sponsor and purchaser with a statutory contribution and payroll interface. For workers, core coverage becomes portable and public, but total-compensation effects do not occur automatically. Wage pass-through, bargaining, small-business impacts and administrative-worker displacement require explicit rules, evidence and transition support.

13.5 Implications for States, Regions, and Tribal Nations
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: National uniformity can either reduce inequity or erase legitimate local and tribal authority; the distribution of standards, operations, compacts, and remedies must be explicit. Why this structure: Implications are organized by affected group so aggregate national gains do not conceal local burdens, duties, or transition risks. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes implications for states, regions, and tribal nations explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Translate the national entitlement into intergovernmental administration, financing, capacity, law, public-health, data and sovereign tribal consequences. |

| System entities | States/territories/localities; RHA/SRCO/TRTO; DNHA/NHTCA; tribal governments/health authorities; federal/IHS interfaces |

| Assumptions | Administrative mode may vary, but national rights, federal payment, direct tribal duties and continuity floors do not vary by state cooperation. |

| Data / parameters | compacts, function/funding allocation, capacity, conforming action, preemption disputes, fallback, tribal approval/data, waiver |

| Requirements / performance | SN-23/24; SR-ARCH-008; SR-EQ-008–010; VR-026 |

| Principal risks | state refusal; duplication; preemption litigation; fiscal stress; tribal-duty erosion; regional inequity |

| Simulation implication | Represent compact/fallback/legal states, regional capacity/funding and tribal jurisdiction; test state-resistance and rural-stress scenarios. |
States and regions remain essential operating partners, but they no longer control whether an eligible person receives the national core entitlement. The architecture converts state participation into a choice among cooperative administration and defined interfaces, backed by direct federal fallback. Tribal nations remain a separate sovereign relationship with direct funding, governance and federal trust protections.

| 72-I02 | Every region operates through a cooperative compact or preauthorized direct-federal fallback; state refusal cannot terminate national coverage or payment. | PROTECTION/DUTY | SR-ARCH-008; LF-11; RISK-STATE-001 | regional coverage/payment/access continuity and fallback activation time | Direct federal administration may be slower or less locally integrated. |

| 72-I03 | Regional Health Administrators become the principal capacity-planning and equalization interface for units, specialists, hospitals, workforce, EMS and public health. | CHANGE/DUTY | ARCH-RHA; ACDRH; capacity ledgers | regional capacity, waits, travel, service continuity and equity | Regional boundaries and authority may not match existing referral or labor markets. |

| 72-I04 | State and local financing transitions to a controlled maintenance contribution with equalization and hardship treatment rather than benefit eligibility control. | CHANGE/OI | FL-02; CP-FIN-003; OI-054 | contribution, fiscal capacity, equalization, compliance and service effects | Base year, effort, territories, local flows and hardship formulas remain open. |

| 72-I08 | Federal trust obligations are not reduced, replaced or conditioned without express tribal agreement through consultation and statutory consent mechanisms. | PROTECTION | Title XIII tribal principle; VR-026 | tribal-approved compact evidence, consultation/consent and duty continuity | Generic stakeholder consultation is not nation-to-nation consent. |

TRIBAL NON-DERIVATION RULE  Tribal eligibility, funding, data governance and participation do not derive from state consent. State systems may support interfaces but cannot substitute for nation-to-nation authority or tribal-approved verification.
13.6 Implications for Drug, Device, and Innovation Markets
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: National purchasing and public manufacturing change prices, margins, shortage incentives, licensing, and innovation finance across medicines, devices, and diagnostics. Why this structure: Implications are organized by affected group so aggregate national gains do not conceal local burdens, duties, or transition risks. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes implications for drug, device, and innovation markets explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.

The market architecture replaces opaque, fragmented purchasing with public rules and scale, while creating public alternatives for supply and innovation finance. This should change bargaining and product strategy, but the direction and size of innovation effects cannot be concluded from structure alone. The relevant test is joint performance on access, supply reliability, quality, therapeutic value, cost and research output.
Table D8C-04. Drug, device, and innovation-market implications

| ID | Controlled implication | Type | Basis / trace | Verification measure | Qualification / risk |

| 73-I01 | National purchasing replaces fragmented payer/PBM negotiation for the core public drug benefit. | CHANGE | NDPA/PCU; ASM-005; CP-RX | net price, access, dispensing, administrative cost and supplier response | Purchasing power can create supplier exit or shortage if price/capacity are miscalibrated. |

| 73-I02 | PBMs are removed from the core public pharmacy benefit, while any administrative contractor role is fixed-fee, transparent and subordinate to public rules. | CHANGE/DUTY | ASM-005; PCU; private-plan role | fees, spread/rebate elimination, claims performance and conflicts | Functions can reappear under new labels without ownership/payment transparency. |

| 73-I03 | A national formulary and therapeutic schedule uses evidence, safety, value and public explanation with exception and appeal channels. | CHANGE/PROTECTION | NFTSB/MARB/DUSO; No Silent Rationing | coverage/exceptions, time to therapy, safety, equity and appeal outcomes | Central rules can become rigid, delayed or insensitive to rare/individual need. |

| 73-I04 | The Public Medicines Corporation routinely manufactures all 200 controlled product families and also maintains surge capability for shortages, essential-product continuity and bargaining resilience. | CHANGE/PROTECTION | PMC; CP-RX; RISK-PMC-001 | qualified capacity, batch quality, inventory, shortage exposure and cost | Public production carries quality, capital, scale and governance risk. |

| 73-I05 | Device, diagnostic and supply purchasing becomes more nationally coordinated, with public production and maintenance options where justified. | CHANGE | MDSA/LDA/AMDDT; CP-DX | unit cost, availability, maintenance, quality, utilization and innovation | Product heterogeneity and clinical switching costs limit simple price standardization. |

| 73-I06 | Biomedical R&D financing is separated from using product prices as the primary recovery mechanism. | CHANGE | ASM-001/002; NBIA/NDIF/TMTFO | public R&D, milestone/prize/subscription funding, outputs and access conditions | Public funding must manage selection, failure, capture and long-horizon risk. |

| 73-I07 | Public-interest licensing, government-use compensation and procurement conditions link publicly supported innovation to access and supply. | DUTY/PROTECTION | PILO; Title XI; LF-06 | license terms, compensation, access, price, supply and follow-on innovation | Authority and compensation design require specialized legal/economic review. |

| 73-I08 | Market incentives shift toward evidence, reliable supply, therapeutic value and public-service contracting rather than rebate, network and price-opacity strategies. | OUTCOME/CHANGE | CEVI; purchasing/formulary architecture | R&D portfolio, entry/exit, competition, launch terms, supply and clinical value | Firm behavior and capital allocation response are calibration-dependent. |

| 73-I09 | National product and supply ledgers make shortage, inventory, quality and source concentration visible for contingency action. | DUTY/EVIDENCE | Information Mesh product ledger; VR-018 | inventory/source concentration, shortage signals, release/recall and emergency procurement | Commercial sensitivity, inaccurate inventory and cyber/data gaps can undermine visibility. |

| 73-I10 | The framework does not establish that innovation will increase, decrease or remain unchanged; that is an empirical and scenario-dependent market question. | EVIDENCE/OI | SCN-DRUG-SHORT; CP-RD/RX/OFF; source completeness | innovation outputs, time, risk-adjusted cost, access, supply and health outcomes | Selective success stories can obscure portfolio failure or delayed benefits. |
13.6.1 Market evaluation rule
Separate acquisition price, dispensing, distribution, production, inventory, quality, R&D and public-financing cost.
Track entry, exit, investment, trial success/failure, time to evidence, license terms, access and shortage effects by product class.
Do not count a negotiated price reduction and an eliminated monopoly rent as two independent savings without reconciliation.
Use public manufacturing as a qualified capacity option with the same or stronger quality, release, recall and transparency controls.
13.7 Implications for Public Finance
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: Public finance absorbs obligations now distributed across premiums, taxes, employers, households, and uncompensated care, changing incidence and fiscal visibility. Why this structure: Implications are organized by affected group so aggregate national gains do not conceal local burdens, duties, or transition risks. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes implications for public finance explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Translate the total-system cost boundary and financing architecture into federal, state/local, employer, household, reserve, transition and scorekeeping consequences. |

| System entities | Congress/Treasury/IRS; THDO/NHA-TRUST/NHETF/HFASB; states/localities; employers/households; NHASB/CHAO |

| Assumptions | The controlled cost position is a framework assumption. Public-finance implications require legislation, calibration, economic incidence and independent scorekeeping. |

| Data / parameters | public/private cost, obligations/outlays, receipts, transfers, incidence, state contributions, reserves, stabilizers, transition and macro variables |

| Requirements / performance | PR-CST; KPP-C1–C8; VR-024/027 |

| Principal risks | budget/total-cost confusion; revenue shortfall; legal invalidation; burden shift; reserve/cash timing; macro response |

| Simulation implication | Run reconciled fiscal paths by payer/group and stress yield, legal, macro, workforce and transition conditions. |
Public finance becomes more transparent and centralized because spending currently distributed across public programs, employers, households and private intermediaries is reorganized around a national entitlement. That does not mean all existing spending becomes a federal outlay or that financing is automatically sufficient. The design requires careful consolidation, incidence analysis, transition cash planning, reserve management and independent scorekeeping.
Table D8C-05. Public-finance implications

| ID | Controlled implication | Type | Basis / trace | Verification measure | Qualification / risk |

| 74-I01 | A larger share of health financing becomes explicit public receipts and outlays, while total-system cost still includes residual private and patient spending. | CHANGE | CP-TOT-001/004–006; public/residual-private boundary | consolidated public/private/patient cost and transfer elimination | Public budget growth can be confused with total resource growth. |

| 74-I02 | Existing federal health spending is redirected through conforming law into the national entitlement and operating architecture. | CHANGE/TRANSITION | FL-01; Title XIX; federal conforming records | program/population/fund transfer, dual-run cost and legacy reconciliation | Delayed transfer can require mandatory bridge financing. |

| 74-I03 | State/local maintenance contributions and national equalization change intergovernmental flows without allowing fiscal capacity to determine core entitlement. | CHANGE/PROTECTION | FL-02; NHETF; OI-054 | state/local contribution, equalization, hardship and regional service outcomes | Poor formulas can reward prior underinvestment or destabilize budgets. |

| 74-I04 | Employer contributions, progressive wealth/high-income/capital sources, health-sector rent receipts and a residual broad backstop form a layered financing waterfall. | CHANGE/OI | FL-03–07; CP-FIN | legally due/collected receipts, incidence, yield, cost and fallback activation | Rates, bases, behavioral response and legal durability remain unresolved. |

| 74-I05 | Ordinary-household protection limits incremental fallback burden and requires economic-incidence analysis rather than remitter labels. | PROTECTION/EVIDENCE | SN-12; KPP-C8; D6B-DEC-09 | ordinary-household burden share <=5% under approved method | Taxes, wages, prices and employment may shift incidence indirectly. |

| 74-I06 | Operating stabilization, shock reserve and permanent endowment accounts separate liquidity, volatility and intergenerational functions. | CHANGE/PROTECTION | NHA-TRUST/NHETF fund accounts; KPP-C6 | eligible balances, haircuts, volatile exposure, draws, replenishment and months | Nominal balances may be illiquid, correlated or legally unavailable. |

| 74-I07 | Fiscal stabilizers and legal fallbacks respond to receipt shortfall or invalidated authorities under registered triggers and burden guards. | PROTECTION/DUTY | trigger ladder; LF-01/02/04; SR-LAW | activation, replacement yield, timing, burden, reserve and payment continuity | Fallbacks may be narrower, slower or less progressive. |

| 74-I08 | Transition creates substantial public cash and administrative demands even when some costs replace existing private spending. | TRANSITION | $1.2T–$2.0T over 10–12 years; TW-01–13 | work-package obligations/outlays, asset acceptance, recoveries and closeout | Cash timing and institutional capacity can bind before mature savings. |

| 74-I09 | The framework's public-finance position is a controlled hypothesis requiring independent fiscal, distributional and macroeconomic scorekeeping. | EVIDENCE | NHASB/CHAO/HFASB; VR-024 | cost, GDP/population denominators, receipts, incidence, macro response and uncertainty | Assumption-consistent models can still be wrong about behavior or macro effects. |

| 74-I10 | Fiscal transparency must show assumptions, forecasts, obligations, receipts, outlays, reserves, scenarios and observed results as separate public records. | DUTY/PROTECTION | public dashboard; fiscal flow; Formula Registry | timely completeness, reproducibility, corrections and public explanation | Aggregation or relabeling can hide shortfall, burden or forecast error. |
FISCAL CLAIM RULE  A rise in federal outlay is not by itself a rise in total-system cost; a fall in private premiums is not by itself household savings; a tax receipt is not a cost; and a reserve balance is not annual spending. Each must be reconciled in its proper accounting view.
13.8 Implications for Communications Planning
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS  Why it is needed: A reform this complex can lose support through exaggerated promises or technical opacity; communication must distinguish assumptions, targets, evidence, and measured results. Why this structure: Implications are organized by affected group so aggregate national gains do not conceal local burdens, duties, or transition risks. Improvement mechanism: compared with the current fragmented arrangement, this section makes implications for communications planning explicit, allocates responsibility, and exposes the claim to requirements, verification, risk analysis, and simulation rather than leaving it as an aspiration.
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define truthful, accessible, audience-specific and feedback-linked communication for design, enactment, transition, operations, incidents and repair. |

| System entities | PRTO/NOPRSL/NHASB/CHAO; DNHA/NHTCA/RHA; service/appeal channels; stakeholder and tribal communications bodies |

| Assumptions | Communications cannot compensate for service failure or convert assumptions into outcomes. Trust is earned through accurate operation, usable rights and visible correction. |

| Data / parameters | claim status/source, audience/task, channel/language/accessibility, comprehension, action/resolution, trust, correction and feedback |

| Requirements / performance | SN-14/19/20; KPP-TRUST1; VR-010/020/028 |

| Principal risks | overpromise; simplification; misinformation; inaccessible service; politicization; selective uncertainty |

| Simulation implication | Model trust/behavior and communication reach only as linked to service state; retain subgroup response and correction events. |
Communications planning is part of service design and legitimacy. The framework is complex, and the temptation to compress it into a cost slogan, benefit promise or institutional label is substantial. The controlled approach is to tell audiences what changes, what protections apply, what remains uncertain, what action they must take, what evidence supports a claim, and how errors are corrected.
Table D8C-06. Communications-planning implications

| ID | Controlled implication | Type | Basis / trace | Verification measure | Qualification / risk |

| 75-I01 | Every public claim is labeled as framework design, final assumption, target, forecast/scenario, verified result, observed outcome or open issue. | DUTY/PROTECTION | D1 simulation-readiness; D8A status convention | claim audit, source/ID, status label and correction history | Unlabeled claims can turn assumptions into promises. |

| 75-I02 | The central narrative explains the system as coverage plus capacity, payment, rights, transition and repair—not 'free care' or a single-payer slogan alone. | CHANGE | Sections 4–6; Layers 3–5 | audience comprehension of responsibilities, sequence and safeguards | Oversimplification can create demand, cost and trust expectations the design cannot meet. |

| 75-I03 | Cost communication uses the controlled $4.75T mature assumption and ranges while clearly separating total-system cost, public outlay, transition cost and financing. | DUTY | Section 8; D8A 63-C01/02 | correct classification and denominator understanding | A headline number without boundary/status can mislead in either direction. |

| 75-I04 | Transition messaging states what changes, what remains continuous, who acts when failure occurs, and how patients/providers/workers obtain immediate help. | TRANSITION/PROTECTION | NHTCA; continuity guarantees; Gate 8 | awareness, channel reach, resolution time and continuity events | Reassurance without operable support can worsen distrust after failures. |

| 75-I05 | Audience materials are role-specific for patients/caregivers, clinicians, hospitals, pharmacies, employers/workers, states/regions, tribal nations and market participants. | CHANGE/DUTY | SN-01–25; Sections 13.1–13.7 | task completion, comprehension, language/disability access and error rates | Generic messaging can omit duties or remedies relevant to a group. |

| 75-I06 | Rights communication makes the No Silent Rationing doctrine, benefit boundaries, explanations, appeals, data rights and human review concrete and actionable. | PROTECTION | Patient Bill of Rights; Health Data Rights Charter | recognition, assisted filing, relief time, correction and nonretaliation | Legalistic descriptions may be technically correct but unusable. |

| 75-I07 | Uncertainty, open issues and failed/indeterminate gate or model results are communicated alongside favorable findings. | DUTY/EVIDENCE | VR-025; D7B/D7C; OI registers | completeness, uncertainty comprehension and correction uptake | Selective disclosure can undermine legitimacy and distort decisions. |

| 75-I08 | Public trust is treated as a measured operational variable with independent survey methods, not a communications score to be optimized through persuasion. | PROTECTION/EVIDENCE | KPP-TRUST1; VR-028; RISK-TRUST-001 | representative trust index, reasons, disparities and service-linked repair | Message testing can become manipulation or suppress substantive criticism. |

| 75-I09 | Misinformation response prioritizes rapid factual correction, service continuity and transparent evidence without stigmatizing uncertainty or dissent. | PROTECTION | public confidence repair protocol; PRTO/NOPRSL | correction reach, belief/service behavior, complaints and trust recovery | Overreaction can amplify claims or politicize public information. |

| 75-I10 | Communications is a closed-loop service: feedback, complaints, appeals, call/portal behavior and field observations drive design and policy repair. | CHANGE/EVIDENCE | appeals learning; Layer 5; service-design standards | feedback closure, recurrent failure, usability, equity and change-control records | Feedback collection without authority or response becomes performative. |
13.8.1 Claim discipline
Table D8C-07. Say / do-not-say control

| Claim class | Permitted formulation | Prohibited shortcut | Required support |

| Framework choice | 'The framework establishes public default coverage.' | 'Everyone is already or automatically covered.' | ASM/SR/ARCH and enactment status |

| Cost assumption | 'Mature total-system cost is assumed at about $4.75T/year in real 2024 dollars.' | 'The system will cost exactly $4.75T.' | controlled cost position; calibration/status |

| Target | 'The maturity target is at least 99.5% continuous core coverage.' | 'Coverage gaps will be eliminated.' | KPP/TPP and verified result |

| Scenario | 'Under SCN-WF-SHORT, vacancy and access effects are stress-tested.' | 'Workforce shortages are predicted to occur at the scenario magnitude.' | SCN manifest, overrides and uncertainty |

| Verified result | 'The measured result passed the stated threshold with this evidence and uncertainty.' | 'The whole system is successful.' | VR evidence, verifier, population/region and date |

| Open issue | 'Rates and bases remain to be legislated and calibrated.' | 'Details will work themselves out.' | OI owner, dependency and closure evidence |
13.8.2 Communications operating cycle
Identify the audience's task, decision, right, burden, timing, language, disability/digital access and trusted channel.
Draft from controlled claim records; attach status, source/version, date, owner, uncertainty and action/remedy path.
Test comprehension and task completion with representative users, including communities with reason to distrust public institutions.
Publish with correction/appeal channels and monitor misunderstanding, service friction, misinformation, complaints and subgroup disparities.
Correct the service or policy when feedback exposes a real failure; correct the message when the service is sound but the explanation is not; document both.

Appendix B — Assumption Register
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Consolidate the design, boundary, comparator and evaluation assumptions that make the architecture and simulation interpretable. |

| System entities | Framework stewards; NHASB; CHAO; simulation builders; legal/fiscal/clinical reviewers. |

| Assumptions | The register itself is controlled. FA, MP and OI status is preserved and does not establish empirical truth. |

| Data / parameters | Assumption statement, status, trace references, simulation treatment and open-issue dependencies. |

| Requirements / performance | ASM-001–ASM-035; linked SN/PR/SR/KPP/TPP/CP/ARCH/RISK/SCN records. |

| Principal risks | Hidden assumptions; deprecated cost estimates; inconsistent scope; false precision; circular calibration. |

| Simulation implication | Instantiate each active assumption as a declared configuration, structural rule or sensitivity branch; never bury it in code defaults. |
The register separates final framework choices from provisional model assumptions and unresolved issues. In particular, framework-specific numbers retain their model-assumption status, total-system cost remains distinct from public outlay, and capacity, transition, regional variation and behavioral response remain endogenous.
COST ASSUMPTION GUARD  The mature $4.75T/year value and its ranges are framework assumptions in real 2024 dollars. They are not verified forecasts and must not be replaced by a superseded working estimate.

| ASM-024 | Provider and market adaptation Proposed / MP | Providers, employers, private plans, suppliers, and households alter behavior in response to payment, coverage, regulation, and capacity changes. | RISK-WF/STATE/FIN; CP behavioral inputs | Represent participation, avoidance, substitution, consolidation, wage pass-through, and supply responses. |

| ASM-025 | Workforce pipeline Proposed / MP | Training expansion has multiyear lags and is constrained by faculty, clinical placements, licensure, geography, and retention. | PR-WF; T-ED-008 | Use occupation-specific stocks, entries, exits, training slots, completion, service obligations, and migration. |

| ASM-026 | Causal offset discipline Adopted / MP | A cost offset is recognized only with a causal pathway, lag, attribution rule, uncertainty range, and double-counting control. | CP-OFF-001–020 | Maintain gross additions and gross savings separately; prohibit a single avoided event from satisfying multiple offsets. |

| ASM-027 | Reserve versus cost Adopted / MP | Reserve balances and authority are not annual consumption cost; contributions, earnings, draws, and transfers are separate cash-flow records. | CP-FIN-011–016 | Report stocks and flows separately and state when a reserve contribution is included in public outlay. |

| ASM-028 | Financing incidence Proposed / OI | Financing adequacy and economic incidence are distinct: the legal remitter may differ from the household or firm bearing the economic burden. | KPP-C5/C8; CP-FIN | Model statutory receipts, behavioral response, wage/profit/price incidence, collection efficiency, and avoidance separately. |

| ASM-029 | Evaluation perspectives Adopted / MP | Results are reported from total-system, federal, state/local, employer, household, provider, and distributional perspectives. | Section 3.4; CP-TOT/FIN | No single fiscal balance is presented as the complete social cost result. |

| ASM-030 | Equity stratification Adopted / MP | Access, coverage, quality, safety, wait, burden, and outcomes are measured by prespecified population and geography groups. | KPP-E1–T-ED-005; SN-18 | Calculate gaps and ratios with sample-size, suppression, and intersectionality rules. |

| ASM-031 | External shocks Proposed / MP | Recession, pandemic, cyberattack, supply disruption, litigation, migration, and workforce shocks can affect both framework and comparator. | SCN; RISK-CYBER/LEGAL/FIN | Apply common shocks where appropriate and architecture-specific propagation/recovery behavior. |

| ASM-032 | Uncertainty representation Adopted / MP | Material uncertain inputs use ranges or probability distributions rather than hidden point estimates. | Simulation-readiness convention | Store distribution family, bounds, correlations, provenance, and scenario overrides; report sensitivity and confidence. |

| ASM-033 | Calibration/validation separation Adopted / MP | Calibration data and validation evidence are separated where feasible. | VR-001–015 | Track dataset role and prevent reuse of holdout evidence for parameter fitting without disclosure. |

| ASM-034 | Target non-achievement Adopted / MP | A requirement or target constrains evaluation but does not force a simulated result to pass. | All PR/SR/KPP/TPP | Compute performance from mechanisms; failed requirements are reported as failures, not corrected by output clipping. |

| ASM-035 | No forecast claim before calibration Adopted / OI | The $4.75T central cost position is a controlling framework assumption, not an empirically validated forecast until the full cost model is calibrated and verified. | CP-TOT-001; ASM-015 | Use central/low/high framework scenarios and report the assumptions and unresolved cost components driving each result. |

Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Preserve the 25 top-level needs as the human outcome and rights layer above requirements, architecture and measures. |

| System entities | Patients, residents, providers, hospitals, workforce, employers, public bodies, regions/states, tribal nations, innovators and oversight institutions. |

| Assumptions | Need satisfaction requires both service performance and enforceable rights; a metric target alone is insufficient. |

| Data / parameters | Need, goal, metric, owner, right/protection, population/geography/time and claim status. |

| Requirements / performance | SN-01–SN-25; PR/SR/VR; KPP/TPP; ARCH owners; IF evidence. |

| Principal risks | Need dilution; metric substitution; missing equity strata; owner diffusion; rights without remedy. |

| Simulation implication | Represent needs as objectives or constraints and report results by stakeholder, region and equity stratum without assuming satisfaction. |
Each need remains outcome-oriented and technology-neutral. The service owner is accountable for performance; the listed right or protection constrains how the system responds when performance fails or a decision is contested.

| VR-011 | Every denial, delay, non-referral, and routing explanation requirement shall be verified by audit of complete decision records. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-012 | Every clinical safety requirement shall be verified using both administrative data and sampled clinical record review. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-013 | Every abnormal-result closure requirement shall be verified by result timestamp, patient notification timestamp, care-plan timestamp, and escalation timestamp where applicable. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-014 | Every specialist-access requirement shall be verified using completed referral packet timestamp, urgency class timestamp, specialist response timestamp, and appointment completion timestamp. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-015 | Every transition-continuity requirement shall be verified using pre-migration and post-migration patient-level continuity records. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-016 | Every displaced-worker transition requirement shall be verified using worker eligibility records, offer records, training enrollment, placement status, and retention data. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-017 | Every hospital global-budget requirement shall be verified using audited hospital financials, public disbursement records, service-line data, staffing data, and regional access metrics. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-018 | Every drug-shortage and public manufacturing requirement shall be verified using inventory records, production records, supplier qualification data, quality-release data, and shortage status. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-019 | Every legal-hardening requirement shall be verified using statutory text, appropriations classification, disbursement logs, vacancy records, staffing records, and litigation records. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-020 | Every public dashboard requirement shall be verified using publication timestamps, completeness checks, privacy review logs, and independent reproducibility tests. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-021 | Every formula affecting payment, access, benefits, priority, or workforce shall be verified against the Formula Registry before operational use. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-022 | Every emergency repair action shall be verified against change-control tier, authority, expiration date, public notice, and ratification status. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-023 | Every regional adaptation waiver shall be verified against its hypothesis, endpoints, patient-protection plan, equity analysis, budget impact, sunset date, and independent evaluation. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-024 | Every trust-fund and fiscal-sufficiency requirement shall be verified using actuarially certified obligations, receipts, transfers, balances, and reserve calculations. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-025 | Every requirement used to block or permit phase progression shall require independent verification before the next phase may begin. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-026 | Every tribal compact requirement shall be verified through tribal-approved documentation and shall not rely solely on state certification. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-027 | Every employer wage-pass-through requirement shall be verified using employer baseline benefit spending, payroll records, worker compensation records, and contribution filings. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-028 | Every public-trust parameter shall be verified using statistically representative survey methods and published sampling methodology. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-029 | Every safety-culture parameter shall be verified using validated workforce safety-culture survey instruments and turnover/workload corroboration data. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |

| VR-030 | Every requirement marked for demonstration shall include an operational scenario, entry criteria, exit criteria, observed outputs, and pass/fail criteria before verification event execution. | No source trace field | Requirement-defined evidence Source-controlled draft |
Appendix E — Requirements Allocation Matrix
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Make upstream needs and downstream ownership, metrics, evidence and interfaces auditable for every controlled requirement. |

| System entities | PR/SR/VR owners; NHASB; CHAO; NHAC; Article I court; operating agencies; interface and data stewards. |

| Assumptions | Explicit source traces take precedence. Parent-, metric- and family-derived allocations are labeled and remain subject to independent adjudication. |

| Data / parameters | SN, parent requirement, KPP/TPP, owner, verifier, verification method/VR, interface and status. |

| Requirements / performance | Appendices C/D/F; ARCH/IF catalogs; VR-001–VR-030. |

| Principal risks | Circular trace; unsupported family inference; missing evidence; owner/verifier conflict; interface orphaning. |

| Simulation implication | Use the matrix as a graph: needs constrain requirements; requirements allocate to agents/functions; metrics and VR records evaluate results. |
The matrix distinguishes four allocation bases: explicit source trace, parent-derived trace, metric- or need-derived trace, and family allocation requiring adjudication. Cross-cutting VR records do not receive invented stakeholder links; they inherit the upstream need of the object they verify.

Appendix F — KPP/TPP Dictionary
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Consolidate outcome-critical and technical performance measures into a computation- and verification-ready dictionary. |

| System entities | Metric owners; NHASB/CHAO/NHAC and other independent verifiers; data stewards; implementers; simulation builders. |

| Assumptions | Targets are source-controlled constraints, not observations. Open denominators, baselines and acceptance protocols remain visible. |

| Data / parameters | Name, target, domain/family, calculation, unit/data references, owner, verifier, trace and status. |

| Requirements / performance | 41 KPP; 79 TPP; SN; PR/SR; VR-002–VR-004; Section 5 datasets; Appendix R dashboard. |

| Principal risks | Denominator drift; target/baseline confusion; unverifiable composites; missing strata; self-verification; output clipping. |

| Simulation implication | Calculate each metric from model state/events using a versioned protocol; store target, result, evidence/provenance and uncertainty separately. |
KPPs express mission-level performance and protection. TPPs express technical or operational performance. Both require a controlled numerator/denominator or statistic, data provenance, update period, equity treatment where relevant, and independent verification before gate use.

Appendix G — Cost Parameter Dictionary
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Publish the complete cost-input, state, ledger and derived-output vocabulary required to construct and audit the framework/comparator simulation. |

| System entities | HFASB; NHASB; CHAO; THDO; NHTCA; operating ARCH owners; data stewards; model builders. |

| Assumptions | Real 2024 U.S. dollars are the default monetary basis. Source-defined names do not imply calibrated values or distributions. |

| Data / parameters | ID, family, name/description, canonical unit and status, model role, temporal class, owner and value/calibration status. |

| Requirements / performance | CP-TOT-001–CP-OFF-020; ASM-015/018/019/026/027/029/032/035; Section 8; Appendix H. |

| Principal risks | Unit ambiguity; stock/flow mixing; transfer double count; hidden price year; uncalibrated values; correlated extremes. |

| Simulation implication | Instantiate each CP with value/distribution, unit, time/geography/population dimensions, source class, provenance, correlation group and scenario override. |
The dictionary is deliberately broader than a budget table. It includes population, activity, readiness, capital, transition, financing and offset parameters so that total-system cost, public outlay and distributional incidence can be reconciled without treating transfers or reserves as resource consumption.

Appendix H — Cost Equations
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the auditable algebra that consolidates category cost, transition, offsets, financing, incidence and reserve states without double counting. |

| System entities | HFASB; NHASB; CHAO; THDO; NHTCA; category owners; simulation and independent verification teams. |

| Assumptions | Equations calculate values from controlled inputs; they do not establish calibration, legal sufficiency or successful performance. |

| Data / parameters | Equation, dependencies, claim/status class, price/time/population basis, ledger events, uncertainty and reconciliation results. |

| Requirements / performance | Appendix G CPs; KPP-C/TPP-EMP1; MC-01–14; TW-01–13; FL-01–07; ASM cost controls. |

| Principal risks | Operator precedence; unmatched denominators; offset overlap; transition/operating duplication; transfer/reserve misclassification. |

| Simulation implication | Implement equations as versioned functions with dimensional checks, dependency graphs, test fixtures and reconciliation tolerances. |
LOCAL LABEL RULE  H-EQ labels are appendix-local equation keys, not a new global identifier family. CP, KPP, TPP, MC, TW and FL references remain the controlled reusable objects.
Table H-1. Controlled equation register

| Local key | Equation | Algebra | Status | Dependencies | Boundary / verification control |

| H-EQ-01 | Master cost | C_total(t) = C_hospital + C_clinical + C_units + C_LTC + C_drugs + C_devices_labs_diagnostics + C_behavioral + C_DVH + C_EMS + C_public_health + C_info_cyber_AI + C_governance_oversight + C_R&D + C_education_workforce + C_transition_net - C_offsets | DV constrained by FA | CP-TOT-001; all operating CP families; CP-TRN; CP-OFF | One category owner per cost event; shared costs use a registered allocation; mature transition is zero except residual closeout. |

| H-EQ-02 | Offsets | C_offsets(t) = admin + PBM + revenue_cycle + debt_collection + ED_diversion + avoidable_admission + readmission + drug_device_purchasing + manufacturing + duplicate_testing + specialist_substitution + prevention_early_detection + other_verified_offsets | DV / OI-051 | CP-OFF-001–020 | Preserve gross savings and interaction terms; no avoided event or baseline difference may be counted twice. |

| H-EQ-03 | Total-system consolidation | C_total_system = C_public_outlay + C_residual_private + C_patient_paid - internal_public_transfers - duplicate_reimbursements | DV | CP-TOT-001/004–006; CP-FIN | Taxes/contributions finance cost but are not additional system cost; eliminate only reconciled internal transfers. |

| H-EQ-04 | Transition-adjusted annual | C_TA(t) = C_operating(t) + C_transition_net(t) + capital_cash_adjustment(t) + residual_private(t) + patient_paid(t) - consolidation_eliminations(t) | DV constrained by FA | CP-TOT-007; CP-TRN; CP-TOT-005/006 | Generate from the resource-loaded time profile; do not divide the cumulative transition envelope uniformly. |

| H-EQ-05 | Per-capita cost | CP-TOT-002(t) = C_total_system(t) / population_denominator(t) | DV / OI-001/OI-050 | CP-TOT-001/002; CP-POP-001 | Population, coverage, territory, period and price-year definitions must be version-matched. |

| H-EQ-06 | GDP share | CP-TOT-003(t) = C_total_system(t) / consistent_GDP(t) | DV / OI-001/OI-050 | CP-TOT-001/003; CP-POP-002 | Numerator and GDP must use a consistent nominal/real and time basis; target remains unbaselined. |

| H-EQ-07 | Mature total constraint | sum_i C_mature[MC_i, t=P8_mature] = 4.75T central; plausible aggregate range = 4.30T–5.25T | FA constraint | CP-TOT-001; MC-01–MC-14 | Category distributions are jointly calibrated and correlated; independent endpoints need not sum to aggregate endpoints. |

| H-EQ-08 | Category cost | C_i = service_volume_i × unit_cost_i + staffed_readiness_i + capital_charge_i + administration_i + other_boundary_i - verified_offsets_allocated_i | MP/DV | Category CP families; CP-OFF | Readiness and low-volume essential capacity remain visible rather than being forced into volume prices. |

| H-EQ-09 | Net savings versus comparator | CP-TOT-008(t) = C_baseline_comparator(t) - C_framework_total_system(t) | DV | CP-TOT-008; comparator path | Comparator and framework use matched scope, price year, population, morbidity and time state; non-cost failures remain binding. |

| H-EQ-10 | Gross-to-net identity | C_framework_net = C_baseline + CP-TOT-009(gross_additions) - CP-TOT-010(gross_savings) | DV | CP-TOT-009/010; CP-OFF | Report interaction and reconciliation terms; do not sum overlapping savings mechanisms independently. |

| H-EQ-11 | Cumulative transition | C_transition_cumulative = sum(unique_incremental_transition_outlays_and_accruals) - recoveries - duplicate_reclassifications | DV constrained by FA | CP-TRN; CP-TOT-007 | Reserve authority/unconsumed balances are not automatically cost; preserve asset and service lineage. |

| H-EQ-12 | Net provider liquidity | CP-TRN-006 = provisional_liquidity_disbursements - reconciled_recoveries - duplicate_or_invalid_payments | DV | CP-TRN-005/006; IF-003/004 | Authority or available capacity is not net cost; valid underlying care payment stays in its service category. |

| H-EQ-13 | Annual transition profile | C_transition_net(t) = committed_incremental_work(t) + continuity_stabilization(t) + failure_repair(t) - recoveries(t) | DV / OI-052 | CP-TRN; TW-01–TW-13 | Use resource-loaded work packages; delays may shift cash while increasing harm, contingency or later cost. |

| H-EQ-14 | Dedicated receipts | R_dedicated(t) = federal_redirect + state_local + employer + extreme_wealth + high_income_capital + health_rent + activated_backstop | DV / legislative calibration | CP-FIN; FL-01–FL-07 | Record legally due, cash collected, refunds, timing, administration, leakage, uncertainty and legal state separately. |

| H-EQ-15 | Revenue sufficiency | KPP-C5(t) = available_dedicated_receipts_for_period / certified_obligations_for_period | TG calculation | KPP-C5; CP-FIN; PH-G4 | Maturity target ≥100%; Gate 4 floor ≥98%; use matched period, legal availability and accounting convention. |

| H-EQ-16 | Collection efficiency | KPP-C7 = certified_collections_received / certified_legally_due_wealth_financing | TG calculation | KPP-C7; CP-FIN | Target ≥92%; refunds, disputes, timing, avoidance/evasion and court-disabled liability are separate states. |

| H-EQ-17 | Ordinary-household protection | KPP-C8 = incremental_financing_burden_on_defined_ordinary_households / total_incremental_financing_burden | TG / OI | KPP-C8; CP-FIN | Target ≤5%; household definition, counterfactual and incidence method require controlled approval. |

| H-EQ-18 | Employer wage pass-through | TPP-EMP1 = compliant_employers_or_covered_workers_under_approved_attribution / eligible_employers_or_workers | TG / OI | TPP-EMP1; CP-FIN; CP-TRN | Target ≥95%; unit, baseline benefit spending, bargaining, timing and attribution remain controlled decisions. |

| H-EQ-19 | Period sufficiency | sufficiency(t) = (legally_available_dedicated_receipts(t) + authorized_current_period_transfers(t)) / certified_obligations(t) | DV/TG | KPP-C5; CP-FIN | Parentheses are mandatory; disclose reserve draws separately even when legally available for payment. |

| H-EQ-20 | Structural balance | structural_balance = cyclically_adjusted_recurring_receipts - recurring_certified_obligations | DV / OI | CP-FIN; CP-TOT | A recurring deficit cannot be permanently cured by reserve draw; register the cyclical-adjustment method. |

| H-EQ-21 | Volatile revenue exposure | VRE_12m = sum_s(expected_12m_receipt_s × stress_loss_fraction_s × liquidity_timing_factor_s) | MP / OI-056 | CP-FIN-011–016 | Specify revenue classes, correlated stresses, horizon, timing and exclusions before gate use. |

| H-EQ-22 | Reserve months | reserve_months = 12 × eligible_liquid_stabilization_assets / VRE_12m | DV/TG / OI-056 | KPP-C6; CP-FIN; PH-G4 | Apply asset haircuts, encumbrances and account-purpose limits; Gate 4 floor ≥6 months and maturity target ≥12. |

| H-EQ-23 | Reserve replenishment gap | reserve_gap = max(target_eligible_balance - eligible_balance, 0) | DV | CP-FIN | A replenishment plan must preserve obligations and ordinary-household guards and avoid automatic destabilizing procyclicality. |
H.1 Anti-double-counting and dimensional controls
Table H-2. Equation execution controls

| Control | Mandatory rule |

| Exclusive booking | Each cost event has one primary category and unique event ID; allocations sum to one. |

| Source class | FA, MP, TG, ED, DV and OI remain distinct fields; repetition cannot upgrade evidence status. |

| Price/time basis | All monetary values carry price year, nominal/real basis, event/effective/ingest time and scenario vintage. |

| Stock/flow | Reserve, inventory and capital stock are not annual consumption; contributions, draws, depreciation and service use are separate. |

| Transfer elimination | Eliminate only reconciled internal transfers and duplicate reimbursement; do not erase external resource cost. |

| Transition transfer | An enduring function exits the transition ledger and enters one operating category without duplicate booking. |

| Offset causality | Require baseline, mechanism, lag, attribution, uncertainty, interaction and rebound control before recognizing an offset. |

| Capacity constraint | Savings that violate required access, staffing, safety or readiness floors are not valid framework savings. |

| Matched comparison | Framework and comparator outputs use aligned scope, population, morbidity, geography, time, price and policy vintage. |

| Non-achievement | Equations compute results; they do not clip values to targets or force a requirement to pass. |
H.2 Mature-category, transition, and financing allocations
Table H-3. Mature cost categories

| ID | Category | CP | Boundary | Owner | Control |

| MC-01 | Hospital, facility, and emergency readiness | CP-HOSP | Operating global budgets, readiness, capital, service lines, rural/teaching/safety-net adjustments | ARCH-NHSA/HFASB/THDO | Hospital operating/capital/readiness/transition ledgers remain distinct |

| MC-02 | Physicians, specialists, and clinical services | CP-CLIN | Primary/complex care, specialist, clinician compensation, e-consult/tele-specialty and clinical team services | ARCH-AHWCS/NPCB/NSAA | Do not duplicate unit labor, hospital-employed labor, or education pipeline |

| MC-03 | Four-unit diagnostic-treatment network | CP-UNIT | Type A/B/C/D capital, operations, diagnostics, staffing, mobile reach, follow-up and maintenance | ARCH-OCDTI/NCDTN/RHA | Allocate shared labs/workforce once; constrain to staffed service-ready capacity |

| MC-04 | Long-term care | CP-LTC | Assessment, home/community/institutional services, caregiver support, DME/home modifications | ARCH-NLTCA | General income/housing excluded unless clinically linked; unpaid caregiver capacity not assumed |

| MC-05 | Drugs, pharmacy, and public manufacturing | CP-RX | Purchasing, pharmacy claims, dispensing, distribution, shortage, PMC production and quality | ARCH-PCU/NDPA/PMC | Separate product acquisition, dispensing, manufacturing capital/operation and R&D |

| MC-06 | Devices, labs, and diagnostics | CP-DX | Devices, diagnostic products, laboratory/imaging acquisition/interpretation, public production and maintenance | AMDDT authorities | Avoid duplicate testing and unit/hospital equipment/labor allocation |

| MC-07 | Behavioral health and SUD | CP-BH | Therapy, psychiatry, medication support, peer/recovery, crisis, inpatient/outpatient continuity | ARCH-NBHA | Separate from general clinical/hospital cost through service/location rule |

| MC-08 | Dental, vision, and hearing | CP-DVH | Prevention, treatment, exams, standard devices, fitting, repair and justified exceptions | ARCH-NDVHO | Device costs follow controlled product/service boundary |

| MC-09 | EMS and medical transport | CP-EMS | Readiness, dispatch, ground/air, treat/refer/transport, nonemergency transport and handoff | ARCH-NEMTA | Readiness cost is not allocated solely by trip volume |

| MC-10 | Public health, prevention, and linked supports | CP-PH | Surveillance, vaccination/screening, outbreak/climate response, prevention and clinically linked supports | ARCH-NPHPA/RHA | General social policy outside boundary; hospital/unit prevention not duplicated |

| MC-11 | Records, information, cybersecurity, and AI | CP-IT | Identity, registries, mesh, exchange, storage, portal, cyber/offline, AI validation/monitoring and vendor exit | ARCH-AHIRC/HCCA/AICIO | Shared platform allocated once; embedded vendor fees identified |

| MC-12 | Governance, claims, appeals, safety, and adaptation | CP-CLM; CP-GOV | Eligibility/claims administration, payment support, oversight, rights, appeals, safety, transparency, audit and repair | DNHA/NHAC/NHASB/CHAO | 0.25%–0.50% legitimacy allocation is a tagged subset, not the whole category |

| MC-13 | Biomedical innovation and R&D | CP-RD | Public R&D, trials, prizes/rewards, licensing, comparative effectiveness and coverage-with-evidence | ARCH-NBIA | Separate product payment/manufacturing; reconcile avoided monopoly cost only as tested offset |

| MC-14 | Professional education and workforce capacity | CP-EDU | Education slots, scholarships, fellowships, hubs, service obligations, rural pipeline and continuing education | ARCH-NHWECA/NHWB | Do not duplicate salaries already paid for service delivery |

Table H-5. Financing layers

| ID | Layer | CP | Basis | Measurement | Fallback |

| FL-01 | Redirected federal spending | CP-FIN-002 | Existing federal health spending redirected under conforming law | Baseline/program transfer; entitlement and population reconciliation | If conforming transfer delayed, protect benefits through mandatory federal bridge |

| FL-02 | State/local maintenance contribution | CP-FIN-003 | Controlled maintenance-of-effort/capacity contribution with fiscal/equalization treatment | State, local, territorial and tribal/direct-federal boundaries remain explicit | Statutory/default contribution and direct administration without service interruption |

| FL-03 | Employer Health Assurance Contribution | CP-FIN-004/018/019 | Predictable employer contribution replacing core sponsorship burden in part | Employer net savings and worker wage pass-through separately verified | Payroll enforcement, correction/restitution and small-business transition |

| FL-04 | Extreme-wealth financing | CP-FIN-005/009/010 | Progressive dedicated receipts administered by IRS/EWTAO | Certified legally due, collection, leakage, timing and court contingency | Mark-to-market, estate/dynasty, borrowing, exit and asset-excise fallbacks as law permits |

| FL-05 | High-income/capital-income taxes | CP-FIN-006 | Dedicated progressive high-income and capital-income receipts | Base/rate/timing/behavior and incidence require legislation/calibration | Alternative income/realization/deemed-sale/minimum-tax structures |

| FL-06 | Health-sector rent taxes | CP-FIN-007 | Targeted receipts from economic rents/extraction consistent with sector reform | Avoid taxing necessary clinical capacity or counting eliminated rent as both receipt and saving | Payment/charter/anti-extraction and general progressive layers |

| FL-07 | Residual broad backstop | CP-FIN-008/017/020 | Last-resort broad contribution activated only by registered stabilizer conditions | Ordinary-household incremental burden share <=5%; caps/relief/refund and expiry | Reserve draw, progressive-layer adjustment and statutory alternatives before broad burden |

Appendix J — Phase Roadmap and Phase Gates
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Integrate the 10–12-year planning sequence with domain work, independent evidence, protective gates, fallback and re-entry. |

| System entities | NHTCA; DNHA/ARCH owners; RHA/state/tribal partners; NHASB; NHAC/NOPRSL; CHAO; THDO/HFASB/NHETF; Article I court. |

| Assumptions | Calendar anchors are planning assumptions. Time passage never substitutes for gate evidence or extinguishes an individual right. |

| Data / parameters | Phase scope, products, exit evidence, domain roadmap, gate thresholds, evidence package, outcomes, review cadence and accountable roles. |

| Requirements / performance | PH-P0–P8; PH-G1–G8; PR-SCH/PR-TRN; VR-025/030; KPP/TPP; IF-028; risk/fallback records. |

| Principal risks | Schedule optimism; capacity lag; evidence gaming; broad conditional pass; state/vendor resistance; transition harm; premature sunset. |

| Simulation implication | Model phase/gate state by region/domain; progression, hold, bounded condition, rollback, re-entry, delay cost and continuity impact are endogenous. |
NO CALENDAR-ONLY PROGRESSION  A phase may overlap or vary regionally, but an affected scope cannot advance merely because its planning year arrived. Mandatory rights, safety, continuity and fiscal floors require independent evidence.
Table J-1. PH-P0–PH-P8 phase register

| ID | Anchor | Purpose | Controlled products / scope | Exit evidence |

| PH-P0 | Year 1 | Statutory and command foundation | Enabling statute; NHTCA; governing bodies; mandatory funding authorities; rights, scorekeeping, risk, transition, and configuration baselines | Core bodies legally established; accountable officials/interim succession; initial funds and controls available; PR-SCH-001 evidence |

| PH-P1 | Year 2 | Identity, registries, cyber, and legal defaults | Person/provider/facility/formulary/claims registries; health identity; cyber baseline; foundational records; legal fallback/default procedures | Authoritative registries demonstrated; access/correction and downtime prototypes; PR-SCH-002 evidence |

| PH-P2 | Year 3 | Pharmacy and purchasing first operation | Public pharmacy claims utility; national purchasing; PBM replacement; PMC Phase I; formulary and marshalling functions | End-to-end pharmacy claim/payment/fill continuity demonstrated; shortage and fallback controls; PR-SCH-003 evidence |

| PH-P3 | Year 4 | Public coverage Wave I | Coverage Wave I; claims rail; uninsured/ACA/Medicaid transition start; eligibility, payment, appeals, liquidity, and continuity operation | Wave I independently evaluated; Gate 1 floor before PH-P4; PR-SCH-004 evidence |

| PH-P4 | Year 6 | Delivery and hospital pilots | Hospital global-budget pilots; regional planning; representative Type A/B/C/D unit pilots; specialist-backplane pilots | Pilot safety/access/finance/workforce evidence; scale-or-repair decisions; PR-SCH-005 evidence |

| PH-P5 | Year 7 | Workforce and delivery scale | Workforce/education/scope reforms; unit network scaled; specialist capacity ledgers/protected urgent slots expanded | Unit coverage >=65% by phase end; workforce and routing readiness; PR-SCH-006 evidence |

| PH-P6 | Year 8 | National public default coverage | National default coverage; major covered-care cost-sharing elimination after Gate 2; payment, rights, transition, and regional operations scaled | Coverage/financial protection and capacity/safety constraints pass; PR-SCH-007 evidence |

| PH-P7 | Year 10 | Expanded benefits | LTC, behavioral health/SUD, dental, vision, hearing, EMS and linked public-health/service capacity expand after Gate 3 | Assessment/access/workforce/home-care/readiness evidence; benefit and appeal operations; PR-SCH-008 evidence |

| PH-P8 | Year 12 | Full integration and maturity certification | Mature manufacturing; information mesh; innovation delinkage; mature payment; fiscal/legitimacy/adaptation integration | All maturity targets assessed; Gate 4 and cross-domain certification; PR-SCH-009 evidence; unresolved defects retained in repair plan |

J.2 Protective phase gates
Table J-3. PH-G1–PH-G8 gate register

| ID | Gate | Decision point | Blocking floor / condition | Evidence / trace | Fallback / repair |

| PH-G1 | Claims readiness | Before major expansion and specifically PH-P3 to PH-P4 | Clean-claim auto-adjudication >=75% for Wave I; payment timeliness; eligibility latency; provider cash-flow disruption within approved floors | PR-SCH-010; TPP-2.1/2.2/2.4; operational logs and timestamped Treasury data | Hold/resize expansion; provisional/manual payment; liquidity protection; root-cause repair |

| PH-G2 | Unit capacity | Before broad cost-sharing elimination | Unit population coverage >=80%; unsafe under-referral <=5/10,000 non-escalated encounters; same-day access and follow-up closure meet approved floors | PR-SCH-011/012; KPP-B2/B7/B8/B9; clinical review and stratified access data | Retain protected cost-sharing bridge where lawful; add staff/sites/mobile capacity; repair routing/escalation |

| PH-G3 | LTC and workforce readiness | Before full expanded-benefit rollout | LTC assessment timeliness >=85%; critical vacancy, home-care sufficiency, BH first-contact, DVH/EMS readiness meet approved floors | PR-SCH-013; TPP-8.1/9.1–9.7; workforce and service records | Limit wave/scope; maintain existing entitlement; surge/contract/train capacity; reassess and re-enter |

| PH-G4 | Fiscal readiness | Before mature full-benefit/maturity certification | Dedicated revenue sufficiency >=98%; reserves >=6 months volatile exposure; wealth collection efficiency and stabilizer readiness meet approved floors | PR-SCH-014; KPP-C5/C6; TPP-6.4; actuarially certified obligations/receipts/reserves | Hold maturity; activate authorized stabilizer/reserve/revenue corrections; publish forecast-error review |

| PH-G5 | AI safety readiness | Before national AI-assisted routing | High-stakes human-review/audit capture >=97%; validation, protected-group comparison, drift, override, suspension, and manual fallback meet approved floors | PR-SCH-015; TPP-11.4–11.6; model-version-specific validation and logs | Restrict to validated bounded pilots or suspend; use human/manual path; review affected cases |

| PH-G6 | Records and cyber readiness | Before national record reliance | Access/correction/segmentation, API conformance, uptime, vulnerability remediation, downtime continuity and reconciliation meet approved floors | SR-DATA-001–012; TPP-10.1–10.6/11.1–11.3; tests, logs, drills and user testing | Continue federated/legacy/manual dependencies; remediate; repeat drill and representative usability test |

| PH-G7 | Legitimacy readiness | Before large-scale coverage conversion | Rights, usable appeal, no-silent-rationing explanation, ombudsman, public reporting, trust baseline and safety-reporting controls meet approved floors | SR-RGT/SR-EQ; TPP-LEG1/USE1/USE2/12.4/12.6; KPP-TRUST1; case audits and representative tests | Hold/resize conversion; improve notice/navigation/relief; independent review; confidence repair |

| PH-G8 | Transition continuity readiness | Before major legacy payer sunset | Active treatment/medication/record transfer, state/tribal compact or fallback, provider liquidity, open appeal/authorization ownership and legacy reconciliation meet approved floors | PR-TRN; KPP-T1/T2; TPP-12.1/12.5/TRIB1; pre/post patient-level evidence | Maintain legacy/dual-run/bridge duty; protect payments/care; correct transfer; recertify scoped sunset |
Table J-4. Gateway floor versus mature target

| Gate | Measure | Progression floor | Mature target | Interpretation |

| PH-G1 | Clean-claim auto-adjudication | >=75% Wave I to move P3→P4 | TPP-2.1 >=95% by P8 | Gateway floor permits next bounded phase; it is not mature claims performance |

| PH-G2 | Unit population coverage | >=80% before broad cost-sharing elimination | KPP-B7 >=95% within access standard by P8 | P5 milestone is >=65%; gateway floor is 80%; maturity is 95% |

| PH-G2 | Unsafe under-referral | <=5 per 10,000 non-escalated encounters | KPP-B9 <=3 per 10,000 | Progression floor is less stringent than maturity and still requires clinical-record review |

| PH-G3 | LTC assessment timeliness | >=85% before full expansion | TPP-9.1 >=95% | Expansion floor does not end improvement obligation |

| PH-G4 | Dedicated revenue sufficiency | >=98% before mature certification | KPP-C5 >=100% obligations | Temporary gap cannot be labeled mature sufficiency |

| PH-G4 | Stabilization reserves | >=6 months volatile exposure | KPP-C6 >=12 months by P8 | Six months is a certification floor; twelve months is mature adequacy |

| PH-G5 | High-stakes AI review/audit capture | >=97% before national routing | TPP-11.5 >=99% | National deployment remains monitored and can be restricted below maturity |
J.3 Universal gate evidence and outcomes
Table J-5. Required gate-evidence fields

| Field | Required content |

| decision scope | Named phase transition, deployment, benefit expansion, record reliance, AI use, conversion, or payer sunset; affected regions/populations/functions |

| requirement baseline | Exact PR/SR/KPP/TPP/VR versions, gateway floors, mature targets, exclusions, approved open issues, and legal authority |

| operational exposure | Representative sites/populations, sufficient volume/time, surge/failure scenarios, unresolved exceptions, and comparison period |

| data/metric package | Owner, numerator/denominator, source, lineage, quality, frequency, Formula Registry version, stratification, uncertainty, and reproducible result |

| test/evaluation | Inspection, analysis, test, or demonstration protocol; entry/exit; observed outputs; pass/fail; independent sampling/audit |

| rights/safety/equity | Patient/provider notices, appeal usability, safety review, subgroup results, protected continuity, complaints, provisional relief, and remedy |

| capacity/fiscal | Staffed capacity, suppliers/facilities, payment/liquidity, obligated funding, reserves/contingency, and cost/schedule exposure |

| risk/fallback | Open findings, risk/FMEA state, corrective actions, residual risk, containment, rollback, manual/offline/legacy bridge, and re-entry plan |

| certification/publication | Operator attestation, independent verifier result, NHAC/CHAO observations where applicable, accountable decision, conditions/expiry, and public report |
Table J-6. Gate outcome states

| State | Decision rule | Required effect |

| pass | All blocking floors and evidence conditions are met for the defined scope | Authorize only the stated progression; continue monitoring toward mature targets |

| conditional_bounded | A non-rights/non-safety evidence gap has a controlled containment and does not invalidate a mandatory floor | Authorize limited scope/time with named condition, expiry, monitoring, verifier, rollback, and public reason |

| hold | A blocking floor, evidence sufficiency, independent verification, rights, safety, equity, fiscal, or continuity condition fails | Do not advance affected scope; protect existing obligations; execute corrective plan |

| rollback_or_repair | Post-pass monitoring reveals material defect, harm, invalid data/formula, or condition breach | Return to protected predecessor/bridge or restrict affected function; remedy and re-enter gate |
J.4 Assurance roles and reviews
Table J-7. Assurance roles

| Actor | Role | Constraint |

| NHTCA | Integrated transition/program command; master schedule; dependency, wave, risk, continuity, and corrective-action integration | Cannot independently certify its own phase exit |

| DNHA and ARCH owners | Design/build/operate work packages; maintain requirements, evidence, configuration, training, fallback, cost and operational readiness | Accountable for truth of operator evidence and immediate containment |

| RHA/state/tribal compact bodies | Regional execution, capacity planning, local data, compacts/waivers, provider/facility readiness, community engagement | National floors and tribal sovereignty/direct pathways remain binding |

| THDO/HFASB/NHETF | Obligation, disbursement, revenue, reserve, provider-liquidity and fiscal-readiness evidence | Fiscal records reconcile to actuarial/Formula Registry basis |

| NHASB | Independent scorekeeping, formula verification, gate certification, retrospective/sunset review, red team, corrective-effectiveness review | Organizational, data, budget, and conflict safeguards protect independence |

| NHAC/NOPRSL | Rights, safety, equity, privacy, appeal usability, public legitimacy and patient/provider remedy oversight | Can require correction/relief and publish objections; does not operate benefits/payment |

| CHAO | Congressional audit of legality, funding, performance, implementation risk, capture, and reported evidence | Legislative oversight is distinct from executive gate operation |

| A1-HCAC | Expedited enforceable claims, care, payment, rights, and anti-impoundment remedies | Court review remains available as specified; a gate cannot extinguish a claim or right |
Table J-8. Readiness and retrospective reviews

| Review | Timing | Minimum content |

| Architecture baseline review | Before committed implementation baseline | Needs, requirements, ARCH/IF/data allocation, legal authority, assumptions, risks, cost/schedule, alternatives and open issues are coherent |

| Detailed design/configuration review | Before build/procurement or major change | Interfaces, data, formulas, security/privacy, human workflow, testability, vendor exit, capacity, fallback and traceability are complete |

| Test readiness review | Before formal test/demonstration | Procedure, environment, representative users/sites/data, entry/exit, expected output, instruments, defects, safety stop and independent witnesses are ready |

| Operational readiness review | Before wave/pilot/service activation | Staffing/training, facilities/suppliers, payment, records, support, notices/appeals, incident command, downtime/manual path and rollback are ready |

| Phase-gate review | At controlled progression decision | Universal gate package, applicable PH-G evidence, open findings, corrective effectiveness, residual risk, conditions and publication are complete |

| Post-implementation review | After sufficient operating exposure | Benefits/harms, access, cost, safety, equity, rights, workforce, trust, continuity, defects and displacement effects are measured |

| Maturity/sunset review | At P8 or statutory review date | Mature targets, fiscal durability, institutional performance, legal resilience, repair portfolio, function transfer, reauthorization or sunset are independently assessed |
Appendix K — Governing Agency Catalog
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Publish the complete institutional topology, including constitutional actors, operating bodies, funds, oversight/courts, transition bodies and innovation institutions. |

| System entities | ARCH-CONG through ARCH-SRAE; external providers, states/regions, tribal nations and market actors connected through contracts/compacts/interfaces. |

| Assumptions | An ARCH record establishes a design element, not enactment, funding, staffing or performance. Statutory composition remains subject to Section 9 controls. |

| Data / parameters | ID, layer, canonical name, role, requirement family, interfaces, lifecycle, separation constraint and status. |

| Requirements / performance | ARCH catalog; SR-ARCH-001–015; domain PR/SR; IF-001–032; PH; VR; legal and financing architecture. |

| Principal risks | Role overlap; self-verification; executive interference; capture; vacancy; temporary-body permanence; orphan function; unfunded mandate. |

| Simulation implication | Represent agencies as accountable agents with authority, capacity, vacancy, funding, information, decision, fallback and oversight states. |
ARCHITECTURE VERSUS ENACTMENT  The 82 records are the controlled design catalog. They do not claim that Congress has enacted, funded or staffed any element, and they do not resolve appointment/removal rules under OI-019.
