Appendix L — Legal Conforming Changes
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Convert the Section 9 legal architecture into a controlled legislative-counsel and implementation inventory without drafting pseudo-statute or treating unresolved constitutional design as settled. |

| System entities | Congress; DNHA; Treasury/THDO; NHAC; NHASB; CHAO; A1-HCAC; federal program agencies; states; RHAs; tribal nations; courts and accountable operators. |

| Assumptions | The National Health Assurance and Health System Transition Act remains a working title. A cataloged provision is not enacted, funded or legally sufficient merely because it appears here. |

| Data / parameters | Title/function/assurance crosswalk; federal and state law domains; compact fields; hardening and fallback records; legal state; requirement/evidence links. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-ARCH-001–015; SR-EQ-008–010; SR-LAW-001–010; VR-015/019/022/024–026; Section 9; Appendix K. |

| Principal risks | Orphan duties; preemption error; tribal trust-duty erosion; invalid authority; impoundment; nonactivating fallback; transition discontinuity. |

| Simulation implication | Represent statute titles, program dispositions, authority states, fallback activation, legal lag, continuity and distributional deltas as explicit stateful objects. |
COUNSEL CONTROL  This appendix supplies drafting instructions and reconciliation fields. It does not provide bill text, a constitutional opinion or legal certification; OI-061–OI-070 remain controlling.
L.1 Enabling-act title architecture
The nineteen-title structure keeps entitlement, financing, operations, rights, transition, anti-sabotage and repair functions separable. Conforming amendments must point each legacy function to one disposition and one accountable custodian.
Table L-1. National Health Assurance and Health System Transition Act — title catalog

| Title | Name | Function | Assurance control |

| I | National Health Assurance Entitlement | Coverage entitlement, benefit rights, medical necessity, point-of-care protection | Patient rights; review; no silent rationing |

| II | Financing and Trust Funds | Dedicated receipts, NHA-TRUST/NHETF accounts, mandatory funding, reserves | Fiscal certification; account integrity |

| III | Enrollment and Public Default Coverage | Automatic/default enrollment, eligibility, identity, continuity | No coverage gap; correction and appeal |

| IV | Claims, Payment, and Appeals | NCCA/THDO payment rail, clean claims, provider rights, Article I review | Payment clocks; deemed allowance; judicial remedy |

| V | Drugs, Devices, Diagnostics, and Public Manufacturing | Purchasing, PCU, access, licensing, PMC and public production | Quality, shortage, competition and access |

| VI | Hospitals and Public-Service Charters | Global budgets, charter duties, capital/readiness, service continuity | Access, staffing, service-line and related-party controls |

| VII | Workforce, Education, Compensation, and Scope | Workforce bodies, education, compensation, federal scope floors | Safety, labor transition, rural distribution |

| VIII | LTC, Behavioral Health, DVH, and EMS | Expanded benefits, assessments, service authorities and continuity | Timeliness, integration and rights |

| IX | Records, Data Rights, Cybersecurity, and AI | Information Mesh, data charter, security, segmentation, AI accountability | Human accountability, audit, downtime continuity |

| X | Public Health and Prevention | Surveillance, prevention, emergency and population-health functions | Federal/state coordination and civil rights |

| XI | Biomedical Innovation | NBIA funding, trials, licensing, prizes and public-interest conditions | Access, evidence and research integrity |

| XII | Fraud, Abuse, and Anti-Extraction | Integrity enforcement, ownership transparency, anti-extraction controls | Due process; recovery; no capacity harm |

| XIII | State, Regional, and Tribal Transition | Compacts, RHA administration, preemption, tribal direct pathways, fallback | Trust duties; continuity; non-veto |

| XIV | Tax and Wealth Financing | Revenue bases, administration, incidence safeguards and fallback authorities | Sufficiency, burden, legality and review |

| XV | Transition Protection | NHTCA, continuity funds, worker/provider/patient safeguards, legacy wind-down | No unmanaged transition gap |

| XVI | Legitimacy and Safety | Bill of Rights, ombudsman, appeals, diagnostics, equity, transparency | Explainability, appealability and audit |

| XVII | Anti-Impoundment and Continuity | Mandatory payment, apportionment defaults, standing, remedies, escrow | 24-hour action; continuity |

| XVIII | Adaptation, Scorekeeping, and Repair | NHASB, Formula Registry, review, waiver, emergency repair, sunset | Independent evidence; bounded change |

| XIX | Conforming Amendments | Federal cross-statute changes, transition clauses and legacy disposition | No conflict, orphan duty or coverage gap |
L.2 Disposition and non-orphaning control
Table L-2. Appendix-local disposition vocabulary

| Local key | Disposition | Meaning | Required continuity evidence |

| L-DSP-preserve | Preserve | Function and authority continue with conforming references only | Named custodian, current funding, records and appeal route remain operative |

| L-DSP-transfer | Transfer | Function, assets, liabilities, workforce and records move to a named NHA owner | Dual-run or bridge; transfer acceptance and reconciliation evidence |

| L-DSP-parallel | Protected parallel | Distinct federal or tribal duty remains alongside NHA | No benefit diminution; interface and funding responsibilities explicit |

| L-DSP-supersede | Supersede | NHA rule replaces a conflicting substitute-coverage or payment rule | No gap; preserved pending rights and more-protective compatible rules |

| L-DSP-sunset | Sunset | Authority closes only after all duties and cases are transferred or certified complete | No orphan appeal, debt, liability, record, contract or workforce obligation |

| L-DSP-fallback | Fallback-ready | Primary authority remains, with a pretested substitute activated by controlled evidence | Owner, trigger, funding, data, capacity, rights, RTO and return condition |
Inventory every function, population, fund, asset, liability, contract, record, authorization, appeal, workforce cohort and enforcement duty.
Assign one primary disposition and a named custodian; record dependencies and any protected parallel duty.
Define effective-time, bridge, reconciliation, fallback, remedy, retention and sunset conditions.
Test no-gap and no-orphan conditions before activation and again before legacy closure.
Publish the disposition crosswalk and preserve historical reproduction and pending-case rights.
L.3 Federal conforming-change inventory
Table L-3. Federal statute and program domains

| Domain | Laws/programs | Required action | Continuity control |

| Coverage/financing programs | Medicare; Medicaid; CHIP; ACA; FEHBA; TRICARE; VA | Map populations, benefits, funds, claims, liabilities and appeals into NHA or protected parallel channels | No beneficiary, provider or pending-appeal gap; preserve VA/TRICARE/IHS-specific duties until explicit transfer |

| Employer/insurance | ERISA; McCarran-Ferguson; insurance law interfaces | Define public-default preemption, supplemental coverage, employer contribution and wage-pass-through treatment | Protect collective bargaining, restitution, state safety authority and lawful supplemental markets |

| Tax/revenue | Internal Revenue Code; payroll/reporting provisions | Create dedicated financing bases, credits, reporting, collection, fallback and transition rules | Incidence guard, due process, anti-avoidance, certified yield and severability |

| Drugs/devices/innovation | FDCA; patent law; Hatch-Waxman; Bayh-Dole; Orphan Drug Act; BPCIA | Enable purchasing, public-interest licensing, government use, evidence and public manufacturing while preserving safety review | FDA quality independence; compensation; innovation/access evidence |

| Controlled substances | Controlled Substances Act | Align prescribing, dispensing, telehealth and SUD continuity with NHA clinical pathways | Diversion controls without care interruption or discriminatory barriers |

| Data/privacy | HIPAA; HITECH; 21st Century Cures; 42 CFR Part 2 | Authorize Mesh exchange, patient rights, correction, segmentation, purpose limitation and federated identity | More-protective privacy, tribal governance, minor/adolescent and sensitive-data rules |

| Fraud/referral/payment | Anti-Kickback; Stark; False Claims Act | Conform public budgets, salaries, referrals, integrity enforcement and recovery to new payment architecture | Safe harbors cannot legalize extraction; due process and whistleblower protections remain |

| Public health/federal systems | Public Health Service Act; Indian Health Care Improvement Act | Authorize national/regional public health, direct tribal funding and federal trust-duty integration | No diminution of tribal obligations; emergency and state coordination |

| Administration/appropriation | Impoundment Control Act; APA | Create mandatory payment, anti-delay remedies, default rules and bounded rulemaking/repair pathways | Notice, evidence, review, emergency expiry and judicial enforcement |

| Competition/corporate | Antitrust; corporate law; nonprofit hospital rules | Address consolidation, ownership, related parties, public-service charters and asset disposition | Preserve necessary capacity; transparent valuation and due process |

| Household protection | Medical debt; consumer-credit statutes | Prohibit or remediate covered-care debt and reporting; govern legacy debt transition | Correction, restitution, limitation periods and appeals |

| Field group | Required content |

| identity/authority | parties, geography, legal authority, effective/sunset dates, amendment and dispute forum |

PREEMPTION AND SOVEREIGNTY  The controlled preemption test reaches rules that prevent, frustrate, duplicate or materially interfere with NHA, while protecting compatible health, safety, licensure, discipline, public-health, supplemental-coverage and more-protective authority. Tribal trust duties, direct funding and tribal-approved verification cannot be reduced or routed through a state veto.
L.5 Executive hardening and legal fallback
Table L-6. Executive-hardening controls

| ID | Control | Rule/target | Trigger | Remedy/default |

| EH-01 | Statutory entitlement | Core covered benefits and enforceable rights are fixed by statute | Benefit restriction outside statutory process | A1-HCAC/district review; continued lawful default |

| EH-02 | Permanent mandatory appropriations | At least 99.5% of core spending under payment protection by P8 | Missing/withheld discretionary action | Treasury payment duty and judicial enforcement |

| EH-03 | Deemed/default apportionment | Formula-based apportionment occurs when ordinary process fails | Deadline passes without lawful apportionment | Registered default amount; narrower fallback if challenged |

| EH-04 | Direct Treasury disbursement | THDO pays certified obligations without policy repricing | Certified obligation reaches payment clock | Deemed payment/remedy, interest and court order |

| EH-05 | Payment rights/defaults | Clean-claim deemed allowance; provider/hospital/pharmacy rights | Agency fails adjudication/payment clock | Provisional/deemed allowance subject to later reconciliation |

| EH-06 | Vacancy-proof governance | Acting succession; no duty failure for vacancy/quorum; continuity >=99% | Vacancy, no quorum or appointment failure | Delegated statutory actor and automatic duty continuation |

| EH-07 | Staffing/anti-hollowing | Critical-office staffing >=98%; no freeze/RIF below floor; direct hire | Vacancy threshold or prohibited staffing action | Direct-hire and enforceable restoration |

| EH-08 | Oversight and remedies | CHAO oversight; standing; Article I and district-court routes | Delay, suppression, unlawful narrowing or impoundment | 24-hour action initiation; injunction/mandamus/payment relief |

| EH-09 | Systems/data continuity | Public data/systems escrow, continuity contracts, portable records and vendor exit | Operator/vendor refusal, termination or outage | Escrow release, step-in rights and offline operation |

| EH-10 | Anti-regulatory sabotage | Automatic defaults for formulary, budgets, claims, LTC, compensation and reporting | Required regulation missing/invalid/withdrawn | Last lawful or statutory default rule with public notice and repair |

| EH-11 | Anti-impoundment | Automated delay flag and action within 24 hours | Unlawful withholding, deferral, transfer or administrative obstruction | Direct payment, expedited review, personal/office accountability as enacted |

| EH-12 | State/regional fallback | Direct federal administration and continuity contracts are preauthorized | Compact refusal, breach or incapacity threatens service | Temporary federal operation with cure/reentry plan |

| SR-LAW-005 | The system shall prohibit reduction of staffing below statutory floors by government-wide hiring freeze, reorganization, personnel ceiling, or reduction in force. Trace: SN-13, SN-09. Verification: Inspection. | Legal Hardening, Continuity, and Anti-Sabotage Requirements |

| SR-LAW-006 | The system shall maintain statutory acting succession for every critical Senate-confirmed health office. Trace: SN-13. Verification: Inspection. | Legal Hardening, Continuity, and Anti-Sabotage Requirements |

Trace: SN-13, SN-21. Verification: Inspection. | Legal Hardening, Continuity, and Anti-Sabotage Requirements |

| SR-LAW-009 | The system shall maintain legal contingency coverage for at least 99% of critical provisions by Phase 8. Trace: SN-21. Verification: Inspection. | Legal Hardening, Continuity, and Anti-Sabotage Requirements |

| SR-LAW-010 | The system shall prohibit executive or contractor suppression of required public performance data. Trace: SN-13, SN-20. Verification: Inspection. | Legal Hardening, Continuity, and Anti-Sabotage Requirements |

| VR-015 | Every transition-continuity requirement shall be verified using pre-migration and post-migration patient-level continuity records. | Verification Requirements |

| VR-019 | Every legal-hardening requirement shall be verified using statutory text, appropriations classification, disbursement logs, vacancy records, staffing records, and litigation records. | Verification Requirements |

| VR-022 | Every emergency repair action shall be verified against change-control tier, authority, expiration date, public notice, and ratification status. | Verification Requirements |

| VR-024 | Every trust-fund and fiscal-sufficiency requirement shall be verified using actuarially certified obligations, receipts, transfers, balances, and reserve calculations. | Verification Requirements |

| VR-025 | Every requirement used to block or permit phase progression shall require independent verification before the next phase may begin. | Verification Requirements |

| VR-026 | Every tribal compact requirement shall be verified through tribal-approved documentation and shall not rely solely on state certification. | Verification Requirements |
Simulation must preserve at least: primary authority state, challenged scope, order/effective time, fallback trigger, activation lag, owner readiness, funding/data/capacity continuity, affected populations and obligations, rights/remedies, distributional delta, restoration condition and reconciliation status. Legal modules may explore consequences; they may not certify legality.

Appendix M — Transition Playbook
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Provide the operating sequence and evidence contract for converting populations, functions, providers, facilities, records, payments, jurisdictions and workforces without an unmanaged gap. |

| System entities | NHTCA; PCO; PLCCO; HESSO; PDCO; HATC; SRCO; TRTO; EPTO; LPWO; DMRCO; TLSHO; TRPGO; operators and independent verifiers. |

| Assumptions | Every wave is evidence-gated and retains a bounded dual-run or continuity bridge, exception queues, liquidity protection, rollback and accountable exit certification. |

| Data / parameters | Wave charter; exposure denominator; architecture/interfaces; readiness evidence; transition states; continuity guarantees; incidents; reconciliations and closure certificate. |

| Requirements / performance | PR-TRN-001–010; SR-IF-014; PH-P0–P8/PH-G1–G8; KPP-T1/T2/W1; TPP-EMP1/TRIB1/12.1/12.5; VR-008/009/015/016/025/026/030. |

| Principal risks | Care/medication interruption; provider insolvency; capacity loss; migration error; worker displacement; compact failure; cyber outage; premature legacy sunset. |

| Simulation implication | Model each wave as an exposure-weighted state machine with dual-run duration, exception queues, liquidity, capacity, incident propagation, rollback and certification outputs. |
NO-GAP RULE  Conversion may change payer, process, budget, purchasing, data or employment arrangements, but it may not leave any patient, provider, facility, pharmacy, jurisdiction, employer or worker in an unmanaged gap.
M.1 Transition command architecture
Table M-1. Transition architecture and accountability

| Entity | Function | Operating contract | Boundary |

| ARCH-NHTCA | Transition command | Integrated wave plan, continuity state, incident command, gates and stabilization | Time-limited; no-later-than-Year-15 sunset absent affirmative extension |

| ARCH-PCO | Patient continuity | Active treatment, medication, referral, appeal, authorization and care-plan migration | Provisional bridge and accountable case owner |

| ARCH-PLCCO | Provider liquidity | Claims continuity, provisional Treasury payment, reconciliation and complaints | No provider bears public-rail failure without remedy |

| ARCH-HESSO | Hospital/essential service | Stabilization corridor, service-line, staffing and regional continuity | Corridor is temporary, evidenced and reconciled |

| ARCH-PDCO | Pharmacy/drug continuity | Pharmacy onboarding, formulary bridge, emergency fill and medication continuity | Critical regimens receive no-interruption protection |

| ARCH-HATC | Worker transition | Eligibility, income bridge, training, placement and retention | Tracks meaningful placement, not referral alone |

| ARCH-SRCO / ARCH-TRTO | State, regional, tribal and rural | Compacts, direct federal fallback, sovereignty, funding, rural continuity and data governance | State cannot veto federal entitlement or tribal participation |

| ARCH-EPTO | Employer/payroll | Contribution conversion, payroll interfaces and wage-pass-through compliance | Worker premium relief and wage treatment remain separately auditable |

| ARCH-LPWO / ARCH-DMRCO | Legacy wind-down and data | Runout, liabilities, appeals, records, authorizations, cleaning and reconciliation | Legacy duty persists until transfer/closure certification |

| ARCH-TLSHO / ARCH-TRPGO | Legal safe harbor and risk/gates | Bounded transition safe harbors, dispute resolution, risk state and gate packages | No safe harbor waives patient safety, fraud, rights or mandatory payment |
M.2 Wave lifecycle
Table M-2. Controlled transition states

| State | Meaning | Guard/output |

| baseline.inventory | People, providers, plans, services, authorizations, records, liabilities and dependencies are enumerated | Population/asset reconciliation and unresolved-case queue |

| readiness.verified | Target rails, capacity, rights, cyber/offline, liquidity and fallback pass wave criteria | Independent evidence package; no schedule-only approval |

| dual_run_or_bridge | Legacy and public mechanisms overlap or continuity guarantees substitute safely | Duplicate/conflict ledger and bounded duration |

| wave.converted | Defined population, region, provider or function moves to public operation | Effective time, notices, owner and rollback point |

| stabilizing | Exceptions, complaints, data mismatches, cash flow and service continuity are actively resolved | Daily/weekly thresholds and corrective authority |

| wave.certified | Continuity, payment, records, rights, compacts and financial reconciliation meet exit criteria | Legacy duty can close only for certified scope |

| rolled_back_or_paused | Safety, continuity, capacity, legal, fiscal or cyber threshold fails | Protected return/bridge; root cause and re-entry gate |
Table M-3. Operator wave sequence

| Local key | Step | Required action | Evidence/output |

| M-STEP-01 | Baseline | Enumerate exposed people, obligations, providers, facilities, records, authorizations, contracts and dependencies | Signed population/object reconciliation; unresolved queue |

| M-STEP-02 | Design wave | Define population, geography, functions, effective time, owners, interfaces, continuity bridge and rollback point | Versioned wave charter and dependency map |

| M-STEP-03 | Verify readiness | Test capacity, payment, records, notices, appeals, staffing, cyber/offline, liquidity and jurisdictional path | Independent readiness evidence; open findings |

| M-STEP-04 | Authorize | Apply the relevant PH gate and universal evidence contract | Pass, bounded condition, hold, rollback or repair decision |

| M-STEP-05 | Dual run/bridge | Operate bounded overlap or continuity substitute; reconcile duplicates and contradictions | Exception ledger, manual-path status and daily/weekly controls |

| M-STEP-06 | Convert | Move the authorized scope; issue notices; preserve case ownership and effective-time lineage | Conversion event and rollback checkpoint |

| M-STEP-07 | Stabilize | Resolve care, medication, payment, data, staffing, rights, capacity and compact exceptions | Threshold trend, remedies, corrective actions and residual risk |

| M-STEP-08 | Certify/close | Independently verify continuity and reconcile obligations before closing legacy duty | Scope-specific certificate; retained evidence; re-entry/repair if failed |

Appendix N — Legitimacy and Safety Playbook
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Make patient and provider rights executable at the decision event and connect adverse decisions, safety events, appeals, remedies, learning and public accountability. |

| System entities | NHAC; NOPRSL; HRPO; PROO; A1-HCAC; NPSMIB; HAAO; PRTO; clinical/payment operators; NHASB; patients and providers. |

| Assumptions | No denial, delay, deprioritization, rerouting or refusal of covered care may rest on an invisible quota, missing-capacity fiction, unreviewed AI output or unusable remedy. |

| Data / parameters | Rights charter; decision record; rationing test; appeal state; safety event; remedy execution; reversal/complaint/trust/equity measures and affected-case cohort. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-RGT-001–012; SR-EQ-001–010; SR-AI-010; KPP-D6/D7/T-ED-001–T-ED-005/TRUST1/CULT1; TPP-LEG1/USE1/USE2/12.4/12.6; VR-004/006/007/010–014/028/029. |

| Principal risks | Silent rationing; inaccessible notice; unsafe delay; AI authority substitution; suppressed event; inequity; retaliation; late or unenforced remedy; trust collapse. |

| Simulation implication | Represent decisions, notices, urgency, human review, provisional relief, appeals, safety events, remedies, reversals, subgroup effects and learning as linked event records. |
RIGHTS AS CONTROLS  Rights attach to the event through usable notice, case-specific explanation, accountable human review, urgency, provisional protection, evidence access, appeal, remedy, correction and system learning.
N.1 Rights charter
Table N-1. Executable rights

| Right | Operational meaning | Evidence/remedy |

| Covered care and continuity | Receive covered medically necessary care without silent financial, administrative or capacity exclusion | Coverage/benefit record; provisional protection; appeal/remedy |

| Explanation | Know facts, rule/version, evidence, accountable authority, timing and reason for a material decision | TPP-LEG1; decision record |

| Human review | Obtain accountable human review of high-stakes AI-influenced or adverse decisions | SR-AI-010; TPP-11.5 |

| Appeal and provisional relief | File accessibly, preserve urgency, obtain interim protection where required and receive enforceable remedy | TPP-USE2/12.6; IF-021/022 |

| Records and privacy | Access, correct, see disclosures, control applicable consent/segmentation and challenge misuse | TPP-10.5; IF-017 |

| Safety and disclosure | Have abnormal results closed, serious incidents learned from, and injury/remedy processes available | KPP-D6; SR-RGT-006/007 |

| Language/disability usability | Use services, notices and remedies in accessible language and form | KPP-E5; SR-RGT-008/009 |

| Equity and civil rights | Receive protected, stratified monitoring and corrective action without discriminatory routing or burden | SR-EQ; IF-032 |

| No retaliation | Report, complain, appeal, decline informal caregiving, or request accommodation without retaliation | NHAC/PROO enforcement |
Table N-2. Material-decision record

| Field group | Required content |

| identity | decision/case/event ID; person/provider/service; urgency; accountable authority; timestamps |

| rule | statutory, clinical, budgetary or evidence-based rule; version; scope; effective date |

| facts | clinical, functional, preference, capacity, accommodation and protected-context facts used or missing |

| reasoning | case-specific explanation connecting facts, rule and outcome; alternatives considered |

| AI/automation | model/version/use class, input/output provenance, human reviewer, override and suspension state |

| notice/usability | language, format, disability accommodation, channel, delivery/comprehension evidence and assistance |

| protection | urgency screen, provisional relief, continuity, medication and safety steps |

| review/remedy | reconsideration/rights/court path, evidence access, clock, decision, remedy and compliance |

| equity/safety | stratified effect, incident linkage, retaliation protection and corrective action |

| learning | appeal outcome, reversal category, affected-case cohort, root cause, repair and public aggregate |
N.2 No Silent Rationing test
Table N-3. Rationing-control test

| Test | Required evidence | Failure condition |

| Rule exists | A statutory, clinical, budgetary or evidence-based rule controls the decision | No informal custom, undisclosed quota or missing-capacity fiction |

| Rule is valid | Current version, authorized owner, evidence, scope and effective date are present | Expired, unpublished or out-of-scope rule fails |

| Facts are complete | Relevant clinical, functional, preference, capacity and accommodation facts are considered | Missing facts trigger correction/provisional treatment, not automatic denial |

| Reason is explicit | The decision shows how facts and rule produce the outcome | Template language without case application fails |

| Human authority | Named accountable reviewer validates the material decision | AI/vendor/system owner cannot replace legal/clinical authority |

| Notice is usable | Language, disability, channel, timing, urgency and next steps meet standards | Delivery alone is not comprehension |

| Review is effective | Appeal, provisional relief, evidence access and remedy can occur before avoidable harm | A technically available but unusable or too-late appeal fails |

| System learns | Outcome, reversal, safety/equity effect and corrective action update oversight | Repeated high-reversal categories trigger review |
N.3 Trigger, appeal and remedy paths
Table N-4. Legitimacy/safety trigger matrix

| Local key | Trigger class | Immediate protection/action | Owner | Trace |

| N-TRG-01 | Adverse coverage/care decision | Explain rule/facts; preserve urgency; human review; provisional relief screen | ARCH-NOPRSL / ARCH-HRPO | SR-RGT; TPP-LEG1/USE2 |

| N-TRG-02 | Delay, deprioritization or non-referral | Apply No Silent Rationing test; expose capacity/routing state; expedite if harm risk | ARCH-PROO / ARCH-NSAA | IF-021/022; VR-011/014 |

| N-TRG-03 | Serious safety or diagnostic event | Protect, disclose/notify, preserve evidence, investigate and remedy | ARCH-NPSMIB | KPP-D6/D7; IF-031 |

| N-TRG-04 | AI-influenced high-stakes decision | Suspend/restrict affected version where indicated; accountable human review | ARCH-AICIO / ARCH-NOPRSL | SR-AI-010; VR-006/007/011 |

| N-TRG-05 | Record/privacy/consent dispute | Access/correct/segment; disclosure accounting; protect sensitive data; review misuse | ARCH-NHRA / ARCH-NHAC | IF-017; TPP-10.5 |

| N-TRG-06 | Language, disability or access barrier | Provide accessible channel/assistance; reset unusable notice or deadline as law requires | ARCH-HRPO / ARCH-PROO | KPP-E5; VR-010 |

| N-TRG-07 | Equity or retaliation signal | Protect reporter/service; stratify evidence; independent corrective action | ARCH-NHAC | SR-EQ; IF-032; VR-004 |

| N-TRG-08 | Trust/complaint/reversal pattern | Category review, service/rule repair, affected-case review and public report | ARCH-NHASB / ARCH-NHAC | KPP-TRUST1; SR-ADP-007/011; VR-028 |
Table N-5. Appeal and remedy states

| State | Meaning | Guard/output |

| decision.issued | Complete adverse/routing/delay record and accessible notice released | Urgency and provisional-relief screen starts |

| reconsideration | Operator corrects clerical, factual or rule-application error through a separate reviewer | Cannot consume time needed for emergency/expedited relief |

| rights_review | NHAC/PROO examines rights, usability, safety, evidence and interim protection | Complete packet and ombudsman assistance |

| tribunal_optional | NAT review occurs only if retained and non-delaying | May not restrict direct urgent Article I relief |

| article_i_review | A1-HCAC can stay, order, reverse, compel payment/care/data, or grant other statutory remedy | Enforceable expedited jurisdiction |

| remedy.executed | Coverage, care, routing, payment, debt, record and publication states are corrected | Downstream replay and compliance evidence |

| learning.closed | Reversal pattern, root cause and systemic corrective action are evaluated | Category review above controlled reversal threshold |
CLOCK CONTROL  Emergency, expedited and standard clocks must be set by controlling law and approved protocols. This appendix preserves urgency and non-delay semantics but does not invent durations while OI-039 remains open.
N.4 Safety learning loop
Table N-6. Safety event lifecycle

| Stage | Required behavior | Record/owner |

| Detect | Patient/provider report, result, bounce-back, trigger, audit, complaint, model or surveillance signal | safety.event; rights.appeal_case |

| Protect | Immediate clinical response, disclosure/notice, provisional relief, model/process suspension and evidence preservation | NPSMIB/NHAC/operator |

| Investigate | Root cause across clinical, diagnostic, human factors, data, AI, staffing and governance | Independent access and just-culture controls |

| Remedy | Patient/provider relief, injury compensation where applicable, record/payment correction and continuity | IF-022/031 |

| Learn | Protocol, training, staffing, design, formula or vendor change with owner and due date | governance.requirement_result |

| Verify | Independent closure testing, recurrence monitoring, stratified effect and public aggregate | KPP-D6; IF-023/032 |
Closure requires evidence that the individual remedy executed, downstream records/payments/routing were replayed, the affected cohort was reviewed where indicated, corrective effectiveness was independently tested, and aggregate learning was published subject to privacy and safety controls.

Appendix O — Adaptation and Repair Playbook
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Provide a bounded, evidence-based pathway to detect, contain, analyze, authorize, implement, verify and close changes without making emergency action permanent or allowing operators to self-certify. |

| System entities | NHASB; NHAC; CHAO; DNHA/RHA operators; Formula Registry owners; THDO/HFASB; A1-HCAC; affected patients/providers and independent evaluators. |

| Assumptions | Transition protection, legitimacy/safety and adaptation/repair begin in PH-P0. Every material formula or rule is versioned, testable, reviewable, reproducible and rollback-capable. |

| Data / parameters | Trigger event; repair case; authority/tier; affected cohort; containment; root cause; formula/configuration; tests; decision; remedy; publication; closure/reopen. |

| Requirements / performance | SR-ADP-001–015; SR-ARCH-015; VR-021–023/025/030; TPP-FORM1/REG1; KPP-TRUST1; IF-020–024/027–028/032. |

| Principal risks | Unauthorized change; permanent emergency rule; operator self-certification; formula drift; affected-case omission; unsafe rollback; vendor lock-in; suppressed learning. |

| Simulation implication | Model trigger arrival, classification, containment effectiveness, repair lag, authority constraints, rollback, affected-case replay, residual risk and parameter/prior updates. |
BOUNDED REPAIR  A repair may alter a technical or policy mechanism only within lawful authority. It cannot waive rights, safety, equity, mandatory payment or continuity, and it must be ratified, replaced, rolled back or otherwise resolved under its controlling process.
O.1 Trigger and case initiation
Table O-1. Adaptation and repair triggers

| Class | Condition | Controlled response |

| Performance | KPP/TPP, SR, queue, quality, access, equity, continuity, or publication misses a controlled threshold or control limit | Parameter review, corrective action, pilot restriction, gate hold |

| Appeal/review | Reversal, remand, complaint, provisional-relief, or no-silent-rationing pattern exceeds the approved category trigger | Category review, rule/workflow repair, affected-case replay |

| Safety/equity | Serious event, diagnostic harm, subgroup deviation, retaliation, or unsafe workload indicates systemic risk | Immediate protection, safety review, restriction/suspension, remedy |

| Fiscal | Forecast error, obligation/receipt variance, reserve erosion, or formula instability crosses a registered threshold | Forecast review, stabilizer/reserve action, formula repair |

| AI/technology | Model drift, audit failure, security defect, end-of-support, lock-in, or vendor exit-plan failure | Restrict/suspend, manual fallback, migrate, review affected cases |

| Legal | Court order, preemption failure, noncooperation, impoundment, vacancy, or authority loss activates a contingency | Default rule, alternate authority, direct federal/tribal path, legal repair |

| Pilot/waiver | Interim/final evaluation shows success, harm, inequity, nonperformance, or external-validity limits | Scale, modify, extend once, terminate, or restore baseline |

| Trust | Representative trust measure, participation, complaint, misinformation, or service-experience trigger is breached | Independent review, disclosure, service repair, public confidence protocol |
Table O-2. Repair case data contract

| Field group | Required content |

| identity | repair case, trigger, affected ARCH/IF/PH/RISK/SCN, population/function and timestamps |

| classification | technical, clinical, fiscal, legal, rights, safety, AI, vendor, waiver or trust; severity/urgency/tier |

| authority | legal basis, decision owner, independent verifier, permissible actions, notice and review path |

| containment | immediate protection, manual/predecessor fallback, scope, affected-case preservation and expiry condition |

| analysis | root cause, cohort, equity/safety/fiscal/legal effects, alternatives, uncertainty and dependencies |

| change | rule/formula/data/software/process version, effective scope/time, training, migration, rollback and communications |

| verification | procedure, expected/observed results, subgroup analysis, reproducibility, corrective effectiveness and residual risk |

| closure/learning | decision, remedy, case replay, registry updates, simulation-prior update, publication and next review |
Table O-3. Appendix-local repair tier vocabulary

| Local key | Tier | Entry basis | Permitted posture | Guard |

| O-TIER-0 | Monitor | Signal below intervention threshold or evidence incomplete | Continue evidence collection; no operational change | No authority expansion |

| O-TIER-1 | Routine correction | Localized, reversible technical or administrative defect | Versioned ordinary change and verification | Rights, safety, equity and continuity floors remain binding |

| O-TIER-2 | Bounded protective change | Material issue needing constrained scope, monitoring and rollback | Contain, test, authorize bounded scope, review affected cases | Expiry/conditions set by controlling authority; no silent permanence |

| O-TIER-3 | Emergency protection | Immediate material risk and ordinary process is too slow | Temporary signed correction, notice, manual fallback, ratify/replace/rollback | Authority, eligible defects and clocks remain open under OI-044 |

| O-TIER-4 | Structural/legal repair | Authority, institution, formula, market or cross-system design failure | Fallback plus statutory/regulatory/program redesign and independent review | Preserve service and enforceable rights during repair |
O.2 Repair lifecycle
Table O-4. Controlled repair states

| State | Meaning | Exit control |

| detected | A signed trigger event identifies source, affected population/function, severity, urgency, and evidence quality | Create repair case; preserve evidence; apply immediate protection if needed |

| classified | Authority classifies technical, clinical, fiscal, legal, rights, safety, AI, vendor, waiver, or trust pathway | Name owner, independent verifier, clock, notice, and permissible actions |

| contained | Temporary guard, manual fallback, payment/coverage continuity, restriction, or provisional relief bounds harm | Containment cannot become a silent permanent rule |

| analyzed | Root cause, affected-case cohort, equity/safety/fiscal impacts, alternatives, legal basis, and dependencies are tested | Publish or protect evidence under controlled transparency/privacy rules |

| decided | Authorized body selects repair, ratification, rollback, scale, termination, sunset, or no-change with reasons | Decision links authority, formula/rule version, effective date, appeal, and rollback |

| implemented | Versioned change is deployed with training, data migration, continuity, communications, and monitoring | No uncontrolled configuration drift |

| verified | Independent evidence determines whether intended effect occurred without unacceptable displacement | VR method, subgroup analysis, reproducibility, and residual risk |

| closed_or_reopened | Effectiveness is certified and learning published, or failure reopens/escalates the case | Update registry, risks, baselines, simulation priors, and future review dates |
O.3 Formula and configuration control
Table O-5. Formula Registry minimum fields

| Field group | Required content |

| identity/authority | formula_id; title; statutory/regulatory authority; owner; independent verifier; affected decisions |

| version/time | version; predecessor/successor; proposed, validated, effective, expiry, sunset, and retirement timestamps |

| specification | variables; units; domains; equation/executable artifact; rounding; missing-data; precedence; dependency graph |

| data/provenance | authoritative sources; schema/version; lineage; quality constraints; protected-group treatment; code/data hashes |

| tests | reference cases; boundary/exception cases; regression corpus; reconciliation tolerance; expected outputs; independent result |

| constraints | rights, safety, equity, fiscal, access, continuity, privacy, anti-gaming, and human-review constraints |

| operations | deployment scope; feature/config flags; monitoring; alert thresholds; manual fallback; rollback package |

| review | notice/comment; appeal/review links; emergency status; retrospective/sunset outcome; corrective actions; public summary |
Table O-6. Formula lifecycle states

| State | Entry meaning | Guard |

| proposed | Purpose, authority, variables, sources, owner, impacts, and draft tests registered | No operational effect |

| validated | Independent technical, legal, fiscal, safety, equity, usability, and regression checks pass for intended scope | Eligible for notice/authorization |

| noticed | Human-readable rule, effects, evidence, tests, and comment/review path are published as required | Comments and defects remain linked |

| active | Authorized signed version is effective for declared scope/time | Every affected event records version and input/output provenance |

| emergency | Temporary corrective version operates under limited authority, scope, clock, notice, and fallback | Must be ratified, replaced, or rolled back before expiry |

| suspended | Version is disabled after safety, equity, legal, security, data, or performance trigger | Manual/predecessor path and affected-case review active |

| superseded | Successor version is effective after controlled comparison and migration | Historical reproduction remains possible |

| retired | No new use; retention, appeals, audit, and reproducibility obligations remain | Dependencies are resolved and vendor artifacts preserved |
O.4 Review, decision and closure
Table O-7. Controlled review paths

| Pathway | Trigger | Disposition |

| Major rule retrospective | Scheduled evidence after sufficient operating exposure | Continue, narrow, repair, replace, or initiate sunset; SR-ADP-004 |

| Sunset review | Authority/program/formula/waiver/vendor arrangement reaches review date | Reauthorize with evidence, transfer duties, repair, or terminate without extinguishing open rights; SR-ADP-005 |

| Emergency technical correction | Narrow defect creates immediate material risk and ordinary process is too slow | Temporary signed version, notice, protection, expiry, ratify/replace/rollback; SR-ADP-006; VR-022 |

| Red team | Scheduled or trigger-based adversarial test of sabotage, capture, gaming, cyber, continuity, equity, fiscal, or legal failure | Finding, severity, owner, target, closure evidence, residual risk; SR-ADP-012 |

| Vendor/technology lifecycle | Critical dependency, end-of-support, concentration, escrow failure, or portability test | Repair contract, migrate, insource, suspend, or retire with continuity; SR-ADP-009 |

| Benefit-boundary update | New evidence/technology, unmet need, safety/value change, or public petition | Cover, cover with evidence, restrict, delist, or retain with explanation and appeal |

| Regional adaptation waiver | Region proposes a bounded variation to improve local delivery while preserving national floors | Approve/deny; evaluate; scale, repair, expire, or terminate; SR-ADP-015; VR-023 |

| Appeals learning/trust repair | High-overturn category or trust trigger | Affected-case review, rule/service repair, remedy, public report, follow-up; SR-ADP-007/011 |
The operator produces evidence and implements authorized changes; it does not independently certify effectiveness or phase/gate impact. NHASB or another designated independent verifier confirms results. NHAC protects rights/safety/equity; CHAO reviews legality, funding, capture and evidence integrity; courts remain available for enforceable claims.

Appendix P — Risk Register and Failure-Mode and Effects Analysis
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Publish the controlled core risk register, provisional FMEA model parameters, legal-risk reconciliation, compound exercise scenarios and minimum risk evidence contract. |

| System entities | Risk owners; NHTCA; NHASB; NHAC; CHAO; DNHA/RHA operators; THDO; HCCA; A1-HCAC; independent red teams and verifiers. |

| Assumptions | RPN is S×O×D, but cannot by itself rank cross-domain harm, authorize a gate, accept residual risk or substitute for velocity, duration, correlation, uncertainty and rights/safety floors. |

| Data / parameters | Risk causal chain; indicator/threshold; S/O/D; velocity/duration; common cause; controls; fallback; RTO/RPO; test; evidence; residual risk; scenario and module linkage. |

| Requirements / performance | RISK-*; SCN-RT-01–10; KPP/TPP and VR links in each record; PH gates; Appendix O repair controls. |

| Principal risks | Under-calibration; score laundering; common-cause omission; unowned legal risks; paper fallback; risk acceptance without authority; closed finding without effectiveness evidence. |

| Simulation implication | Represent each risk as a stateful causal object; use correlated compound injections, control/fallback effectiveness and recovery curves; retain raw dimensions and uncertainty. |

P.2 FMEA scale and provisional scores
Table P-2. FMEA ordinal scale

| Dimension | Score | Interpretation |

| Severity S | 1 | Negligible; no care disruption; localized reversible administrative effect |

| Severity S | 2 | Minor; short localized delay; no expected clinical harm |

| Severity S | 3 | Moderate; material access/payment impact or reversible patient harm |

| Severity S | 4 | Major; serious harm, regional disruption, substantial fiscal/legal effect |

| Severity S | 5 | Catastrophic; deaths/severe harm, national continuity failure or existential legal/fiscal loss |

| Occurrence O | 1 | Remote within scenario horizon |

| Occurrence O | 2 | Unlikely |

| Occurrence O | 3 | Plausible |

| Occurrence O | 4 | Likely |

| Occurrence O | 5 | Frequent/expected without control |

| Detectability D | 1 | Near-certain early detection with operational telemetry |

| Detectability D | 2 | High detection before material harm |

| Detectability D | 3 | Mixed; detected near onset |

| Detectability D | 4 | Low; often detected after harm |

| Detectability D | 5 | Very low; latent, suppressed or not measurable |

Use severity, occurrence and detectability as separate modeled inputs, disclose their evidence status, and re-score only through a versioned evidence record that preserves the prior score and rationale.
Retain velocity, duration, tail behavior, common-cause dependence and subgroup harm outside RPN.
Do not compare RPN mechanically across legal, clinical, fiscal, cyber and trust domains or permit a lower RPN to waive a statutory right, safety floor, mandatory payment or continuity control.

| LR-FB-001 | Fallback exists on paper but cannot activate in time | 51 | Pretested trigger, owner, assets/data, funding and RTO | appendix-local legal refinement; mapped to a canonical parent risk by the release adjudication register; owner/indicator calibration remains open under OI-069/OI-071 | not scored; empirical/provisional allocation required before ranking or acceptance |
ID RECONCILIATION  RISK-LEGAL-001 and RISK-STATE-001 already exist in the Section 10 core register; their Section 9 text is retained as supplemental legal cause/control detail, not a second definition. LR-TRIB-001, LR-IMP-001, LR-CONF-001 and LR-FB-001 remain controlled legal-only entries pending full owner, indicator and FMEA allocation.
P.4 Risk evidence, workflow and compound exercise coverage
Table P-5. Minimum risk record schema

| Field group | Required content |

| identity | risk ID, title, version, status, owner, accountable executive, affected ARCH/IF/PH/SCN objects |

| causal structure | initiating cause, enabling condition, dependency, failure mode, local effect, system/patient/cost/equity/legal effects |

| measurement | indicator ID, source, cadence, threshold, confidence, stratification, leading/lagging designation and missing-data rule |

| assessment | severity, probability/occurrence, detectability, velocity, duration, correlation/common cause and uncertainty |

| response | preventive control, detective control, mitigation, fallback, decision authority, resources, trigger, RTO/RPO and escalation |

| assurance | requirement/VR, exercise/test, evidence, verifier, residual risk, acceptance authority, review date and closure criteria |

| simulation | state transition, injected parameters, affected modules/interfaces, propagation rule, recovery curve and outputs |
Table P-6. Risk-control workflow

| Local key | Step | Required action |

| P-STEP-01 | Identify | Create or update risk record with causal chain, affected objects and evidence confidence |

| P-STEP-02 | Measure | Define leading/lagging indicators, thresholds, cadence, missing-data rule and stratification |

| P-STEP-03 | Assess | Score S/O/D separately; capture velocity, duration, correlation, uncertainty and status |

| P-STEP-04 | Control | Assign prevention, detection, mitigation, fallback, decision authority, resources and RTO/RPO |

| P-STEP-05 | Exercise | Use requirement tests and SCN-RT compound injections; preserve observed outputs |

| P-STEP-06 | Decide | Accept, condition, hold, reduce, transfer or prohibit only under approved appetite/authority |

| P-STEP-07 | Verify | Independently test corrective effectiveness and residual risk; reopen when evidence fails |

| P-STEP-08 | Learn | Update register, FMEA, common-cause graph, playbooks, phase gates and simulation priors |
Table P-7. Compound red-team scenarios

| ID | Name | Compound injection | Risk linkage | Expected controls | Required outputs |

| SCN-RT-01 | Payment cascade | Cyberattack disables claims + pharmacy while provider liquidity is low | RISK-CYBER/CLAIMS/PHARM | offline continuity; provisional payment; emergency fills; reconciliation | patient interruptions; unpaid obligations; recovery time; duplicate/improper payment |

| SCN-RT-02 | Capacity squeeze | Unit network underbuild + workforce shortage + BH surge + rural stress | RISK-UNIT/WF/SPEC | gate delay; mobile/team capacity; urgency protection; transport support | waits; ED load; unmet need; equity; burnout; cost |

| SCN-RT-03 | Hospital destabilization | Underbudgeted hospitals + drug shortage + workforce attrition | RISK-HOSP/PMC/WF | corridor payment; service-line protection; dual source; premium staffing | closure risk; diversion; mortality proxy; reserve draw |

| SCN-RT-04 | Fiscal-legal shock | Wealth receipts fall as court narrows financing and OMB bypass | RISK-FIN/LEGAL/EXEC | legal tax fallback; reserve; court-ordered payment; stabilizer | revenue gap; burden incidence; payment continuity; reserve months |

| SCN-RT-05 | Federalism fracture | Hostile states block compact, data and credentials during migration | RISK-STATE/DATA/WF | conditional funding; direct administration; federated data; direct credentials | coverage gap; access; legal RTO; state/tribal disparity |

| SCN-RT-06 | Algorithmic inequity | AI under-refers a protected group while dashboards average the effect away | RISK-AI/TRUST | stratified detection; suspension; human re-review; restitution; disclosure | harm; delayed diagnosis; appeal; trust; correction time |

| SCN-RT-07 | Migration harm | Legacy authorizations and cancer-treatment records fail to transfer | RISK-DATA/CLAIMS | provisional coverage/payment; manual clinical reconciliation; ombudsman | missed treatment; appeal; safety event; cost and closeout time |

| SCN-RT-08 | Manufacturing recall | PMC batch failure coincides with external supplier shortage | RISK-PMC/PHARM | recall; emergency procurement; therapeutic substitution; allocation transparency | shortage exposure; adverse events; price/cost; trust |

| SCN-RT-09 | Legitimacy attack | Withheld performance data + service delays + coordinated misinformation | RISK-EXEC/TRUST | data escrow; independent publication; confidence repair; service correction | trust; utilization avoidance; complaints; recovery |

| SCN-RT-10 | Pandemic transition collision | Public-health surge during coverage conversion and workforce shortage | RISK-WF/CLAIMS/UNIT/HOSP | transition pause; surge funding; flexible capacity; continuity defaults | mortality proxy; access; staffing; cost; phase delay |
Scenario results update evidence and priors; they do not automatically change risk acceptance, authorize progression or claim external validity. Red-team independence, safe testing, disclosure, remediation clocks and retest remain open under OI-074.

Appendix Q — Simulation Input Schema
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Define the versioned, machine-valid contract by which a simulation run declares metadata, dimensions, modules, initial state, parameters, scenario logic, correlations and provenance. |

| System entities | Model integrator; module owners; data stewards; NHASB/CHAO independent verifiers; configuration authority. |

| Assumptions | The schema validates structure and selected semantics; it does not calibrate the model or establish policy outcomes. |

| Data / parameters | Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema; example input; 19 MOD, 33 SV, 310 CP, 20 SCN and provenance catalogs. |

| Requirements / performance | VR-002/003/005/020; KPP/TPP/CP dictionaries; OI-020/OI-081–090. |

| Principal risks | Schema drift; unknown vocabularies; invalid units; hidden defaults; target-forced outputs; non-reproducible transformations. |

| Simulation implication | A simulator must reject structurally invalid runs, quarantine semantic errors, and preserve warnings and provenance with results. |
SCHEMA STATUS  Version 1.0.1 is a structural contract and patch-level correction. It is not calibration-complete. OI-089 and OI-090 remain open for vocabulary services and long-run migration governance.
Table Q-01. Controlled artifact set

| Artifact | Version / identity | Role | Validation |

| National_Health_Assurance_Framework_Simulation_Input.schema.json | 1.0.1 / urn:nhaf:schema:simulation-input:1.0.1 | Normative input structure | pass |

| National_Health_Assurance_Framework_Simulation_Input_Example.json | schema_version 1.0.1 | Illustrative structural instance | pass_with_controlled_warnings |

| National_Health_Assurance_Framework_Deliverable_7C_Machine_Simulation.json | D7C controlled catalog | Allowed MOD/SV/CP/SCN and output dictionary | Referential source |
Table Q-02. Top-level input objects

| Object | Required | Content | Failure treatment |

| metadata | Yes | Schema/model/data versions; run ID; comparator; time; currency; notes | Reject unknown comparator, invalid years or non-2024-real-dollar basis |

| dimensions | Yes | Regions, populations, services, agencies and optional typed domain vocabularies | Reject duplicate/unknown enumerations; quarantine vocabulary mismatch |

| module_config | Yes | Enabled module, time step, version and options | Reject unknown/duplicate modules; semantic suite requires all 19 in the example |

| initial_state | Yes | SV, period, unit, dimensions, value and provenance | Reject unknown SV, unit mismatch, missing provenance or invalid bound |

| parameters | Yes | CP, status, unit, value or distribution, dimensions, time and provenance | Reject unknown CP or incoherent calibrated/uncalibrated state |

| scenario | Yes | SCN, seed, parent, overrides and timed events | Reject unknown target/operation or missing NHA scenario |

| correlations | No | Member parameters and matrix | Reject invalid member/matrix; calibrate dependencies under OI-024 |

| provenance | Yes | Source, reference, version date, transformation, owner/reviewer | Reject dangling provenance references |
Table Q-03. Validation hierarchy

| Level | Tests | Disposition |

| Q-VL-1 Syntax/schema | JSON parse; Draft 2020-12 types, required fields, enums, additional properties and conditional branches | Hard reject |

| Q-VL-2 Referential | MOD/SV/CP/SCN/provenance existence; uniqueness; unit and dimension vocabulary | Hard reject or quarantine before run |

| Q-VL-3 Semantic | Time order; calibrated status; bounds; matrix shape; event precedence; no hidden target achievement | Hard reject for incoherence; warning only where explicitly incomplete |

| Q-VL-4 Accounting | Stock-flow, cost, transfer, reserve, cohort and inventory conservation | Run fails certification; retain diagnostic output |

| Q-VL-5 Calibration | Reproduce source baselines within approved tolerance and uncertainty | No comparative release until passed |

| Q-VL-6 Scenario/assurance | Deterministic seed replay; stress behavior; subgroup/equity; independent reproduction | No certified result until passed |
Table Q-04. Example validation result

| Check | Result | Evidence / caveat |

| Draft 2020-12 structural subset | pass | 0 errors; all schema keywords used by the contract checked |

| Module inventory | Pass | 19 unique controlled modules |

| State and parameter references | Pass | 1 state and 2 parameter records; provenance resolved |

| Scenario reference | Pass | SCN-BASE exists; NHA comparator has scenario ID |

| Calibration completeness | Controlled warning | Only two parameters supplied; example is structural and cannot support comparative results |

| Outcome forcing | Pass | No input field asserts KPP/TPP achievement; target text remains separate from observations/results |
Q.1 Versioning and extensions
Patch changes correct validation without changing field semantics; minor changes add backward-compatible optional fields; major changes may break consumers and require a migration tool and dual-read period.
Extensions use an approved namespace and cannot weaken required fields, provenance, data rights, accounting identities or human-accountability controls.
Every run freezes schema, model, data, formula, scenario and code versions; results retain the input hash, seed, warnings and validator version.
Unknown fields are rejected by default. A controlled migration must explicitly map, test and sign each transformed object; silent coercion is prohibited.
Catalog scope carried forward: 19 modules, 33 state variables, 310 cost parameters, 20 controlled scenarios and 29 outputs.

| Control | Values | Meaning |

| Uncertainty | value; lower/upper; method/quality flags | Intervals and estimation status travel with the metric |
Table R-03. Release pipeline and accountability

| Step | Primary action | Required evidence |

| Ingest/validate | Validate period, denominator, lineage, access class and completeness | DQ results; quarantine log |

| Calculate/stratify | Execute signed calculation; retain national and authorized subgroup results | Formula/data versions; numerator/denominator |

| Privacy/quality review | Apply small-cell, dominance, differencing, security, legal and quality controls | Release decision and suppressed-cell metadata |

| Independent certification | Verifier reproduces material values and checks target/observation class | VR-004/020/028 evidence |

| Publish/archive | Issue accessible payload/UI and immutable manifest | Release ID, hash, as-of and certification times |

| Monitor/correct | Detect stale/error conditions; publish correction/supersession and affected scope | Correction notice; replay; root-cause closure |

R.2 Accessibility, interpretation and correction
Every view provides plain-language definition, numerator/denominator, period, geography, uncertainty, status, source, owner, verifier and change history; visual color is never the only signal.
Users can compare NHA and existing-system pathways only where definitions and periods are harmonized; otherwise the interface explains non-comparability.
A correction never overwrites history. It publishes the original release ID, affected metrics/cohorts/periods, reason, corrected value, method change, certifier and downstream replay scope.
The public interface provides downloadable machine payloads and accessible tables, language/disability support, feedback and complaint routes, and an archive of delayed/suppressed releases.

Appendix S — Open Issues and Research Agenda
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Consolidate every unresolved, bounded, partially closed and controlled-closed matter under one stable OI identifier and a governed closure method. |

| System entities | Named policy/technical/legal owners; NHASB/CHAO/NHAC verifiers; configuration authority; research sponsors and affected stakeholders. |

| Assumptions | An issue is not closed by prose completion. Closure requires authority, evidence, affected-object updates, verification and release control. |

| Data / parameters | OI-001–OI-121; all source variants; status, owner/domain, treatment, agenda, closure evidence and integration disposition. |

| Requirements / performance | All affected ASM/SN/PR/SR/VR/KPP/TPP/CP/ARCH/IF/PH/RISK/SCN objects; Appendix T evidence gaps. |

| Principal risks | False closure; duplicate/conflicting variants; ownerless research; unresolved blockers hidden in polished prose; renumbering that breaks traceability. |

| Simulation implication | Open issues become explicit model uncertainty, alternative scenarios, validation dependencies or prohibited claims—not invented point estimates. |

S.9 Research execution and closure workflow
Triage the issue as integration decision, statutory/legal design, empirical research, technical standard, calibration, implementation test or external dependency.
Assign one accountable decision owner and one independent verifier; identify affected stakeholders and controlled IDs before work begins.
Pre-register the question, method, evidence standard, uncertainty, alternatives, equity/safety/rights constraints and stop criteria.
Publish the decision record and verification evidence; update every affected document, machine schema, test, scenario and dashboard definition in one configuration release.
Retain residual risk, monitoring trigger and reopen condition. Closed issues are never deleted or recycled.

Appendix T — PMC Essential Product Family Register
NORMATIVE REGISTER  PF-001 through PF-200 are the complete controlled product-family baseline for SR-DRUG-006 and TPP-4.1. Each family requires routine PMC-controlled public production by PH-P8. Clinical experts and FDA must still approve exact strengths, presentations, specifications, and labeling; those subordinate decisions may not delete a family without formal framework change control.
Table T-1. Product-family definition and production rule

| Control | Rule |

| Family boundary | Clinically coherent active ingredient, combination, biologic, solution family, or antidote platform plus essential dosage-form group; not an individual NDC. |

| Production test | Released conforming lot, current validated process, current source/control record, and routine output on a PMC-owned or PMC-controlled public line. |

| Deadline | All 200 families qualified and in routine production by PH-P8; earlier phase targets vary by manufacturing complexity. |

| Redundancy | SR-DRUG-007 dual-source requirement remains separate; a PMC line may be one of the qualified sources but does not eliminate redundancy. |

| Quality | SR-DRUG-008 batch-release target and ordinary FDA statutory quality authority apply to every family. |

| External evidence | T-ED-019 through T-ED-024 inform selection and calibration; the 200-family portfolio remains a framework design decision. |

T.1 Selection and maintenance controls
The initial portfolio uses clinical indispensability, shortage or platform vulnerability, population burden, affordability and equity, maternal-child need, and national preparedness. Annual review may change subordinate strengths and presentations. Adding or deleting a PF family requires public evidence, NHASB scorekeeping, NBIA and DNHA technical review, NHAC equity review, a transition and shortage analysis, and a versioned requirements change.

Appendix U — Bibliography and Evidence Base
Section control record

| Control field | Controlled content |

| Purpose | Fix the source hierarchy, quantitative-evidence classes, external-source register, claim-use boundaries and unresolved evidence gaps used by the framework and simulation. |

| System entities | Framework configuration authority; evidence/data stewards; legal counsel; model integrator; NHASB/CHAO independent review. |

| Assumptions | The framework source package controls framework design. External evidence supports comparator facts, methods and standards but does not silently amend policy. |

| Data / parameters | Authoritative framework files and hashes; 18 empirical sources; standards/guidance; law/official summaries; evidence-gap register. |

| Requirements / performance | ASM/requirements/KPP/TPP/CP/comparator/scenario/open-issue provenance; VR-002/003/005/020. |

| Principal risks | Stale links or versions; secondary-source substitution; year/definition mismatch; treating guidance as law; treating assumptions as forecasts; circular model validation. |

| Simulation implication | Each input and calibration record cites a versioned provenance object and states whether it is FA, MP, TG, ED, DV or OI. |
SOURCE HIERARCHY  Most recent, most detailed controlled framework material governs. The Original Conversation Transcript is general context only. External sources support facts, methods and legal/technical context; conflicts or updates trigger review rather than silent substitution.
Table T-01. Quantitative classes

| Class | Meaning | Permitted simulation/dashboard use |

| FA | final framework assumption | Input assumption with sensitivity; label as assumption, not forecast. |

| MP | model parameter | Calibrated or scenario parameter with units, distribution and provenance. |

| TG | target | Acceptance/aspiration comparator; never insert as achieved output. |

| ED | externally sourced data | Observed/projected external record with definition, year, vintage and uncertainty. |

| DV | derived value | Reproducible equation and source IDs required. |

| OI | open issue | No false precision; use range/alternative or prohibit claim. |

U.1 Evidence maintenance and citation rules
Cite the direct authoritative publication or primary legal text where available; record title, issuing authority, version/vintage, observation period, URL, access date and retained hash where lawful.
Keep observation year, publication year and access date distinct. Dynamic comparators also identify policy continuation and forecast vintage.
A changed source triggers impact analysis on definitions, parameters, equations, conclusions and public releases; it does not overwrite prior baselines.
Model outputs cannot validate their own input assumptions. Independent reproduction and external comparator evidence remain separate from framework-source authority.
This integrated release normalizes citation style and in-text cross-references while preserving these IDs and machine provenance records.
